articles.title: Carneiro’s global dataset of cultural traits in ethnographic and historical societies: a digital edition
articles.abstract: Abstract The late Robert L. Carneiro was a prominent anthropologist who devoted his life to the study of political evolution and the evolution of complex societies. In the 1960s and 1970s, he and his colleagues created a cross-cultural dataset for their Scale Analysis project, collecting ethnographic and historical data on hundreds of cultural traits in more than a hundred societies worldwide. Although Carneiro presented the results of the project in several papers, the dataset itself has not yet been published. Here we present a digital version of two editions of the dataset, based on Carneiro’s documentation stored in the archives of the American Museum of Natural History. The 4th edition contains 127 societies and 354 cultural traits, and the 6th edition features 74 societies and 618 traits. Both represent unique sets of coded cross-cultural information that can be used as a comparative source to other cross-cultural datasets, as a starting point for one’s own collection of cross-cultural data, and for quantitative testing of cultural evolutionary hypotheses.
articles.authors: Václav Hrnčíř, Robert Forkel, Russell D. Gray
articles.titleCn: Carneiro的民族志与历史社会文化特征全球数据集：数字版本
articles.interpretationCn: 该数据集源自人类学家Robert L. Carneiro及其同事在20世纪60至70年代为Scale Analysis项目收集的跨文化数据，基于美国自然历史博物馆档案中的文档整理而成。数字版本包含两版：第4版涵盖127个社会和354项文化特征，第6版涵盖74个社会和618项特征。数据为编码后的跨文化信息，可用于与其他跨文化数据集比较、作为自行收集跨文化数据的起点，以及定量检验文化演化假说。

articles.title: SEA-Driven OdorNet: A Large-Scale Standardized Molecular Olfactory Dataset Based on a Hybrid Semantic Taxonomy
articles.abstract: The development of machine olfaction (digitization of odor) is currently hindered by data scarcity and the lack of standardization in descriptive labels. Datasets integration faces the challenges of descriptor-level conflicts, including cross-source labeling inconsistencies, synonym redundancy, skewed distributions, etc. To address the semantic confusion inherent in multi-source data, we developed a SEA (Statistical co-occurrence, Expert correction, and AI alignment) taxonomy framework that integrates statistical co-occurrence analysis, expert knowledge (perfumery taxonomy), and AI-assisted semantic alignment based on the definitions from both encyclopedia and odor-related scientific literatures. A unified-labeled olfactory dataset, namely OdorNet, is further presented, which is by far the largest molecule dataset with unified olfactory labels comprising over 20,000 entries and 9,000 unique molecules originated from academic literatures (1960–2021) and open databases. This process consolidates cluttered labels into a hierarchical system with the most extensively effective vocabulary coverage in the field to date. Technical validation demonstrates that a baseline model on OdorNet achieves a Macro F1 score of 0.42, substantially higher than the scores obtained on commonly used odor datasets and on OdorNet itself using the same model but without the SEA-based label taxonomy. This indicates that OdorNet allows to better capture learnable structure-odor relationships, laying a solid fundamental for digital odor editing and human-computer interaction.
articles.authors: Liyuan Yang, Zhiyang Liu, Bin Shao, Feng Liu, Zhuo Ma, Juntao Niu, Chunning Zhao, Xiang Wan, Weichao Wang
articles.titleCn: SEA驱动的OdorNet：基于混合语义分类的大规模标准化分子嗅觉数据集
articles.interpretationCn: 该数据集面向机器嗅觉研究，旨在解决多源嗅觉描述标签的语义冲突与标准化缺失问题。作者提出SEA分类框架，融合统计共现分析、专家知识（香水分类）和AI辅助语义对齐，将来自1960至2021年学术文献和开放数据库的杂乱标签整合为层级化统一标签体系。OdorNet包含超过20,000条记录和9,000个独特分子，是迄今最大的统一嗅觉标签分子数据集。技术验证显示，基于该数据集的基线模型Macro F1达0.42，显著高于常用嗅觉数据集及未使用SEA标签分类的OdorNet自身，表明其能更好捕捉可学习的结构-气味关系，为数字气味编辑和人机交互奠定基础。

articles.title: Multimodal 3D X-ray Topotomography Dataset of Slip Activity and Transmission in Ti-7Al
articles.abstract: Abstract Plastic deformation in polycrystalline metals is usually primarily accommodated through dislocation glide, which often organizes into discrete slip bands. The evolution of plasticity is governed by the interactions of these dislocation structures with one another, as well as with grain boundaries and other microstructural interfaces or features. Traditional observations of slip bands are largely limited to free surfaces, constraining our understanding of their three-dimensional behavior within the bulk. The X-ray topotomography and diffraction contrast tomography (DCT) datasets presented here enable direct visualization of the three-dimensional morphology of slip bands in relation to the surrounding grain structure. These data reveal, for instance, in the investigated titanium alloy that slip transmission across grain boundaries is more prevalent at free surfaces, while in the bulk, transmission events are often driven by geometrically constrained regions, such as triple junctions, where elevated local stress heterogeneity promotes dislocation activity across interfaces. This dataset is shared with the community to facilitate broader access to and analysis of correlated 3D deformation and microstructure alloy datasets, which are expected to become increasingly prevalent in the near future.

articles.title: A multi-phase shaking table dataset of reinforced concrete frames retrofitted with a timber–aluminium exoskeleton
articles.abstract: Abstract A significant portion of the existing reinforced concrete (RC) building stock in Europe was designed according to outdated standards and is vulnerable both to earthquake damage and to poor energy performance. Retrofit solutions that integrate structural strengthening with envelope upgrading have therefore emerged as a promising strategy to address safety and decarbonisation objectives simultaneously. Within this context, the EU-funded Horizon Europe project Engineering Research Infrastructures for European Synergies (ERIES) supported the REsilient and SUstainable envelope for vulnerable buildings in seisMic affected areas at the time of climatE crisis (RESUME) project, which investigated the seismic response of RC frames strengthened with a hybrid timber–aluminium exoskeleton system incorporating prefabricated façade panels for thermal upgrading. To investigate seismic vulnerability, two geometrically scaled (1:3) two-storey RC frame specimens representative of non-ductile typologies were constructed and tested on a shaking table at the Institute of Earthquake Engineering and Engineering Seismology (IZIIS), North Macedonia. The experimental campaign comprised 66 shaking table tests conducted in three phases. The dataset includes synchronised time-history measurements of accelerations, displacements and strains, together with input ground motions and detailed metadata describing geometry, materials, instrumentation and testing sequence. The data support validation of numerical models and comparative assessment of structural retrofit configurations within an integrated retrofit framework.

articles.title: A century-long provincial dataset of agricultural land use structure in China (1924–2024)
articles.abstract: Long-term, large-scale data on agricultural land use are essential for understanding land-use transitions and human-environment interactions, yet century-scale, provincial-level datasets are lacking for China. To fill this gap, we constructed a provincial dataset of agricultural land use structure in China covering the period 1924–2024. The dataset integrates multi-source historical materials, including official statistics, historical archives, remote-sensing products, and international reconstruction databases. A consistent land classification system was defined (cropland, garden land, forest land, grassland, aquaculture and fishing water surface, facility agricultural land), and a backward anchoring reconstruction method was applied to fill early-period data gaps. The dataset provides annual areas (in 10 3 ha) for six agricultural land types across 31 provincial units. It can be used for studying long-term agricultural transitions, validating land-use models, and supporting sustainable land-use policy analysis. The dataset is available for peer review via a temporary link.

articles.title: Global compilation of in situ particulate organic carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus concentrations in coastal and open ocean waters
articles.abstract: We present a global compilation of in situ marine particulate organic carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus concentrations (POC, PON, and POP, respectively), from multiple sources to provide one of the most comprehensive collections of marine particulate organic matter (POM) to date. The dataset includes 155137 measurements (70586 POC, 69290 PON, and 15261 POP) from 25944 independent stations, more than doubling the number of previously available observations. Observations span more than three decades (1988–2025) and cover the global ocean from the surface to 6009 m depth. Notably, 52% of stations are located in shallow, coastal waters (<200 m bottom depth), enhancing coverage of productive nearshore regions and improving representation of dynamic coastal biogeochemistry. To address methodological heterogeneity among the compiled datasets, detailed metadata describing sampling strategies, filtration protocols, filter types, and analytical techniques were systematically assembled for each measurement whenever available. This dataset provides a resource for quantifying the spatial and temporal variability of POM distributions, and the elemental stoichiometry of marine particles, supporting biogeochemical modeling efforts. The dataset will also enable the development and validation of both bio-optical models and satellite-derived estimates of POM, including applications to the Sentinel-3 and the Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem (PACE) missions.

articles.title: A multi-level dataset of China’s energy-transition policies from national to prefecture levels over 2000–2024
articles.abstract: China’s energy transition has generated a vast and heterogeneous body of policy documents across multiple administrative levels. Existing datasets, however, remain largely confined to national-level analyses or single-domain applications and rely predominantly on proxy variables or keyword-frequency methods that may inadequately capture the substantive content of policy texts. To address this gap, this study constructs a title-anchored, multi-level inventory of China’s energy-transition policies spanning 2000 to 2024, based on an exact-match search of seven selected energy-transition-related terms in official policy titles, yielding 7,295 policy texts retrieved from PKULaw across national, provincial, and prefecture-level administrative tiers. Each policy is annotated with 14 structured metadata fields and classified according to a four-category objective typology with 16 sub-objectives and a three-category instrument typology with 9 subcategories. Multi-label classification allows each policy to carry multiple objectives and instruments simultaneously. The dataset is designed to support empirical research on policy mix composition, multi-level governance, and the drivers of energy transition outcomes at regional and firm levels.

articles.title: PORTIA: A Large-Scale Port Acoustic Dataset with AIS-Grounded Annotations for AI-Based Vessel Monitoring
articles.abstract: Monitoring underwater anthropogenic noise in busy commercial ports is critical for marine spatial planning, yet the development of AI-based tools is often limited by the scarcity of large-scale, annotated acoustic datasets from realistic high-traffic environments. We present PORTIA, a passive acoustic dataset collected over a 26-day campaign in the Port of Valencia, Spain. It comprises 260,932 three-second audio windows paired with synchronized Automatic Identification System (AIS) metadata. To facilitate direct reuse, we provide three task-oriented benchmarks: a Binary Detection subset (36,148 samples), a Single-Vessel Classification subset (39,125 samples), and a Multi-Label Monitoring subset (34,996 samples) explicitly designed to handle concurrent acoustic scenes and source proximity. All benchmarks were constructed using Maritime Mobile Service Identity (MMSI)-aware splitting to prevent identity leakage across partitions and utilized stratified sampling to preserve representative vessel-class distributions while remaining manageable for research. PORTIA serves as a realistic benchmark for vessel detection, typological classification, and proximity estimation in dense Mediterranean port soundscapes.

articles.title: A Satellite-based Four-decade High-resolution Quasi-global Mesoscale Convective Systems Database
articles.abstract: Mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) are fundamental to the global energy and water cycles and account for a large fraction of extreme weather events. Yet the lack of a temporally consistent, long-term observational record has hindered robust quantification of their variability. Here, we construct the longest-to-date global MCS database (1985–2024) by applying a widely used object-based tracking algorithm to two high-resolution satellite infrared brightness temperature datasets. To enhance temporal homogeneity, we implement a latitude-stratified, seasonally varying adjustment to reduce discrepancies between the datasets. The resulting database provides quasi-global (60°S–60°N), object-based records of MCS frequency, life cycle, size, intensity, and associated precipitation characteristics. Evaluation of key MCS features, comparisons with alternative tracking methods, and the use of flexible thresholds that support user-defined applications demonstrate the robustness of the tracking framework and long-term record. We anticipate that this extended global MCS database will facilitate the evaluation of MCS simulations and predictions, enable the detection of climate-driven changes in organized convection, and support assessments of their climatic impacts and associated weather risks.

articles.title: A Curated Dataset for Chemical Characterization of Heated Tobacco Product Aerosol
articles.abstract: We addressed the task of chemical characterization of the aerosol emitted by heated tobacco products (HTPs) and of the smoke emitted by conventional/commercial cigarettes, usually adopted as a reference. Emphasis was placed on quantifying constituents for enabling the identification of novel compounds through targeted and untargeted analyses, and the evaluation of reductions in toxicant exposure under standardized smoking regimens. We curated and harmonized experimental data across studies, addressing methodological inconsistencies in puffing protocols, analytical approaches, reporting formats, and treatment of detection limits. The dataset, named HTP-AeroChem, covers data from both industry-funded and independent investigations, offering an aggregated resource for critical comparison of experimental quality, reproducibility, and data reliability. By consolidating and standardizing findings, this work provides a valuable resource to support regulatory assessments and risk evaluations of HTPs in comparison to combustible cigarettes.

articles.title: Microscopic images of pollen germination under natural heat stress in four cucurbit species
articles.abstract: We present a microscopy image dataset of pollen germination and tube growth from melon, watermelon, cucumber, and pumpkin cultivated under naturally occurring heat stress conditions. Beyond supporting computer vision research, the dataset is linked to two agronomic assays involving a diverse panel of cultivars, providing a phenotyping resource for studying pollen viability responses to warm cultivation conditions across cucurbit germplasm. The dataset comprises 3089 microscopy images accompanied by experimental metadata. A curated subset of 122 images includes instance-level annotations in COCO format distinguishing germinated grains, non-germinated grains, and pollen tubes, while a complementary subset of 639 images provides expert visual scores describing pollen abundance, germination level, and tube development. Additionally, 129 images are flagged for visual noise. Technical validation was performed by training and evaluating several semantic segmentation models on the annotated subset, demonstrating that the annotations support reliable automated pollen segmentation. The dataset provides a benchmark for developing and validating automated pollen analysis methodologies while supporting future studies on pollen viability under naturally occurring high-temperature conditions.

articles.title: A multimodal synthetic 3D point cloud dataset of shoe uppers for robotic processing boundary segmentation
articles.abstract: Abstract Robotic processing of shoe uppers requires accurate segmentation of thin processing boundaries in 3D point clouds. However, acquiring and annotating large collections of real-world scans is costly. We present a multimodal synthetic 3D point cloud dataset of shoe uppers for robotic processing boundary segmentation. The dataset contains 1,067 samples, including 1,000 synthetic point clouds and 67 real-world test scans for independent evaluation. The synthetic data generation pipeline includes texture and appearance augmentation, region-aware geometric deformation, and sensor degradation simulation. Both branches provide three-dimensional coordinates, RGB attributes, and pointwise binary processing boundary labels. The synthetic branch additionally includes panel identifiers, while the real-world labels were manually refined. Technical validation with standard point cloud segmentation backbones assesses dataset usability under a controlled synthetic-to-real evaluation protocol. The released point clouds form a complete, directly usable dataset. The accompanying code and assets support regeneration and adaptation of synthetic subsets.

articles.title: High-frequency eDNA metabarcoding survey data of coastal fish across the Japanese Archipelago
articles.abstract: The Japanese archipelago, spanning over 3,000 km from subarctic to subtropical zones (approximately 24°N to 45°N), hosts a diverse array of coastal fish communities shaped by pronounced latitudinal gradients. Here, we present a high-frequency environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding dataset of coastal fishes collected across the archipelago. Using the MiFish primer set targeting a hypervariable region of the mitochondrial 12S rRNA gene, we conducted surveys at 211 sites, yielding 690 samples collected through one-time (annual), monthly, and biweekly sampling schemes. The inclusion of high-frequency sampling enabled the detection of fine-scale temporal variations in fish community composition. From January 2018 to March 2019, eDNA samples were collected along with metadata on geographic and environmental variables, including coastal structure, wave height, tide, currents, and water temperature. The resulting dataset comprises fish eDNA records for 1,477 species across 171 families. This dataset offers a valuable resource for investigating fish community structure, temporal dynamics, and biodiversity in the coastal ecosystems of the Japanese archipelago, supporting a range of applications in ecology, conservation, and eDNA-based research.

articles.title: An EEG dataset for multi-state memory processing in an associative word-pair task
articles.abstract: Memory processing unfolds across successive cognitive states rather than within a single isolated phase, making multi-state neural recordings important for characterizing state-dependent brain dynamics. Here, we present an open-access electroencephalography (EEG) dataset from 41 participants collected during a structured associative word-pair memory protocol that included questionnaires, encoding, retrieval, re-encoding, and interleaved resting-state (RS) periods. The data include 28-channel EEG, 4-channel electrooculography, participant-level questionnaire measures, and trial-level behavioral annotations, including retrieval responses, reaction times, and subjective difficulty ratings. By combining interleaved RS and task phases within a single protocol, this dataset enables investigations of neural dynamics across successive cognitive states within a common experimental framework. It also supports analyses of behavior-linked variability at the trial level and may facilitate studies of individual differences in memory-related cognition.

articles.title: Time series data with and without anomalies from a continuous distillation plant
articles.abstract: Abstract Reliable detection of process anomalies remains a challenge in industrial chemical plants. The ability of machine learning (ML) to recognize patterns has triggered numerous research efforts to apply ML to anomaly detection (AD). Simulation-based benchmarks, such as the Tennessee Eastman process, are widely used to develop and train AD methods. Well-annotated real-world process data, which are crucial for meaningful research advancements, are lacking due to industry-wide proprietary limitations. To overcome this issue, we present an openly accessible dataset of time series generated from an industry-like continuous distillation mini-plant under constant operating conditions. The data generated have different complexities: water runs, a heteroazeotropic separation of n-butanol–water, and a reactive process to produce a fuel additive. Chemical systems, plant setup, and anomalies (whether encountered or manually induced) are described alongside the process data. The complete dataset, including sensor and actuator data, annotations marking anomalies, and other metadata, is available in open access via an online Zenodo repository. It serves as training and testing data for ML-based AD and other data-driven applications.

articles.title: Weather station data from the Mount Everest region, Nepal: 3810–8810 m above sea level
articles.abstract: Between 2019 and 2025, as part of the National Geographic and Rolex Perpetual Planet Everest expeditions, a team of National Geographic Explorers, scientists, and elite climbing Sherpas installed a network of Automatic Weather Stations (AWSs) to improve understanding of the climate at high altitudes in the Nepal Himalaya. This knowledge is critical in the Mount Everest (Khumbu) region, due to its extreme altitude, popularity amongst trekkers and mountaineers, and its importance as a source of freshwater for downstream communities. Here we present quality controlled (QC) meteorological data from six AWSs extending from Phortse (3810 m above sea level, m a.s.l.) to Bishop Rock (8810 m a.s.l.) in the Everest region, including the seasonal climatology focused on the three lower elevation AWSs, and a comparison with ERA5 reanalysis data from the South Col AWS. The data is accessible from https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18849098 (Khadka, 2026a).

articles.title: A harmonized dataset for dams and  reservoirs in West Africa
articles.abstract: Most existing datasets that could support dam and reservoir management and assessments of their impacts in West Africa are limited by inaccurate georeferencing, inconsistent accessibility, heterogeneous data records, and a lack of validation against field observations. In this study, we review and assess existing datasets containing information on dams and reservoirs in West Africa and subsequently integrate them into a harmonized and consolidated regional dataset. We benchmarked the quality of the newly compiled dataset at watershed scale through an extended field study, and statistical analyses. The resulting dataset (https://doi.org/10.60507/FK2/YLDK1Y, Kouassi et al., 2026) includes 1429 georeferenced dams and 1258 reservoirs (with a minimum surface of 0.57×10-3 km 2 ) exceeding the count of dams and reservoirs in West Africa reported by any available dataset. It contains 38 attributes and an estimated total reservoir surface area of 14 038 km 2 and a cumulative storage capacity of 2.83032×10 11 m 3 , thereby enhancing data accessibility in West Africa. The regional compiled dataset contains fewer missing entries and exhibits lower bias compared to the originate datasets, advancing the existing efforts by explicitly integrating both large (≥10 km 2 ) and small (<10 km 2 ) scale reservoirs. The ground-based watershed scale assessment revealed strong spatial and temporal coherence for large scale reservoirs, but a systematic underrepresentation of small scale infrastructure in both the sources and thus also in the compiled dataset highlighting the importance of field validation. The field benchmarking advocates for collaborative research and data sharing initiatives among scientists and institutions across West Africa to improve the accuracy and completeness of dam and reservoir data, especially for small scale infrastructure.

articles.title: The WoKaS-Iso database: workflow for a global  compilation of oxygen-18 and deuterium  records in karst springs and cave drip water  for enhanced understanding of karst systems
articles.abstract: For analysing karst hydrogeological systems, observations of karst springs and cave drips are considered indispensable. In addition to hydrometric observations, knowing the oxygen and hydrogen stable isotope ratios has improved the understanding of vadose zone and aquifer dynamics, likewise supporting system characterisation and modelling. However, limited accessibility and high costs of the analysis of stable isotopes in karst aquifers have hindered progress in karst research and impeded the accurate understanding of karst processes especially when it comes to comparative or large-scale studies. In this study, we present our workflow to compile the WoKaS-Iso database, the first extensive collection of time series data for Oxygen-18 and Deuterium isotopes in karst springs and cave drip water from diverse sources, encompassing publications, theses, reports, online archives, and collaborative initiatives worldwide. The database incorporates data sourced from 241 springs and 74 caves, of which 73 caves contain 365 individual drip sites and one cave contains input data only. In total, the database comprises 1007 time series, including 389 spring time series and 618 cave drip water time series. The compiled isotope records span the period from 1967 to 2024, with the strongest temporal coverage during the 2010s and continuing coverage into the early 2020s. Of these sites, 148 springs and 64 caves contain both δ 18 O and δ 2 H records, while 93 springs and 9 caves contain only one isotope tracer. These datasets provide coverage across significant karst regions globally, spanning China, the USA, Europe, the Middle East, and Australia. Within datasets, 79 % for springs and 68 % for cave drip water exhibit resolutions finer than monthly intervals. In addition, by integrating isotopic records with ancillary environmental variables including spring discharge, cave drip rate, precipitation, and rainwater isotopes, the database offers a more comprehensive perspective on hydrological behaviours in karst aquifers, hence advancing hydrogeological characterisation and modelling. The WoKaS-Iso database not only deepens the understanding of the complex systems but also promotes sustainable water resource management as well as the potential to foster collaborative research. The database can be accessed at: https://doi.org/10.25532/OPARA-909 (Zang, 2025).

articles.title: 16S rRNA Datasets of Gut Microbiota in Stent-Based Diverting Technique and Ileostomy from A Prospective, Open-Label, Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial
articles.abstract: Abstract Accumulating evidence implicates gut dysbiosis in postoperative complications and delayed intestinal recovery after rectal cancer surgery. Although stent-based diverting technique (SDT) and conventional ileostomy exert divergent impacts on gut microbial balance, high-quality comparative microbiome data from randomized trials are lacking. We report a 16S rRNA amplicon dataset from 80 patients randomized to SDT (n = 37) or ileostomy (n = 43), with fecal samples collected preoperatively and on postoperative day 90. We characterized phylum-level taxonomic composition, α-diversity and intergroup β-diversity across four subgroups, and identified discriminatory taxa via LEfSe. Functional prediction detected differential metabolic pathways after surgery. We additionally performed correlation analyses to link clinical covariates with microbial signatures. This public dataset enables independent reprocessing and cross-study comparisons, facilitating exploration of diversion-strategy-specific microbial remodeling and validation of SDT’s gut microbiota-preserving capacity.

articles.title: A single-cell RNA-seq dataset characterizing cellular diversity in healthy equine skin
articles.abstract: Abstract The skin serves as the primary barrier tissue in horses and is frequently affected by immune-mediated dermatological conditions, most notably insect bite hypersensitivity (IBH). Yet, the cellular composition and transcriptional landscape of normal equine skin have never been characterized at single-cell resolution. Here, we present a single-cell RNA sequencing dataset of healthy equine skin comprising 85,574 high-quality transcriptomes from two horses, with one skin biopsy collected from each horse, divided into two portions for independent processing via manual or automated tissue dissociation. The dataset resolved 22 transcriptionally distinct cell populations, encompassing keratinocyte subpopulations that reflect discrete epidermal differentiation states, adnexal epithelial lineages, stromal and vascular compartments, and resident immune cell types. Cell-type identities are supported by marker gene expression, KEGG pathway enrichment analysis, and functional module scoring. This dataset constitutes the first single-cell transcriptomic reference of normal equine skin, enabling investigations into equine dermatological diseases, wound healing, immune responses and comparative skin biology.

articles.title: A haplotype-resolved chromosome-scale genome assembly of the triploid Boechera sierraensis (Brassicaceae)
articles.abstract: Boechera sierraensis is a recently described apomictic triploid species (Brassicaceae) endemic to the high-elevation granitic slopes of the Sierra Nevada, USA. It displays extraordinary tolerance to heat, drought, and high light stress, making it an important emerging model for understanding plant adaptation to extreme alpine environments and rapid climatic change. Despite its physiological and ecological significance, no genomic resources have been available for this taxon, limiting investigation into the genetic basis of its stress resilience, apomictic reproduction, and complex hybrid origin involving B. lemmonii , B. paupercula , and B. retrofracta . To address these gaps, we generated a haplotype-resolved, chromosome-scale assembly of the B. sierraensis genome (2n = 3x = 22) using a combination of long-read and short-read sequencing. The assembly fully phased the three parental subgenomes, yielding assembled sizes of 210.8 Mb, 198.6 Mb, and 213.2 Mb. Assembly contiguity was high, with scaffold N50 values of 28.2–31.1 Mb, and BUSCO completeness reached 99.5–99.8% across haplotypes. The phased nature of the assembly preserves subgenome-specific architectural features, including centromeric and pericentromeric regions, enabling comparative analyses of repeat composition and centromere-associated sequences. Repetitive elements constitute a substantial fraction of each subgenome and are dominated by long terminal repeat (LTR) retrotransposons, particularly Gypsy and Copia families. Using PacBio Iso-Seq and Illumina RNA-seq, we annotated 79,345 protein-coding genes across the three subgenomes, the majority of which received functional assignments through multiple annotation frameworks. This study provides a haplotype-resolved genomic resource for B. sierraensis , which can support studies of apomixis, hybrid triploidy, and the genetic basis of stress tolerance in this alpine species.

articles.title: A genus-labeled dataset of individual trees outside forests in Baden-Württemberg, Germany
articles.abstract: Abstract Detailed data on individual trees growing outside forests (TOF) are essential for arboriculture, biodiversity assessment, ecosystem services assessment, climate adaptation, and environmental health research. However, existing datasets are often incomplete and seldom provide taxonomic information beyond publicly managed trees in cities of Germany and other countries where maintaining a tree cadaster is a legal requirement. Here, we present for the first time a statewide dataset of individual TOF in the state of Baden-Württemberg, Germany, including tree locations, crown geometry, height, and genus-level labels. We mapped trees from high-resolution multi-spectral aerial imagery and height data using deep learning, with terrestrial LiDAR surveys used to create training labels within the URBORETUM project. The released dataset includes ten genus-level classes, including the aggregate categories “Other Deciduous” and “Coniferous” where assignment from aerial imagery is uncertain. The final ten-class genus model achieved a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.382 at an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.5 (mAP@0.5) and a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.627 for taxonomic class assignment, while a separately trained one-class tree detector achieved an mAP@0.5 of 0.647, indicating stronger reliability for crown detection than for taxonomic classification. The final inventory contains 16.3 million predicted trees across the mapped non-forest domain of Baden-Württemberg. Beyond providing a statewide dataset, this work offers a scalable vision and operational blueprint for an evolving tree inventory that can be systematically improved over time through better imagery, richer local reference data, and targeted retraining.

articles.title: Strengthening Rare Disease Data Readiness: a semantic approach to cross-registry interoperability
articles.abstract: Abstract Rare diseases affect an estimated 446 million people worldwide, yet reliable epidemiological data are scarce due to insufficient data sources and lack of standardization. The German National Registry for Rare Diseases (NARSE) aims to establish a comprehensive epidemiological data basis and enable data availability for research. However, limited interoperability between clinical and epidemiological data sources restricts secondary use and cross-registry research. This study assesses the semantic interoperability between NARSE and two core data sets: the German Medical Informatics Initiative (MII) core data set and the European Rare Disease Registry Infrastructure (ERDRI) core data set. Using a formal consensus process, mapping categories (exactMatch, closeMatch, broadMatch, narrowMatch, relatedMatch) were defined, analyzed, and evaluated for information loss using a heuristic scale. Most NARSE elements aligned with the MII core data set, while mapping to the ERDRI core data set revealed more challenges due to undefined value sets and inconsistent coding systems. These findings highlight the importance of consistent application of coding standards to safeguard information value and improve interoperability in rare disease research.

articles.title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of the Ornamental Amaranth (Amaranthus caudatus)
articles.abstract: Amaranthus caudatus L. is an ornamental and pseudocereal species of the Amaranthus genus, notable for its striking pendulous panicles and vibrant crimson coloration. Despite its distinctive morphology and economic value, its genome has remained uncharacterized. Here, we present a high-quality chromosome-scale genome assembly of A. caudatus totaling 426.72 Mb, with 93.68% of sequences anchored onto 16 chromosomes. The assembly comprises contigs with an N50 of 12.64 Mb. The genome contains 26,343 predicted protein-coding genes, 95% of which were functionally annotated. This high-quality genome provides a valuable resource for elucidating the genetic basis of its ornamental traits, pigment biosynthesis, and domestication.

articles.title: Genome-wide DNA methylation profiling of the zebrafish forebrain
articles.abstract: Abstract The zebrafish forebrain is a central hub for cognitive and social behaviors, yet a comprehensive, region-specific DNA methylation reference for this tissue is not available. To address this gap, we generated a genome-wide methylation map of the adult zebrafish forebrain using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) long-read sequencing. Forebrains from six individuals were profiled, enabling direct detection of multiple DNA base modifications at single-base resolution. The resulting dataset includes CpG-associated 5-methylcytosine (5 mC) and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5 hmC), as well as non-CpG 5 mC and candidate N6-methyladenine (6 mA) signals, with 96.8% genome coverage. CpG methylation was widespread, with 64.2% of CpG sites classified as highly 5 mC-modified. In contrast, 5 hmC and non-CpG methylation were markedly less abundant, and 6 mA was detected at very low levels and showed poor reproducibility across replicates. CpG islands showed a bimodal distribution of methylation, promoter regions displayed elevated variability compared to gene bodies, and CC-context non-CpG methylation exhibited significant strand asymmetry. This resource provides a high-resolution epigenomic baseline for the adult zebrafish forebrain.

articles.title: Genome assembly and gene annotation of Babesia ovis Israeli strain (Piroplasmida: Babesiidae) using PacBio HiFi sequencing
articles.abstract: Abstract Babesia ovis is a unicellular parasite of sheep and goats transmitted by the tick Rhipicephalus bursa . B. ovis infection is widespread and can be lethal, and therefore there is need for a deeper understanding of its biology and pathogenesis. There is currently a single genome available for a clinical isolate of B. ovis , and no laboratory strains have been sequenced so far. In this study we have sequenced and assembled the genome of the Israeli laboratory strain of B. ovis using highly accurate long-read sequencing (PacBio HiFi). The resulting assembly has high contiguity, with the four largest contigs comprising 96% of the assembly and representing putative near-complete chromosomes. Annotation identified 3,549 genes, of which 3,046 (85.6%) could be functionally annotated. BUSCO analysis on the annotated genes revealed 95.5%, 98.8% and 100% completeness of the Aconoidasida, Apicomplexa, and Alveolata lineages, respectively. Comparative analysis with other annotated piroplasmida genomes reveals the vast majority of predicted genes clustered in orthogroups. The availability of a high-quality genome assembly for a tractable laboratory strain could prove impactful in unlocking more basic and applied research avenues to be pursued for this important parasite system.

articles.title: Brain 18F-FDG template using images from a new brain-dedicated positron emission tomography scanner
articles.abstract: Abstract 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography ( 18 F-FDG-PET) may be a useful tool as a biomarker of neurodegeneration. However, commercial brain templates may differ substantially from the PET images generated in new scanners in terms of resolution. We aimed to build an 18 F-FDG-PET image template using images acquired in a brain-dedicated PET to enable normalization optimization. A total of 167 patients underwent an 18 F-FDG-PET study on a brain-dedicated PET system. The images were automatically co-registered in Pmod 4.1, followed by iterative deformable registration in ANTs (Advanced Normalization Tools) to build the template. We obtained an 18 F-FDG-PET brain template with 1-mm 3 voxels and a 268 x 268 x 152 matrix to use as a reference for PET image normalization. In addition, we generated a map with 66 regions of interest (ROIs) manually adapted from the Automated Anatomical Labeling (AAL) ROI map for quantification of the normalized images and a mask to exclude extra-parenchymal regions. The development of a brain template with images acquired on the dedicated brain PET is of great utility for application in new scanners with improved resolution.

articles.title: Marine Heat Waves and Cold Spells – Multiple Analysis/Definitions (MHW-MAD): A Multi-Definition Global Marine Heatwave Database from Satellite Sea Surface Temperature Data
articles.abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are prolonged anomalies of warm sea surface temperature (SST) that can disrupt marine ecosystems, physical climate processes, and human coastal activities. MHW definitions vary due to different stakeholders requirements, such as ecological scientists and climate scientists having differing yet specific thresholds and metrics. Here we introduce a new global database of daily MHW metrics: climatological baselines, threshold exceedances, SST anomalies, and categorical event classifications of severity, derived from the European Space Agency SST Climate Change Initiative (ESA SST CCI) climate data record (CDR; 1982–2021) version 3.0 and an extension from 2022–2024 provided as an interim climate data record (iCDR). Building on the widely used definition of MHWs, periods in which SST exceeds the local 90th percentile for 5 or more days, our database extends this framework by incorporating multiple baseline climatologies (including fixed 30-year periods and rolling 30-year windows, as well as the period for reanalysis 1993–2022), varied percentile thresholds (90th, 95th, 99th), and both raw and linearly detrended SST anomalies. We also implement alternative event duration criteria (minimum 10 and 30 d persistence) to classify longer-lasting warm events. In addition to warm extremes, we provide marine cold spell (MCS) indices derived from the 1st, 5th and 10th percentiles, enabling analysis of cold as well as warm ocean extremes within the same framework. All data products are provided at daily resolution on a 0.05° (∼ 5 km) grid, with outputs including daily climatological percentiles, SST anomalies and binary MHW flags with severity category indices. This comprehensive database provides a consistent foundation for detecting and analysing MHWs across time and space, enabling researchers to assess how methodological choices affect MHW characterisation. By offering multiple definitions in parallel, the database facilitates intercomparison studies and supports applications from climate monitoring and model evaluation to marine ecological impact assessment, thereby providing users with pre-made indices for extremes, with the ambition to be rolled out into the future with new data releases. The dataset is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21835325 (Hayward et al., 2026).

articles.title: SHELDA: sub-hourly European quality  controlled sea level dataset
articles.abstract: Freely accessible sea level databases often contain time series measured with hourly or even longer sampling step, or they contain high-frequency data that have not undergone quality control procedures. To address this gap, the SHELDA (Sub-Hourly European Quality Controlled Sea Level DAtaset) has been created. This dataset comprises 257 individual tide gauge records in NetCDF format (https://doi.org/10.14284/764, Balić and Šepić, 2025), each representing quality-controlled sea level time series sampled at intervals between 1 and 15 min, along with residual time series derived by removing tidal components. The duration of individual records ranges from a minimum of one month to a maximum of 13 years. This manuscript outlines the rigorous quality control procedures (i.e., removal of out-of-range values, application of an automatic spike detection algorithm, visual inspection) implemented and discusses the procedures that were not implemented (i.e., corrections of datum shifts). The manuscript further describes the spatial and temporal coverage of the dataset, along with technical specifications. All data are distributed under the CC BY 4.0 licence. SHELDA enables precise identification and analysis of sea level variability at timescales ranging from minutes to seasonal and longer, depending on the stability of the long term series along the European coasts and along the coasts of Greenland, Canary Islands, Israel, Lebanon and Türkiye.

articles.title: History of anthropogenic Phosphorus inputs (HaPi)  to the terrestrial biosphere from 1860 to 2020
articles.abstract: Nitrogen (N) and Phosphorus (P) are essential nutrients for sustaining life on Earth and regulating ecosystem productivity and Earth system biogeochemistry, and have been increasingly applied in global agriculture to meet the growing demand for food production. Quantifying the spatial and temporal dynamics of nutrient inputs to the terrestrial biosphere is crucial for understanding global biogeochemical cycles, analyzing nutrient flows in crop-livestock systems, managing nutrient resources sustainably, and mitigating nutrient-related environmental impacts. Here, built upon our previous work mapping global nitrogen inputs (History of anthropogenic Nitrogen inputs, HaNi), this study presents the History of anthropogenic P inputs (HaPi) dataset, a comprehensive quantification of human-driven P fluxes to terrestrial ecosystems. HaPi covers the period from 1860 to 2020 and has a spatial resolution of 5 arcmin (about 10 km at the equator) with an annual time-step. This harmonized dataset integrates seven components, including P fertilizer application on croplands and pastures, manure P application on croplands and pastures, manure P deposition on pastures and rangelands, and atmospheric P deposition. The results reveal that global total P input increased more than tenfold, from 3.8 Tg yr −1 in the 1860s to 41.0 Tg yr −1 in the 2010s, with mineral fertilizer and livestock manure contributing equally to the increase. Regional patterns have shifted significantly over the study period, with China, South Asia, and Brazil surpassing Europe and the USA as the regions with the highest P inputs in recent decades. Furthermore, mineral fertilizers dominate P inputs in most industrialized countries in the Northern Hemisphere, whereas manure P remains the primary source in many countries of the Southern Hemisphere. The HaPi dataset improves P mass budget calculations and provides essential forcing data for empirical or mechanistic models, supporting critical research in Earth system biogeochemistry, agricultural nutrient management, water quality control, and assessments of the coupled human-Earth system. The dataset is available at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.29930279 (Bian et al., 2026).

articles.title: Longitudinal Vestibular Schwannoma Dataset with Consensus-based Human-in-the-loop Annotations
articles.abstract: Abstract Accurate segmentation of vestibular schwannoma (VS) on MRI is essential for clinical management, yet large-scale, high-quality annotated datasets remain scarce. We present a publicly available longitudinal VS dataset comprising 534 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted scans from 184 patients across 15 or more clinical sites, hosted on The Cancer Imaging Archive. To generate trustworthy annotations at scale, we developed a human-in-the-loop framework combining a bootstrapped 3D nnU-Net model with multi-round consensus-based expert review and correction. This methodology, rather than the model itself, is the primary contribution, offering a reproducible and resource-efficient protocol for annotating complex longitudinal imaging data. The framework reduced annotation time by approximately 37.4% compared to conventional manual approaches. Segmentation accuracy on the internal test set improved across bootstrapping rounds (DSC: 0.9141 to 0.9687), while performance on external datasets remained stable, demonstrating cross-domain robustness. Expert radiological review further revealed nuanced failure cases, underscoring the necessity of human oversight in annotation pipelines for heterogeneous clinical data.

articles.title: A Spatially Explicit 1-km Gridded Multi-sector Carbon Emission Dataset for China (2000–2020) with an Extension to 2021–2023
articles.abstract: Abstract Integrating carbon mitigation into territorial spatial governance can facilitate the achievement of emission reduction targets. High-resolution datasets with detailed spatiotemporal and sectoral information enable more precise and effective spatial planning and management of carbon emissions. Taking territorial space as the fundamental carrier of carbon emissions, this study constructs- differentiated spatial proxy-factor weighting layers based on the emission characteristics of different sectors. Sectoral emissions are then allocated to the corresponding territorial spaces through an iterative mapping process using these weighting layers. Based on this approach, this study develops a 1 km × 1 km gridded carbon emission dataset for China’s agriculture, mining, industry, transportation, commercial services, and residential sectors at five-year intervals from 2000 to 2020 and extends the dataset annually to 2021–2023 using 2020 as the baseline. This spatially explicit carbon emission dataset integrates comprehensive spatial coverage, sectoral detail, and high spatial resolution, providing a robust foundation for carbon management within territorial spatial governance and supporting the formulation of spatial planning strategies for emission reduction.

articles.title: The State of Scientific Poster Sharing and Reuse
articles.abstract: Abstract Scientific posters are one of the most common forms of scholarly communication and contain early-stage insights with potential to accelerate scientific discovery. We investigated where posters are shared, to what extent their sharing aligns with the FAIR principles, and how commonly they are reused. We identified 86 platforms hosting posters, with many not assigning persistent identifiers. A total of 150k posters are shared as of 2024 on the 43 platforms where we were able to count, which is relatively low. Looking in more detail at posters shared on Zenodo and Figshare, we found that repositories are not always supporting structured metadata critical for poster discovery, like conference information, and that researchers are not providing such metadata even if they are supported. We also observed that while there is some engagement with posters in terms of views and downloads, citing posters is not yet a common practice. These gaps mean valuable early-stage insights are being lost to the scientific community, pointing to a need for clearer guidelines and stronger incentives for FAIR poster sharing and reuse.

articles.title: A clinical brain MRI dataset of naturally occurring motion artifacts with paired artifact-free images
articles.abstract: Motion artifacts remain a major challenge in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), degrading image quality and compromising diagnostic reliability. Although deep learning–based retrospective correction methods have advanced for brain MRI, their development is constrained by training datasets dominated by synthetic or task-induced motion artifacts, which do not adequately represent real-world clinical motion. We present a brain MRI dataset of naturally occurring motion artifacts derived from routine examinations at a large medical center. The dataset comprises 5,143 paired 2D slices (4.0–6.7 mm slice thickness) derived from 747 paired volumes across 731 patients, and 147 paired 3D volumes (0.67–1.1 mm slice thickness) from 146 patients, spanning T1-weighted, contrast-enhanced T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery sequences. Data were curated through a five-step pipeline comprising deep learning–based prescreening, sequence filtering and acquisition categorization, rigid registration, automated screening, and manual quality control. Each motion-corrupted/artifact-free pair is annotated with objective image quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM, MS-SSIM, and LPIPS) and subjective artifact severity scores, enabling the development and evaluation of clinically applicable motion correction methods.

articles.title: An fMRI dataset of verbalized spontaneous thought with annotated transcripts and self-report trait measures
articles.abstract: Spontaneous thought is pervasive in everyday human cognition, yet datasets capturing its neural dynamics under minimally interrupted conditions remain limited. The current dataset was acquired from a think-aloud functional MRI experiment in which 118 participants continuously verbalized their spontaneous thoughts during 10-minute scanning sessions. The raw MRI data and verbal transcripts with sentence-level timestamps were previously released and analyzed in our prior study examining neural activity associated with thought transitions. Building on that release, we additionally provide preprocessed MRI data, speech transcriptions with word-level timestamps aligned to image acquisition, large language model-generated ratings of transcribed thoughts across emotional and sensory dimensions, and self-report survey measures assessing personality, mental health, and cognitive abilities. Validation analyses demonstrated activation in expected cortical regions associated with speech production and sensory content identified from transcript annotations, agreement between language model and human ratings, and adequate internal consistency of survey measures, supporting the dataset’s overall quality. This dataset enables reuse for investigations of spontaneous thought, speech generation, and individual differences using naturalistic functional MRI data.

articles.title: A knowledge graph and dataset of natural cell-penetrating peptides
articles.abstract: Abstract Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) are short sequences characterized by their ability to translocate across cell membranes without significant damage. This property allows CPPs to function as molecular carriers that facilitate the intracellular delivery of bioactive cargoes. Despite their potential, the discovery of new CPPs relies on time-intensive experimental validation. In silico methodologies offer an alternative; however, existing tabular databases hinder the extraction of relational biological context. Consequently, this data structure may restrict the capacity of computational models to learn biologically meaningful relationships. To address this gap, we structured experimentally validated CPP data into a knowledge graph that explicitly represents this relational biological context. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first knowledge graph that integrates cell-penetrating peptides with their associated cellular uptake mechanisms, cell lines, cargo molecules, and subcellular delivery locations. To establish a functional biological context, we linked the specific uptake mechanisms to regulatory genes and chemical inhibitors. To construct this resource, we collected 5,288 peptide sequences from CPPsite3, processed the annotations through a normalization workflow, and used a graph retrieval-augmented generation method (Graph RAG) for ontology mapping. We mapped annotations such as uptake mechanisms, subcellular locations, cell lines, and cargo types to the Gene Ontology (GO), Cell Line Ontology (CLO), and Chemical Entities of Biological Interest (ChEBI) to ensure interoperability. We serialized the dataset as a Resource Description Framework (RDF) graph and applied the Semanticscience Integrated Ontology (SIO) as an upper-level ontology. The complete dataset and knowledge graph are openly available from Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21031596 ); in addition, we provide an interactive, queryable version at https://cppkg.bio2vec.net/ .

articles.title: An objective hourly dataset of typhoon remnant vortices affecting China (1980–2024)
articles.abstract: This study presents an objectively identified and hourly resolved dataset of Typhoon Remnant Vortices (TRVs) affecting China during 1980–2024. Based on the tropical cyclone best-track dataset and ERA5 reanalysis, we developed an automated identification and tracking algorithm to detect and follow TRVs after the dissipation of their parent typhoons. The dataset covers 15°N–55°N, 95°E–140°E, including vortices located within 200 km of the Chinese mainland. A total of 341 TRVs, comprising 11,728 hourly records, were identified and tracked. For each TRV, the dataset provides a more objective and temporally continuous description of TRVs affecting China, including geographic position, 850 hPa stream function, relative vorticity, wind speed, extratropical transition status, and termination category. Climatological analyses reveal pronounced seasonality, with activity concentrated from June to November and peaking in August. Spatial analysis indicates that TRVs predominantly form in low-latitude coastal regions of South China and subsequently propagate inland toward mid–high latitude regions. With long-term coverage, hourly resolution, and standardized dynamical parameters, this dataset provides a consistent and reproducible foundation for TRV climatology, extreme rainfall attribution, and numerical modelling studies.

articles.title: A standardized collection of human stool and fermented food microbiomes from the Launch Phase of the Microbiota Vault Initiative
articles.abstract: Abstract The human gut microbiome and traditional food systems are threatened by lifestyle changes linked with industrialization. The gut microbiome plays a key role in human health, yet publicly available microbiome data lack global representation. Similarly, while fermented foods serve as an important nutritional and cultural resource, the microbial diversity of traditional fermented foods remains relatively unexplored and is equally at risk. Here we present a collection of human gut and fermented food microbiota profiles generated during the Launch Phase of the Microbiota Vault Initiative (MVI). This dataset includes standardized metadata and the 16S rRNA-based amplicon sequencing data from human stool (N = 767) and fermented food samples (N = 157) deposited into the MVI by researchers across Asia, Africa, Europe and Latin America. These data are broadly compatible with other public microbiome datasets and are readily reusable, provided that appropriate attribution is given to the local researchers who maintain ownership of these collections. We anticipate that this resource will facilitate future comparative studies and meta-analyses across diverse human populations and fermented food systems, promoting more representative microbiome research.

articles.title: High temporal-resolution microclimate and photovoltaic power dataset for sustainable rooftop design in subtropical humid city
articles.abstract: This paper presents a high resolution microclimate monitoring dataset designed to explore rooftop microclimate responses to different rooftop configurations within a subtropical humid campus setting. The dataset comprises measurements from seven rooftops representing five roofing types: bare roof, bare roof with HVAC units, green roof, PV roof, and PV integrated green roof (PVIGR). The dataset is based on data collected over a one-and-a-half-year period on a university campus in Hong Kong. Microclimate data were collected using various sensors, including temperature and relative-humidity sensors, anemometers, and pyranometers. In addition, the dataset also provides PV power generation data, which supports studies of PV performance and the microclimate impacts of PVIGR designs. Lastly, weather data from a nearby weather station were also included in this dataset for future reference. This dataset addresses a significant gap in existing literature that primarily focuses on conventional roof types and supports the evaluation of alternative rooftop designs under comparable campus-scale conditions. This paper provides a comprehensive description of the rooftop sites, data collection methods, records, and validation processes. Potential applications encompass analyzing microclimate characteristics, supporting validation or benchmarking of computational fluid dynamics models under comparable rooftop conditions, optimizing photovoltaic conversion efficiency, and informing sustainable rooftop design studies.

articles.title: A Monthly Coal Mine-Level Methane Emission Dataset for China from 2018 to 2024
articles.abstract: Coal mine methane (CMM) is a major source of methane emissions in the energy sector and plays a significant role in global climate change. However, existing CMM emission inventories are typically limited to national or provincial scales and lack long-term, high spatial resolution datasets at the coal mine level. To address this gap, this study develops a comprehensive methane emission dataset covering over 3,000 coal mines across China (excluding Taiwan) from 2018 to 2024. The dataset systematically integrates multi-source coal production data and applies a hybrid estimation framework combining IPCC Tier 1, 2 and 3 methodologies. It includes detailed information on mine name, administrative location (province and prefecture-level city), geographic coordinates, production capacity, mining type, methane emission factors, and monthly emissions. Uncertainty in emissions is quantified using Monte Carlo simulations. National CMM emissions increased overall from 25.10 Mt CH 4 in 2018 to 32.87 Mt CH 4 in 2024, despite a slight decline from the 2023 peak. The estimated uncertainty ranges from 8.93% to 14.74%, indicating that the results remain within an acceptable level of uncertainty. Multi-scale comparisons indicate that the dataset applies more localized emission factors, provides more accurate source locations, and captures broadly reliable temporal trends. This dataset provides a robust foundation for analyzing the spatiotemporal patterns of CMM emissions, assessing mitigation potential, and improving greenhouse gas inventories, thereby supporting methane mitigation efforts in China and globally.

articles.title: A paediatric dataset of non-dermoscopic skin images for dermatological AI research
articles.abstract: This paper introduces DermoPed, a non-dermoscopic dermatology dataset composed almost entirely of paediatric patients’ images. The long-term goal is to advance research in automated dermatological image analysis with a specific focus on non-dermoscopic images, i.e., those captured using consumer-grade cameras, thereby promoting accessible diagnosis for underprivileged and underserved populations. However, this objective is often challenged by the limited availability of data and the heterogeneous quality of clinical images, issues that are discussed in detail in this work and carefully addressed during the preprocessing phase. The resulting dataset comprises more than 46,000 medium-to-high quality images from 229 distinct patients, the majority of whom are paediatric. In addition, we release a separate “challenging” subset of lower-quality crops with automatically computed image-quality labels, intended to support the study of model robustness under realistic acquisition conditions.

articles.title: A dataset of full-length transcripts for the giant freshwater prawn (Macrobrachium rosenbergii)
articles.abstract: Macrobrachium rosenbergii is a major global aquaculture species, but its large (~3-4 Gb), highly heterozygous and repeat-rich genome has resulted in fragmented draft assemblies, limiting accurate gene annotation and functional genomics. High-quality, isoform-resolved full-length transcripts are therefore essential for gene discovery and downstream applications. Here, we present a dataset of full-length transcripts generated from seven tissues of an adult female M. rosenbergii (i.e., hemolymph, antennal base, eyestalk, gill, brain, intestine, and abdominal ganglion), producing 4,131,688 circular consensus sequences and 38,955 non-redundant full-length transcripts (N50 = 3,383 bp) using PacBio Iso-Seq. Functional annotation was assigned to 32,275 transcripts using multiple public databases, and 17,696 candidate long non-coding RNAs were predicted, including 2,712 high-confidence lncRNAs supported by four complementary tools. The reliability and reusability were independently validated by mapping Illumina short-read RNA-seq data from nine libraries constructed from brain tissues of three male morphotypes to the Iso-Seq reference transcripts, achieving 72.44% overall mapping rates. This dataset provides a comprehensive, reference-quality full-length transcripts for M. rosenbergii , enabling improved genome annotation, isoform-level expression analysis, and comparative transcriptomics.

articles.title: Multiproxy dataset for the Holocene sedimentary record of the Sado Valley, southwest Portugal
articles.abstract: Abstract Paleoenvironmental characterization and studies of the environmental evolution of coastal basins (e.g. lagoons and estuaries) are based on information retrieved from sedimentary records through the analysis of diverse environmental proxies. This information is often presented only in figures, illustrations, and graphics in published papers, while the raw data are difficult to access. Nevertheless, this information is valuable for (i) increasing resolution (adding more data) within the same sedimentary basin, both vertically (i.e., in-depth; through time) and horizontally (i.e., spatial analyses); (ii) comparing results among similar coastal systems, and iii) analyzing different responses to diverse forcings in coastal systems located elsewhere. This dataset provides the results of sedimentological and paleoenvironmental (texture, magnetic susceptibility, total organic matter, organic carbon and total nitrogen content, C/N elemental ratios, and C and N stable isotope ratios) proxy analyses in sediment cores collected in the lower Sado Valley (Portugal).

articles.title: A Multi-Center, Multi-Modal Chest CT and Clinical Dataset for Differentiating Pulmonary Aspergillus from Non-Aspergillus and Non-Fungal Infections
articles.abstract: Pulmonary Aspergillus infection (PAI) presents a critical diagnostic challenge due to its clinical management differing significantly from that of pulmonary non- Aspergillus fungal infection (PNAFI) and pulmonary non-fungal infection (PNFI). While Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a promising solution for rapid triage, its development is currently severely bottlenecked by data scarcity. Existing studies primarily rely on small, private, and single-center datasets, which hampers the generalizability of models and precludes reproducible research. To date, there is no publicly available, multi-center benchmark dataset that integrates imaging with key host immune factors for this domain. To address this critical gap, we present the first comprehensive, open-access dataset of its kind, collected from 569 patients across 4 hospitals in China. This dataset comprises: (1) standardized volumetric chest CT scans in NIfTI format; (2) a curated clinical record containing definitive diagnostic labels, demographics, and critical laboratory variables (e.g., lymphocyte counts, D-dimer). Technical validation was conducted for two binary tasks: Task 1, Fungi vs Non-Fungi, and Task 2, Aspergillus vs non- Aspergillus . This study introduced three models for classification: a clinical model using clinical variables, an imaging model based on CT images, and a fusion model combining both clinical variables and CT images. Model performance was evaluated through receiver operating characteristic analysis, with sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and area under the curve (AUC) reported as key metrics. As a rare and versatile resource, this dataset supports not only the development of robust AI classification algorithms but also facilitates clinical prediction modeling, the investigation of the predictive role of host variables (e.g., age, comorbidities), decision-making regarding invasive interventions, and radiological education, thereby accelerating precision medicine in pulmonary infectious diseases.

articles.title: A global 60 m land cover dataset with a fine classification system for 1975 and 1980 derived from Landsat MSS observations
articles.abstract: Abstract Long-term land cover datasets are essential for understanding human-environment interactions and global environmental change, yet global land cover information pre-1985 remains scarce because of limited availability of early satellite observations. Here, we present GLC_FCS60, the first global 60 m land cover dataset with a fine classification system for 1975 and 1980, derived from Landsat Multispectral Scanner (MSS) observations. Specifically, an improved comprehensive change detection method with an adaptive thresholding strategy was applied to identify changed and unchanged land-cover pixels. The detected changed areas were then updated using high-confidence temporally stable training samples and locally adaptive classification models on the Google Earth Engine platform. The updated land cover maps were further optimized through post-processing to mitigate potential spurious changes, after which the GLC_FCS60 time-series maps were generated. Finally, using 71,983 globally distributed validation samples, we assessed the accuracy of GLC_FCS60, achieving overall accuracies of 80.13% and 80.08% for the 10 basic classes in 1975 and 1980, respectively, while a dedicated change/no-change validation achieved an overall accuracy of 78.61%. Therefore, GLC_FCS60 fills a critical gap in global land cover observations prior to the mid-1980s and provides a valuable baseline for investigating long-term land cover dynamics from the mid-1970s to the present.

articles.title: A Chromosome-level reference genome assembly of the Fusarium avenaceum
articles.abstract: Fusarium avenaceum is a widely distributed fungal species that includes polyphagous plant pathogens, some of which produce mycotoxins of concern to agricultural production and food safety. Here, we present genome sequencing data and an RNA-seq dataset generated to support gene annotation for F. avenaceum strain XZ-22-127, which was isolated from highland barley. PacBio HiFi reads and Hi-C data were used to generate a 42.26-Mb assembly comprising nine chromosomes, with a scaffold N50 of 5.07 Mb and a GC content of 47.97%. BUSCO analysis identified 99.9% of the expected BUSCOs as complete. Compared with the previously available chromosome-level assembly of F. avenaceum strain WV21P1A, the XZ-22-127 assembly had a slightly higher scaffold N50 (5.07 versus 4.96 Mb) and BUSCO completeness (99.9% versus 99.7%), while the two assemblies were similar in genome size, GC content, and chromosome number. The deposited resources include the raw sequencing reads, chromosome-level assembly, protein-coding gene models, repeat annotations, predicted transcript, coding-sequence and protein files, and InterProScan and eggNOG-mapper functional annotation files. These datasets provide a complementary genomic resource for F. avenaceum and related fungi.

articles.title: Daily snow depth in the Southern Andes (2010–2024):  a quality-controlled dataset from Chile and Argentina
articles.abstract: Seasonal snow is a critical component of the water cycle in the Southern Andes of Chile and Argentina. Quantitative assessments of snow accumulation remain constrained by the scarcity, heterogeneity, and inconsistency of in situ observations, resulting in substantial uncertainties in mountain hydrological modeling. To address this gap, we compiled and quality-controlled snow depth observations to produce a consistent daily dataset from 81 stations between 21 and 54° S covering 2010–2024. Our quality-control procedure involved data compilation and preprocessing, followed by harmonization of snow depth observations, primarily by correcting the ground reference level relative to the soil surface during snow-free periods and removing anomalous spikes and observations outside physically plausible ranges. This process improved data reliability, increasing the Physical Consistency Index (PCI) from 87 % to 95 % at selected stations in the Maipo River Basin, while reducing the median number of days with data across stations by 23 % (from 1392 to 1074 d). The snow depth data availability increased from one station in 2010 to 57 stations in 2024, largely driven by the expansion of the monitoring network operated by the General Directorate of Water (DGA), Chile. However, this expansion remains spatially uneven across the Andean zones. The Mediterranean Andes have the largest number of stations (39), as well as the largest number of stations with highly complete records with 17 stations reaching 80 %–100 % data coverage, compared with only nine stations each in the Arid and Wet Andes, highlighting persistent spatial and temporal gaps. Using this newly quality-controlled dataset, we find that snow depth generally increases from the Arid to the Wet Andes in association with increasing precipitation, whereas its relationship with elevation is not consistently positive. The snow depth-elevation relationship is nonlinear in the Arid and Mediterranean Andes, with maximum observed snow depths at 4300 m a.s.l. in the Elqui River Basin and 3300 m a.s.l. in the Maipo River Basin. In contrast, the available observations indicate a positive snow depth-elevation relationship in the Wet Andes (Maule–Itata River Basin). However, these relationships should be interpreted in the context of the specific spatial and temporal conditions represented by the available observations. This open-access, quality-controlled snow depth dataset (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21577171, Medina and Caro, 2026) represents the largest and most complete collection of continuous snow depth observations for the Southern Andes and provides a basis for hydrological applications, reanalysis evaluation, and seasonal streamflow forecasting.

articles.title: A harmonized cross-national dataset of digital sectors
articles.abstract: Digital sectors have emerged as a key driver of firm innovation, productivity and economic growth. Building on the OECD framework, the United Kingdom introduced a digital sector classification in 2015. China has likewise developed its own digital sector classification as part of its broader effort to define and measure the digital economy. However, the absence of a harmonized correspondence between these classification systems constrains cross-country comparisons and empirical research, particularly when Chinese datasets are integrated with international data involving digital inputs and outputs. To address this gap, we construct a concordance dataset linking the Chinese and UK digital sector classifications. Using nearly 15 million firms from the Orbis database, we document differences in the coverage and distribution of digital sectors across geographies, countries, and industries under the three classification frameworks. The dataset enables researchers to evaluate how alternative definitions influence the measurement of the digital economy at the firm, industry, and aggregate levels, providing a valuable resource for comparative research and evidence-based policy-making.

articles.title: Nationwide annual agricultural land-use maps of Germany from 1990 to 2023 derived from satellite imagery
articles.abstract: Abstract We present German-wide annual agricultural land-use maps from 1990 to 2023, created from Landsat and Sentinel-2 images using a deep learning approach. Based on farmers’ declarations from 2006 to 2022, we extracted annual training samples for 13 crop classes and one grassland class. These samples were used to train a multi-year one-dimensional convolutional neural network, which was subsequently applied to generate the annual land-use maps. Between 2010 and 2022, overall map accuracies ranged between 85% and 93%. When averaged over time, dominant classes like grassland, rapeseed, winter cereals, sugar beet, and maize were detected with high accuracy (≥90%). Conversely, minor classes such as fallow land and plantation were predicted with low accuracy (≤52%). Comparison of map areas with agricultural statistics over time revealed high correlations for most classes, particularly maize ( r = 0.978). The presented maps provide an essential basis for analyzing long-term trends in agricultural land-use. They can be used to fill temporal gaps in national agricultural statistics and to disaggregate those statistics to higher spatial units.

articles.title: A dataset of strong dependency and conflict graphs generated from Boolean formulas encoding the variability of highly configurable software systems
articles.abstract: Abstract Variability models describe the configuration options of highly configurable software systems and the direct constraints between them. The dependencies and conflicts those constraints indirectly cause are hidden in the model and too hard to check manually, making it difficult to analyze very large systems like the Linux kernel. This Data Descriptor documents a dataset of 5,709 records that makes those indirect relationships explicit. Each record includes two graphs based on the Boolean formula that represents the variability model of one configurable system: a strong dependency graph and a strong conflict graph. We created each record from publicly available Boolean formulas that other researchers made from variability models and shared under an open license, using our own tool: a C++ program that runs two algorithms based on step-by-step satisfiability solving. The resulting graphs range from 99 to 35,907 options, with a median of 2,874. Provided in the Pajek NET format with clear documentation, and released with the input formulas and the code that builds and checks the graphs, the dataset helps test configuration and sampling methods and supports research on conflict detection, impact analysis, and automated reasoning.
