articles.title: PRIME-CVD: Paired Synthetic Cohort and Structured EMR-Style Data Assets for Education in Cardiovascular Risk Modelling
articles.abstract: Abstract In recent years, progress in medical informatics and machine learning has been accelerated by the availability of openly accessible benchmark datasets. However, patient-level electronic medical record (EMR) data are rarely available for teaching or methodological development due to privacy, governance, and re-identification risks. This has limited opportunities for students from healthcare and clinical backgrounds to gain hands-on experience in coding, data management, and cardiovascular risk modelling. Here we introduce PRIME-CVD, a parametrically rendered informatics medical environment designed explicitly for medical education. PRIME-CVD comprises two openly accessible synthetic data assets, each representing 50,000 adults undergoing primary prevention for cardiovascular disease and parameterised to reproduce the statistical characteristics of a derivation cohort from the Australian New South Wales Lumos linked-data resource. The datasets are generated entirely from a user-specified causal directed acyclic graph parameterised using characteristics of the reference cohort, publicly available Australian population statistics and published epidemiologic effect estimates, rather than from patient-level EMR data or trained generative models. Data Asset 1 provides a clean, analysis-ready cohort suitable for teaching exploratory analysis, stratification, statistical coding, and survival modelling, while Data Asset 2 systematically transforms the same cohort into a structured relational, EMR-style database with deliberately introduced data-quality challenges, including missingness, heterogeneous terminology, inconsistent measurement units, and cross-table linkage requirements. Together, these complementary assets enable healthcare and clinical learners to develop practical skills in coding, data cleaning, harmonisation, cohort reconstruction, and cardiovascular risk modelling without exposing sensitive information. Because all individuals and events are generated de novo, PRIME-CVD preserves realistic subgroup imbalance and risk gradients while ensuring negligible disclosure risk. Although the released PRIME-CVD cohort represents adults with no prior history of cardiovascular disease undergoing primary-prevention risk assessment, the complete data-assembly pipeline is provided through the dedicated GitHub repository. Educators may adapt the supplied code, parameters, and data-generating assumptions to construct alternative synthetic cohorts suited to their own teaching objectives. PRIME-CVD is released under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence to support reproducible and scalable health data science education.

articles.title: Renewable generation and electricity consumption datasets for energy market models generated with artificial intelligence
articles.abstract: Analysis of future energy scenarios requires comprehensive and reliable input datasets. Open-access datasets increase transparency and reduce barriers to entry in modeling. In our study, we use artificial neural network models to transform 43 years of weather reanalysis data into hourly resolution, nationwide time series of renewable energy production (solar, onshore and offshore wind) and electricity consumption datasets. During our research, we developed a data quality control procedure for the ENTSO-E hourly-resolution database based on heat maps, histograms, and z-score values, thereby ensuring that our artificial intelligence models learn from high-quality data. Modeling was performed for all European countries with sufficient data quantity and quality to train machine learning models. The proposed neural-network-based database combines the widest spatial coverage among the reviewed datasets with accuracy that in most cases exceeds existing solar, wind, and electricity consumption databases, making it a valuable complement for European electricity system modelling. The open-access data series created can be used directly as input data for electricity market models, e.g., in unit commitment, network load distribution and pricing studies, and are also particularly suitable for analyzing the frequency, duration, and regional overlap of periods of low renewable energy production (Dunkelflaute events).

articles.title: A Benchmark Dataset of Simultaneous Pickup-Delivery Instances for Demand-controlled and Emission-aware Routing
articles.abstract: Vehicle routing with simultaneous pickup and delivery is a routing problem in which a customer may receive goods from the depot and return goods to it during the same visit. It is the routing structure underlying reverse logistics, the circulation of reusable containers, and circular supply chains. The benchmark instances available for this problem are comparatively small, cover a narrow range of customer counts, and provide little systematic control over the balance between pickup and delivery demand, the tightness of vehicle capacity, or the severity of the time windows. We present SPIDER (Simultaneous Pickup-Delivery Instances for Demand-controlled Emission-aware Routing), a collection of 1,152 instances generated from a complete factorial design over six customer-size levels, three spatial layouts, four pickup-to-delivery demand-ratio strata, four vehicle-capacity levels, and four time-window regimes. Instances range from 50 to 1,000 customers. Each instance specifies depot and customer coordinates, delivery and pickup demands, service times, time-window bounds, and optional load-dependent emission parameters. A master index, a parser, and a distance utility accompany the data, so that instances can be selected or regenerated by design factor.

articles.title: A curated comprehensive dataset of asymmetric organocatalytic Mannich reaction
articles.abstract: Abstract The asymmetric organocatalytic Mannich reaction is one of the key methods for constructing chiral β-aminocarbonyl moieties that occur in the structures of many biologically active compounds, including drugs. The selection of a catalyst and reaction conditions that ensure high enantioselectivity for specific substrates remains a largely empirical task. The scarcity of structured, openly available data hinders the application of machine-learning methods to enantioselectivity prediction and rational catalyst design. We present a dataset of 4015 reactions manually extracted from 153 publications spanning 2000–2025 and covering 468 unique organocatalysts. The structures of the reagents and catalysts, the reaction conditions, and the target values ( ee , ΔΔG‡) are provided in a machine-readable form suitable for training AI-models.

articles.title: A Pan-European Multimodal Dataset Linking Field Photos with Satellite Image Time Series for Agricultural Mapping
articles.abstract: Abstract AgroFusion is a continental-scale, multimodal, pixel-based reference dataset designed to support rigorous evaluation and reproducible research in agricultural remote sensing and geospatial Artificial Intelligence (AI). Built upon the 2018 and 2022 Land Use/Cover Area frame statistical Survey (LUCAS), the dataset integrates 211,483 field observations (107,642 in 2018 and 103,841 in 2022), each linked to field photos (four cardinal views, point centered view, and a close-up), LUCAS land-cover and land-use annotations, with monthly pixel-based Satellite Image Time Series (SITS) from Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, and Landsat-8, agrometeorological data from ERA5-Land, topography from the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, soil properties from AI4SoilHealth, and annual embeddings from AlphaEarth geo-foundation model. AgroFusion is the first continental-scale resource for pairing geo-tagged field photos with pixel-based SITS, semantically rich agricultural covariates, and precomputed foundation model embeddings. This combination will enable a wide range of applications, including multimodal and multiscale crop type classification and phenology retrieval, and the interpretation of satellite-derived agricultural products using ground-level visual context.

articles.title: A harmonized European database of education, telework, labour market and earnings from three Eurostat surveys
articles.abstract: Abstract VSET is a harmonized cross-survey profile-space resource documenting the alignment of education, occupation, labour-market, telework, establishment size, and earnings variables from three Eurostat surveys. It combines three Eurostat microdata sources accessed under an approved research proposal: the Adult Education Survey (AES) 2022, the Labour Force Survey (LFS) 2023, and the Structure of Earnings Survey (SES) 2018. The final harmonized database contains data for 22 countries, 1,440,134 unique demographic profile cells, 39 variables, and a summed profile multiplicity of 3,249,634. Occupations are standardized using ISCO-08 at the 2-digit level, educational attainment is harmonized into four ISCED-based groupings, and SES earnings are converted to euros before aggregation. The integration workflow uses sequential outer joins and deterministic coalescing of overlapping variables. The final rows describe harmonized profiles rather than linked individuals. The N_instances variable records the multiplicity of identical rows combined during final profile compression. The release has no integrated survey weight. Its rows represent harmonized profile combinations rather than linked respondents or population units, and the dataset is intended for inspecting category mappings, profile coverage, merge compatibility, and reproducible cross-survey processing rather than for population inference.

articles.title: A dataset of multichannel broadband recordings of sounds and vibrations acquired from arteriovenous fistulas via a novel force sensor array
articles.abstract: Abstract Arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) are the preferred vascular access for hemodialysis in end-stage renal disease patients. AVFs generate vibrations and sounds due to the peculiar blood flow. Frequent monitoring of these signs is essential for early diagnosis of stenoses, which are the main complication of AVFs. Existing datasets contain only recordings of AVFs bruit sounds acquired via electronic stethoscopes. This paper presents the “Fistula Sounds and Vibrations (FiSaV)” dataset, the first ever publicly available dataset of broadband vibrations and sounds recordings from radio-cephalic AVFs that comprise sphygmic pulses, thrills, and bruits sounds. Signals were acquired by means of an array of broadband force sensors placed onto patients’ skin along the cephalic vein from the anastomosis to the elbow crease. An electrocardiographic lead was simultaneously acquired to provide heartbeats reference. The dataset contains recordings of at least 3 minutes, acquired from 59 patients, 40 with stenosis and 19 without stenosis, comfortably seated with their forearms resting on a table. For some patients, recordings include an additional occlusion test. The open accessibility of the FiSaV dataset aims to facilitate advances in non-invasive monitoring of AVF function by providing objective support for physical examination. The data may promote the development of innovative diagnostic tools and algorithms to detect AVF dysfunction and hemodynamic alterations for a better surveillance and management of hemodialysis patients.

articles.title: Long-term seasonal ruminant livestock distribution datasets in China’s grazing production systems
articles.abstract: Accurate spatial distribution data of grazing livestock are essential for rangeland management and sustainability assessments, yet existing global datasets lack production system differentiation and seasonal resolution. We present China’s Long-term Ruminant Livestock Distribution in Grazing Livestock Production Systems (CLRD-GLPS) dataset, providing seasonally resolved distributions of cattle, sheep, and goats across China’s grazing systems from 2000 to 2021. The dataset was generated using a stacking ensemble machine learning framework integrating Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, and Extra Trees, combined with interpretable machine learning for livestock segmentation. CLRD-GLPS includes 1-km resolution gridded maps distinguishing warm-season and cold-season distributions, with CV-based model-uncertainty layers. Model validation on independent test data achieved R 2 values of 0.954–0.961 for cattle and 0.896–0.915 for sheep/goats. External validation at city level yielded R 2 of 0.74–0.81, supporting dataset reliability across spatial scales. The dataset addresses critical gaps in livestock distribution mapping by separating grazing from non-grazing systems and capturing seasonal dynamics, supporting applications in forage-livestock balance assessment, climate impact studies, and evidence-based policy development.

articles.title: Global 30 m annual cropland extent dynamics (2000–2024): a harmonized baseline of structural evolution and regional disparities
articles.abstract: Accurate annual information on cropland extent is essential for monitoring agricultural change, yet existing global products are often limited to snapshots or multiyear epochs and differ in their cropland definitions. Here we present GACED30, which, to our knowledge, is the first dedicated global 30 m annual cropland-extent dataset covering 2000–2024. The mapping framework combines gap-free SDC30 observations, spectral-semantic alignment of expert-annotated and spatially augmented samples, and rule-based spatial and temporal refinement. Independent classifiers were trained for each year using a common observation, feature, sample-construction, and modeling protocol, and the resulting annual record was used to derive pixel-level Cropping Frequency and 1 km Structural Evolution Indicators. Against independent stable-site FAST-Crop samples, GACED30 achieved an overall accuracy of 0.965 and an F 1 score of 0.844. Multitemporal assessments using GLAD Cropland and LUCAS reference samples showed higher recall and F 1 scores than GLC_FCS30D for both crop gain and crop loss, although the absolute transition scores remained modest. In a matched regional assessment in China, GACED30 achieved OA and F1 scores of 0.946 and 0.840, respectively, showing performance comparable with CACD. At the national scale, GACED30 agreed closely with definition-reconciled FAOSTAT statistics ( R 2 : 0.95; area-weighted direction match rate: 83.1 %). The sample-adjusted global cropland area was estimated at 1488.5 Mha in 2024, approximately 30.0 Mha higher than in 2000. Persistent expansion was concentrated in parts of Africa and South America, whereas stability and reduction were more widespread across much of the Global North. GACED30 provides a harmonized baseline for monitoring global cropland-extent dynamics and is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18199675 (Chen et al., 2026).

articles.title: META4.0: a new global mesoscale eddy  network atlas derived from altimetry
articles.abstract: This study introduces the new global Mesoscale Eddy Trajectory Atlases, META4.0 available in an AVISO repository at https://doi.org/10.24400/527896/a01-2026.001 (CLS and CNES, 2026). META4.0 provides eddy detections, trajectories, and interaction networks derived from satellite altimetry. Eddy detection relies on the pyeddytracker (PET) algorithm (Mason et al., 2014), further optimized by Pegliasco et al. (2022), and represents a substantial improvement over the previous META3.2 product (SSALTO/DUACS, distributed by AVISO+ with CNES support). The main advance of META4.0 is the explicit identification of eddy merging and splitting events. By combining grouping, which links detections across consecutive days, and segmentation, which tracks continuity through interaction events, trajectories are organized into networks of interconnected eddies. This network-based representation complements the single-trajectory view of eddy life cycles by explicitly accounting for eddy interactions. The paper presents both diagnostic tools designed to explore individual eddy networks (e.g., timelines, spatial trajectories, and eddy properties such as effective radius or shape error) and the results of a global statistical analysis over more than three decades. These tools and analyses offer new diagnostics for investigating network properties, eddy lifetimes, and the spatial and temporal distribution of merging and splitting events of the META4.0 atlas. Clustering analyses reveal recurrent interaction patterns and identify regions where eddy networks are particularly active. An independent dataset of surface chlorophyll concentration is used for qualitative validation of selected events. Finally, Lagrangian advection of synthetic particles highlights coherent forward and backward transport signatures associated with interaction events, providing a physical validation of the reconstructed networks. Overall, META4.0 offers a novel and physically consistent framework to characterize mesoscale eddy interactions and to better understand their role in shaping ocean dynamics.

articles.title: The FunAqua dataset of global fungal biodiversity in aquatic ecosystems
articles.abstract: Abstract Advances in high-throughput DNA sequencing technologies have accelerated research on aquatic microorganisms, their diversity, and ecological functions. This has also significantly advanced research on fungi that shape aquatic ecosystems and food webs. Here, we present the FunAqua dataset, which describes global fungal biodiversity in aquatic ecosystems based on eukaryotic long-read metabarcoding data from 1,076 sediment and 1,299 filtered water samples collected across 1,452 sampling sites in 87 countries. We targeted the internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region. In total, 50,152 fungal OTUs were recorded. The sequencing data is accompanied by comprehensive sample metadata, including physicochemical data of water and sediments. The FunAqua dataset provides a new resource for analysing and better understanding the biodiversity of fungi in different types of aquatic habitats across biogeographical regions. The dataset described in this data paper will be periodically updated with additional metabarcoding data.

articles.title: ACEL-Eval: A Benchmark Dataset for End-to-end Entity Linking in Classical Chinese
articles.abstract: As premodern texts become increasingly accessible in digital form, a major obstacle to their computational analysis is the lack of structured resources for identifying and normalizing historical entities. This challenge is especially evident in Classical Chinese, where standardized benchmarks for end-to-end entity linking remain limited. To address this need, we present ACEL-Eval, a benchmark dataset for evaluating entity linking in Classical Chinese. ACEL-Eval is derived from the Shiji and covers six entity categories that frequently occur in classical historical writing: person , location , state , official title , book , and time . The dataset supports end-to-end entity linking by combining named entity recognition over six entity categories with entity disambiguation for person mentions. To facilitate person referent normalization, we provide a person-oriented knowledge base containing core attributes such as personal names, aliases, and state affiliation. We conduct baseline experiments on the two target tasks to validate dataset usability and to establish reproducible reference results for future comparison. ACEL-Eval is designed to serve as a benchmark resource for Classical Chinese entity linking and as a reference for related computational studies of premodern Chinese historical texts.

articles.title: CCF Database: A Machine-Learning-Annotated Corpus of 283,964 Canadian Climate Articles (1978–2026)
articles.abstract: Abstract News media shape how societies perceive and respond to climate change, yet fine-grained analysis remains hindered by fragmented corpora and ad hoc coding schemes. The Canadian Climate Framing (CCF) database answers both with a large-scale bilingual annotated corpus and a generalizable annotation framework. It covers 283,964 climate-related articles from 22 Canadian news outlets (1978–2026), processed into 9,908,776 two-sentence units (83.4% English, 16.6% French). Each unit carries 65 hierarchical binary annotations spanning eight main frames, actors, events, solutions, tone, geography, and urgency, produced by 128 BERT and CamemBERT classifiers trained on 4,000+ expert-coded sentences. Against a 1,000-sentence gold standard double-coded by an independent annotator (Cohen’s κ = 0.596, Krippendorff’s α = 0.698, Gwet’s AC1  = 0.894), the classifiers reach a pooled macro F 1 of 0.866 (mean per-category macro F 1 = 0.773), and every category carries an A/B/C reliability tier. The database—sentence-level annotations, per-article aggregations, and 10,192,740 BAAI/bge-m3 embeddings in six relational tables—is openly released on Zenodo (CC-BY 4.0) as a PostgreSQL edition and an Apache Parquet mirror, refreshed roughly every six months by the CCF Observatory.

articles.title: Italian Fluvial Sediment Transport Database: a comprehensive hub for archiving and analyzing hydrological data
articles.abstract: Fluvial sediment transport plays a key role in geomorphological and hydrological processes, influencing river morphology, watershed and coastal sediment balances, and the environmental response to climatic and anthropogenic changes. In Italy, the availability of homogeneous and long-term data is strongly limited due to the discontinuity of monitoring activities and the fragmentation of existing sources. This study presents the development of a relational database and web application specifically designed for the collection, storage, and consultation of sediment transport data, aimed at integrating and enhancing heterogeneous datasets from both historical and contemporary monitoring networks: the Italian Fluvial Sediment Transport Database (ITASED). The database architecture, developed in PostgreSQL with the PostGIS extension, enables a direct link between observational data and their associated geographical, instrumental, and methodological metadata, ensuring traceability, interoperability, and the possibility to perform multi-temporal analyses. The web interface, built using open-source technologies, allows controlled data entry and interactive data exploration through maps, tables, and export functions. Analysis of the archived datasets highlights strong instrumental, temporal, and spatial heterogeneity: some physical-chemical parameters (e.g., pH and electrical conductivity) show standardized measurement protocols, whereas sediment transport variables exhibit high methodological variability. Time series range from sub-daily to annual observations, with denser coverage in northern Italian basins (e.g., Po, Adige, Piave, Tagliamento) since 1924. Despite these inconsistencies, integration within a unified relational framework enhances the value of a largely underused data heritage. The experience gained through this project enabled the identification of both the limitations and the potential of Italy's sediment monitoring system, providing operational guidance for methodological standardization, metadata improvement, and data harmonization at the national scale. The ITASED represents a concrete step toward establishing a shared sedimentological archive that supports scientific research, environmental management, and sustainable river basin planning. The dataset is publicly available on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18799025 (Luppichini et al., 2026).

articles.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the model organism Lumbriculus variegatus (Lumbriculidae: Clitellata)
articles.abstract: Aquatic oligochaetes (~10% of annelids) are important of pollutant toxicity assessment but lack genomic resources. We report the first chromosome level genome of Lumbriculus variegatus (a model organism for toxicity accumulation experiment) by using long-read sequencing data, short-read sequencing data, Hi-C, and RNA-seq. The 1.15 Gb assembly has contig N50 2.01 Mb, with 98.98% sequences anchored onto 17 chromosomes (scaffold N50 67.05 Mb), and high completeness (BUSCO 97.0%, a short-read mapping rate 99.49%, and a long-read mapping rate 98.94%). The QV values based on short- and long-reads were 57.45 and 61.21. Repetitive elements comprise 56.27% with LINEs accounting for 17.21%. We annotated 24,754 protein-coding genes with a BUSCO of 97.3% (96.56% functionally assigned) and 16,288 non-coding RNAs. This genome provides a crucial resource for studying cryptic speciation, genome evolution, adaptation, and toxicological mechanisms in annelids.

articles.title: CTX-UXO: Contextual visual dataset for localisation, classification and identification of unexploded ordnance
articles.abstract: Unexploded Ordnances (UXOs) are explosive weapons that failed to detonate during deployment, posing significant threats to civilian safety and post-conflict recovery. The Contextual Vision for Unexploded Ordnances (CTX-UXO) dataset addresses this challenge by providing 3520 high-resolution RGB images, median size 2124 px square, containing UXOs collected over four years across all seasons and weather conditions. The dataset encompasses 15 449 annotated instances labeled as UXOs, with twelve subcategories for identification tasks, in which mortar bombs, projectiles and grenades constitute the predominant classes, supporting systems research and development in UXO classification, detection, instance segmentation and related applications, and providing multiple labelling formats such as YOLO and COCO. For the detection task including binary classification, an end-to-end solution for training, validation and testing is available as a reference by presenting a neural network optimized for edge deployment, Faster-RCNN with MobileNet V3 backbone, deployed for real-time inference with reduced costs on Nvidia Jetson Orin, achieving up to 23 frames per second with 62.18% Ap50 for UXO localisation and binary classification.

articles.title: Global monthly diurnal temperature cycle parameters over land at 0.1° resolution for 1990–2024
articles.abstract: We describe a global gridded dataset of monthly climatological diurnal temperature cycle parameters over land at 0.1° resolution for 1990–2024. Using hourly 2 m air temperature from ERA5-Land, we fitted a dual-harmonic model to the multi-year mean hourly climatology for each eligible ERA5-Land grid cell and calendar month. The archive stores monthly mean temperature, the amplitudes and phase parameters of the 24 h and 12 h harmonics, fitted diurnal temperature range, fitted hours of daily minimum and maximum temperature, and quality-control diagnostics. Together these variables provide a compact description of local diurnal temperature shape that can be used for hourly reconstruction, temporal disaggregation, and gap filling when only daily summaries or sparse intra-day observations are available. Technical validation against ERA5-Land and NOAA hourly station observations shows that the parameterised diurnal template reproduces the main amplitude and timing structure across most land regions. In the full 2015–2020 NOAA evaluation, supplying observed daily range in addition to daily mean reduced pooled hourly RMSE from 2.24 to 1.94 °C. Under strict anchor-only held-out evaluation, fixed 12 UTC one-point and clipped fixed 00/12 UTC two-point reconstruction achieved pooled RMSE values of 3.045 and 2.976 °C, respectively. The dataset is publicly available through Zenodo and provides a compact, globally consistent prior for reconstructing sub-daily temperature variation from daily summaries or sparse observations.

articles.title: A high-resolution global flood susceptibility dataset derived from multi-source earth observation and geospatial data
articles.abstract: Abstract Floods are among the most damaging disasters worldwide, necessitating high-resolution modeling of where terrain and environmental conditions predispose societies to flooding. While geospatial data are invaluable for flood susceptibility mapping, comprehensive and globally consistent datasets remain scarce. We present the Global Flood Susceptibility Map (GFSM v1), a globally harmonized 30 m flood susceptibility dataset produced by incorporating multi-source flood conditioning factors accounting for topographic, hydrological, meteorological, and anthropogenic characteristics within a machine learning framework. A gradient-boosted tree model was trained on ~17,000 curated grid tiles with ~30.45 million training samples, using a global flood inundation dataset as training labels and nine conditioning factors (elevation, slope, aspect, wetness index, vegetation index, height above nearest drainage, water/roads proximity, and rainfall frequency). The model was deployed based on geopolitical and climate strata (units n = 192) to generate global pixel-level susceptibility. Rigorous cross-validation indicates strong model predictive accuracy (median area-under-curve ~0.95), and the output captures localized flood-prone regions worldwide. GFSM v1 offers a global open-source, high-resolution resource to support informed flood risk management, particularly in data-sparse regions.

articles.title: Vineyard RGB-D, LiDAR and GNSS/RTK datasets for grapevine segmentation and localisation to enable autonomous robotic pruning
articles.abstract: Agricultural robotics is becoming increasingly relevant for executing arduous tasks where human labour is scarce. Grapevine pruning is a seasonal task that, when performed manually, requires a worker to perform selective cutting of the grapevine canes. For a robot to conduct this type of task autonomously, it needs to navigate the vineyard rows without colliding with the grapevines, as well as retain information regarding each grapevine to perform the operation. This work presents datasets collected in a vineyard, comprising RGB and depth images, LiDAR and GNSS/RTK data, acquired using both a handheld device and a mobile robot. Furthermore, 494 RGB images obtained from the handheld device recordings were annotated with segmentation masks in YOLO format. The datasets support the development and evaluation of computer vision, localisation, mapping and sensor fusion algorithms for autonomous robots. Technical validation demonstrates the consistency and usability of the annotated data for training deep learning models.

articles.title: A multisensor dataset of energy use and activity in Dutch social housing
articles.abstract: Abstract This research introduces the HOMESENSE dataset, comprising indoor environmental quality data from 11 social-rental dwellings in Limburg, the Netherlands, together with available electricity and gas measurements over 366 consecutive local calendar days ending in November 2025. Released files use a common 10-minute publication grid rather than uniform native resolution. This interval is native to the principal room-environment and thermostatic-valve streams, supports aggregation of faster streams, and aligns slower and event-driven streams using documented bounded-gap rules. Each measurement is paired with a quality-control (QC) field distinguishing , , , and  values. The release also includes Maastricht weather records. Data are provided as comma-separated value (CSV) files with source code and Jupyter notebooks for reproducible loading, analysis, and release processing. The dataset supports research on activity patterns, heating control, indoor thermal conditions, low-frequency load attribution, and coarse-resolution non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) using appliance-level measurements alongside whole-dwelling grid exchange.

articles.title: AGPC: an Annual 500 m Gridded Population (1990–2020) for China incorporating 3D building volume dynamics
articles.abstract: Gridded population datasets with long-term temporal coverage and fine spatial resolution are essential for earth system modelling, urban studies, and disaster risk assessment. However, existing population products often fail to adequately represent population distribution in vertically developed urban environments. This paper presents the AGPC dataset, a temporally consistent gridded population dataset for China at 500 m spatial resolution covering the period 1990–2020. AGPC was generated using a machine-learning-based dasymetric mapping framework, integrating multi-source covariates including three-dimensional (3D) building volume, building function, and other socioeconomic variables. County-level census data were used for model calibration, while annual provincial population totals from official statistical yearbooks were applied as constraints to ensure temporal consistency. The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis confirms the dominant roles of commercial activity intensity and 3D building volume in shaping fine-scale population distribution and highlights the added value of vertical and functional information beyond conventional two-dimensional (2D) indicators. Population estimates were produced annually and aggregated to multiple administrative scales for validation. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate the reliability and accuracy of the dataset across spatial and temporal scales. At the county level, AGPC shows strong agreement with census data, with correlation coefficients R greater than 0.89 and relative RMSE values below 1 % on the independent validation sets for the baseline years 2010 and 2020. At finer scales, grid-level population estimates aggregated to the township level exhibit high consistency with independent census data with R greater than 0.90, indicating satisfactory capability in capturing finer-scale spatial heterogeneity in population distribution. Multi-temporal validation at the city level for seven time points between 1990 and 2020 yields correlation coefficients ranging from 0.79 to 0.99, indicating stable temporal performance. Comparisons with existing global and regional population datasets show that AGPC better captures population patterns in high-density and vertically developed urban areas, avoiding the density saturation effects commonly observed in 2D products. The AGPC dataset provides a robust and scalable population data resource for long-term socioeconomic and environmental analyses in China, and it is available at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31338352 (Xu et al., 2026).

articles.title: Extending daily river discharge records across China using satellite-derived river widths
articles.abstract: Long-term monitoring of global river discharge has been hindered by the uneven distribution of gauging stations and limited data accessibility, a challenge that is particularly acute in China. Although China contains one of the world's densest river networks, high-frequency in situ discharge observations remain largely unavailable in the international public domain. To address this gap, we compiled daily discharge records from 1196 gauges across China, comprising approximately 2.33 ×10 6 observations – 39 times as many gauges as are currently available for the region in the Global Runoff Data Centre (GRDC). Leveraging this unprecedented collection of in situ discharge records, along with river width time series derived from Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery and gauge-specific hydraulic geometry relationships, we reconstructed and extended daily river discharge observations for 310 gauges from 1990 to 2024, resulting in the China Daily River Discharge Records (CDR 2 ) dataset. Compared with existing global satellite-derived discharge products, CDR 2 expands the number of available gauges in China by more than fivefold while delivering substantially improved performance, achieving a median Kling–Gupta efficiency of 0.66 during validation. Moreover, uncertainties propagated from the fitted hydraulic geometry parameters remain low, with a median relative uncertainty of only 11.89 % in the reconstructed discharge estimates. Sensitivity analyses further indicate that discharge estimation accuracy increases markedly with greater river width variability and stronger hydraulic sensitivity. Trend analysis reveals that nearly 65 % of gauges exhibit declining discharge over 1990–2024, with a median relative trend of −0.21 % yr −1 , most pronounced in the Haihe, Liaohe, Yellow River, and middle Yangtze River basins. As the most extensive satellite-derived, gauge-constrained river discharge dataset currently available for China at daily resolution, CDR 2 bridges a critical geographic gap in global river monitoring and provides a valuable benchmark for future discharge estimation, hydrological research, water resources management, and the calibration and evaluation of satellite missions. The CDR 2 dataset is publicly available on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22231453 (Wang and Li, 2026).

articles.title: Multivariate Electrical Measurements of Household Appliances with Synchronized Zone Occupancy Tracking
articles.abstract: Home energy management systems can reduce electricity consumption and operating costs, leading to environmental benefits. Their effective operation relies on accurate information about real-time and long-term appliance usage, which can be obtained via nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM). Progress in NILM, including fair benchmarking of algorithms, critically depends on well-documented, high-quality datasets. Here, we describe a multimodal dataset comprising synchronized recordings of 12 commonly used household appliances and radar-based zone occupancy data tracking occupants’ presence across zones during appliance operation. The dataset provides voltage and current waveforms sampled at 20 kS/s, harmonic components up to the 50th order, power measurements at 200 ms resolution, and radar-derived zone occupancy data at 1 s resolution. By combining rich electrical measurements with radar-based contextual information, the dataset supports research on multimodal NILM, activity-aware disaggregation, and context-informed energy management. This publicly available dataset combines a broad set of electrical features with synchronized radar-based zone occupancy context.

articles.title: A dataset of biomass burning emissions from multiple sources in China covering 1980 to 2024
articles.abstract: Biomass burning (BB) is an important source of atmospheric carbonaceous aerosols and trace gases, exerting significant impacts on air quality, climate, and human health. However, a nationwide, long-term, and integrated BB emission dataset for China remains limited. Here, we construct a monthly gridded BB inventory for China covering 1980–2024. The dataset quantifies emissions of black carbon (BC), organic carbon (OC), sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ), carbon monoxide (CO), and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from seven source categories, including forest fires, shrub fires, grassland fires, in-field straw burning, domestic straw burning, firewood burning, and livestock-manure burning. Emissions from domestic BB and in-field straw burning are reconstructed for 1980–2024 and are spatially allocated using rural-residential population and cropland proxies, respectively. Forest, shrub, and grassland fire emissions are estimated from satellite observations for 2001–2024 and aggregated with the other sources to a common 1 km grid. Parameter and reconstruction uncertainties are quantified using Monte Carlo and bootstrap methods, while key structural assumptions are evaluated through sensitivity analyses. Comparisons with published studies and global fire-emission inventories show broadly consistent magnitudes and temporal variations. The dataset supports analyses of long-term emission trends, source attribution, atmospheric modelling, and environmental assessment.

articles.title: High-resolution dataset of core needle prostate biopsies with expert pathologist annotations
articles.abstract: Abstract We present an expert-labelled image dataset designed to support automated analysis of image-guided prostate core needle biopsies (CNBs) in the context of prostate cancer diagnosis. The dataset includes 37 whole slide images (WSIs), corresponding to 60 CNBs stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), from 32 patients. The dataset contains 15480 manual expert annotations, covering benign glands, tumor, stromal tissue, adipose tissue, nerves, nerve ganglia, blood vessels, muscle, and inflammatory cells. Additional recorded features include stromal retractions, normal and abnormal glandular secretions, and tissue or digital image artifacts. These annotations represent the normal findings that pathologists encounter in routine diagnosis. The annotations were performed by two experienced uropathologists with final labels determined by consensus; immunohistochemical techniques were used as guidance. This dataset provides a foundation for training and benchmarking machine learning models for prostate biopsy assessment and is openly available to facilitate reproducibility and further research.

articles.title: A Four-Decade Dataset of Cotton Phenological Dynamics from the Agrometeorological Network in Xinjiang of China
articles.abstract: This study presents a four-decade dataset (1981–2024) of cotton phenological dynamics, derived from 37 agrometeorological stations across China’s primary cotton production zone, the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region (hereinafter referred to as Xinjiang). The dataset comprises a total 22,274 records (589 MB (uncompressed); 364 MB (compressed)) documenting 9 key phenological periods—sowing, emergence, three-leaf, five-leaf, squaring, flowering, boll crack, open boll, and physiological maturity—and 5 derived growth phases. It integrates historical paper-based records with modern electronic archives, ensuring continuity and reliability through a multi-tiered quality control process. Advanced analytical methods, including kernel density estimation and univariate linear regression, were employed to characterize spatial distributions, interannual variability, and long-term trends in phenology. Application of these methods revealed a significant advancing trend in most phenological stages across the region, highlighting a clear response of cotton growth to climate change. This dataset offers a robust resource for investigating crop-climate interactions, validating process-based models, and informing climate adaptation strategies in arid and semi-arid agricultural systems. Its high spatial and temporal resolution supports diverse applications in agronomy, ecology, climatology, and agricultural policymaking. The dataset is publicly accessible via the Science Data Bank, providing a valuable benchmark for future studies on cotton phenology and sustainable crop management under changing climatic conditions.

articles.title: Beyond built-up land: Mapping complete settlement footprint in China from 1990 to 2020 with Landsat imagery
articles.abstract: Abstract Accurate mapping of human settlements is vital for understanding urbanization, human-environment interactions, and sustainable development. Existing medium-resolution products often underestimate the real spatial extent of settlements by focusing solely on built-up cores. Here, we present the China Settlement Footprint 1990–2020 (CSF30) dataset, a nationwide product depicting complete human settlement footprints from Landsat imagery at five-year intervals. CSF30 was generated using an Entity-Based Image Analysis framework integrated with a deep learning architecture. To ensure spatio-temporal generalizability and boundary accuracy, the model was trained via a two-stage strategy utilizing a built-up area dataset and a newly annotated settlement footprint dataset. Comprehensive validation demonstrates that CSF30 achieves a mean F1-score of 0.91 across the 30-year period, showing distinct advantages in representing rural and peri-urban areas compared to existing products. CSF30 provides a critical, high-quality baseline for diverse applications, including investigating settlement trajectories, assessing ecological and environmental impacts, and monitoring progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

articles.title: SRAD: A Multibeam Acoustic Dataset for Submerged Reef Detection in a Laboratory-Recreated Seafloor Environment
articles.abstract: Abstract Multibeam sonar is an important sensing modality for submerged reef detection, with potential applications in ROV operations, navigation safety, and offshore engineering. However, dedicated public acoustic datasets with object-level annotations for submerged reef or reef-like target detection remain limited, restricting the development and evaluation of relevant algorithms. To address this gap, we present SRAD, a multibeam acoustic dataset for submerged reef detection in a laboratory-recreated seafloor environment. The dataset contains more than 3,650 8-bit grayscale sonar images with corresponding ground-truth bounding-box annotations, together with native Oculus sonar logs and supporting data-processing tools. Data were collected in a controlled basin within a large-scale ocean engineering laboratory, where seafloor-related materials, including sand, gravel, natural rock reefs, algal reef materials, shell reefs, and simulated coral structures, were physically arranged to recreate a laboratory seafloor environment. To improve data consistency, an Oculus M750d multibeam sonar mounted on an ROV was used under consistent acquisition settings, and the ground-truth annotations were subjected to expert review and additional consistency checks. The resulting dataset provides labeled multibeam sonar images for the development, validation, and testing of submerged reef detection methods under controlled laboratory conditions, while the native Oculus sonar records and supporting processing tools enable further acoustic-data analysis and reuse.

articles.title: A near telomere-to-telomere genome assembly of the freshwater pearl mussel Margaritifera dahurica
articles.abstract: Margaritifera dahurica (Middendorff, 1850) is an ecologically and evolutionarily significant freshwater pearl mussel species belonging to the ancient family Margaritiferidae. Despite its critical role as a bio-indicator for ecosystem health, the lack of a high-quality reference genome has hindered research into its complex life cycle and conservation biology. Here, we present a near-complete telomere-to-telomere (near-T2T) genome assembly of M. dahurica generated by integrating high-depth PacBio HiFi (~90×), Nanopore ultra-long (~37×), and Hi-C data (~113×). The final assembly spans 2.86 Gb across 19 pseudo-chromosomes, with a scaffold N50 of 152.68 Mb and a contig N50 of 138.90 Mb. The successful identification of telomeric repeats at multiple chromosome ends confirms the assembly’s near-completeness. Genome annotation identified 1.98 Gb of repetitive elements (69.11% of the genome) and predicted 36,112 protein-coding genes, of which 93.95% were functionally assigned. Technical validation demonstrated high assembly quality, with a BUSCO completeness score of 98.55% and high consensus quality (QV) values. This near-T2T genome provides a foundational genetic resource for investigating the evolutionary history, specialized parasitic mechanisms, and conservation strategies of this endangered bivalve.

articles.title: Small RNA sequencing dataset from muscle, gills and skin of Orestias ascotanensis obtained during winter and summer seasons
articles.abstract: Orestias ascotanensis is an endemic teleost inhabiting the spring-fed streams of the Ascotán salt pan (~3,700 m a.s.l.), in the Chilean Altiplano. This environment is characterized by variable water chemistry and high-altitude stressors, including hypoxia and ultraviolet radiation. Due to these unique ecological pressures, O. ascotanensis represents a valuable model system for studying molecular mechanisms of environmental adaptation. Among gene regulatory layers, microRNAs play a central role in fine-tuning gene expression by forming complex regulatory networks with mRNAs and long non-coding RNAs, ultimately shaping phenotypic responses to environmental change. This dataset provides small RNA expression profiles from three tissues of O. ascotanensis , to support characterization of its tissue-specific microRNA repertoire and seasonal expression patterns. The dataset comprises 42 sequencing libraries generated from gills, skin, and skeletal muscle of 14 wild adult individuals captured during winter (n = 7) and summer (n = 7). Raw sequencing data are accompanied by sample metadata and technical validation metrics to support data reuse and integrative analyses with existing genomic and transcriptomic resources.

articles.title: Multi-omic landscape of a porcine SCID model with a single-codon RAG2 deletion
articles.abstract: Severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) research requires models that closely mimic human physiology. This study presents a comprehensive multi-omics dataset from a porcine model of RAG2bKO SCID, characterized by minimal genetic editing and extended survival. We generated a precise in-frame single-amino-acid deletion (p.His109del) in RAG2 using transcription activator-like effector nuclease (TALEN)-mediated editing. The dataset includes: (1) genomic sequencing data confirming the mutation and computational predictions of its structural impact on the RAG2 protein; (2) flow cytometry data quantifying the near-complete absence of mature adaptive lymphocytes; (3) histopathological images demonstrating thymic aplasia and splenic hypoplasia; (4) RNA-seq transcriptomic profiles from the thymus, spleen, and lymph nodes; and (5) ChIP-seq data for H3K4me3 histone modifications. This multi-layered and comprehensively characterised dataset provides a resource for studying SCID pathophysiology, comparative immunology, and benchmarking of therapeutic interventions in physiologically relevant large-animal models.

articles.title: An observation-based daily gridded precipitation dataset for forecast verification
articles.abstract: As numerous artificial intelligence (AI)-based weather forecasting models are trained by climate reanalysis, there is an urgent need for independent observation-based datasets for forecast verification. Mainly based on the Global Historical Climatology Network (GHCN), this paper develops the GHCN daily gridded precipitation (GHCNdgp) dataset, covering the period from 2020 to 2025. Specifically, two daily station-based observation datasets–GHCN daily and Global Surface Summary of the Day–and three subdaily datasets–GHCN hourly, Integrated Surface Database and Integrated Global Land surface Dataset–are integrated to enhance global station density and spatial coverage. The spatiotemporal consistency checks are combined with integrity and reporting time checks to identify anomalous observations and infer stations’ reporting times. Furthermore, the GHCNdgp is compared against three existing precipitation products using Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC), i.e., the Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for Global Precipitation Measurement (IMERG) V07 Late, the Multi-Source Weighted-Ensemble Precipitation (MSWEP) V2.8 and the Global Precipitation Climatology Centre (GPCC) First Guess Daily product. The results show that more than 90% of the anomalous observations come from identical values and duplicate sequences. The median PCC for stations with daily accumulation periods shifted by 24 hours is generally below 0.25. The quality control checks improve the median PCC from 0.46 to 0.62 under the IMERG, from 0.54 to 0.71 under the MSWEP and from 0.33 to 0.47 under the GPCC. These findings indicate that the GHCNdgp dataset effectively mitigates mismatches in observation reporting times and aligns with the grid resolution of 0.25° × 0.25° common in AI weather forecasts. This dataset is publicly available on Zenodo in the Network Common Data Form format, providing essential ground-truth precipitation observations specifically for benchmarking AI weather forecasts.

articles.title: Improving global and regional ocean heat content by consistently combining GRACE gravity, satellite altimetry and Argo profile observations in a joint inversion framework
articles.abstract: The current energy imbalance at the top of atmosphere and corresponding heating of the Earth system is the main driver of steric sea level change through ocean heat uptake (OHU). A global constant heat capacity factor is commonly applied to retrieve ocean heat content (OHC) from observed ocean-average steric sea level. We propose an extension to this methodology, which focuses on the leading modes of steric variability, which are derived from an ocean model and fitted to GRACE gravity, satellite altimetry and in situ Argo observations within a joint inversion framework. These modes are utilized to obtain data driven OHC estimates by establishing a mapping between modeled OHC and steric sea level, and rescaling each mode individually based on observed steric sea level change. On global scales for the period January 2005 till December 2024, our OHU results (0.62 W m −2 ) agree well with a variety of published datasets from in situ Argo data, model reanalyses and space-geodetic approaches as well as independent estimates from the CERES project. At basin scales, we demonstrate the global OHU to be driven mainly by warming of the Pacific Ocean (0.23 W m −2 ), followed by contributions from the Indian (0.20 W m −2 ) and Atlantic (0.13 W m −2 ) oceans. Minor contributions are found from the Arctic Ocean (0.01 W m −2 ), the Southern Ocean (0.02 W m −2 ) and the residual ocean (0.03 W m −2 ). Our results also indicate a shift from dominant heating in the Indian Ocean driven by heat transport from the Pacific Ocean, e.g. found during 2005–2015, towards a more evenly distributed global ocean heat budget. Monthly gridded OHC data from our Grace, Altimetry and Argo Mode Rescaling (GAAMR) method together with corresponding error estimates is available from https://doi.org/10.1594/PANGAEA.994058 (Uebbing and Kusche, 2026).

articles.title: A random forest isoscape model of bioavailable Sr for South America: a focus on southern Brazil
articles.abstract: In recent years, advances in machine learning have greatly improved the generation of maps showing the geographic distribution of isotope ratios (isoscapes), which have become essential tools for environmental, mobility and provenance studies in both modern and archaeological contexts. Among the various isotopic systems employed, strontium (Sr) is particularly useful because its 87 Sr / 86 Sr ratio in the environment is largely controlled by the underlying geology through the composition of local soils and rocks. In this work, we present a new dataset of bioavailable 87 Sr / 86 Sr ratios derived from n =233 plant samples collected across southern Brazil, covering the states of Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul (ca. 370 000 km 2 ). The measured ratios span from 0.70521 to 0.76039 and capture the bioavailable Sr isotope signatures over all major geological units in the region. We combined these new data with an extensive compilation of published bioavailable Sr measurements from across South America (including plants, fauna, ancient human remains, shells, snails, lichens, water and soils) to construct three random forest Sr isoscapes using different subsets of the combined dataset at the regional and continental scales. The first model incorporates the entire dataset (“All” dataset, n = 883 sites), the second is based on plant + fauna + lichen + human ( n = 661 sites) and the third is limited to plant + lichen samples ( n = 531 sites). Among the three models, the full dataset model shows lower predictive power, while the plant + fauna + lichen + human and the plant + lichen models yield better results, with similar RMSE (0.0049 and 0.0054) and R 2 values (ca. 0.76). Compared to existing Sr isoscapes of South America, our models significantly enhance both spatial coverage and resolution of bioavailable Sr predictions, particularly in southern Brazil. The new bioavailable Sr isotope dataset from Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul states is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17988601 (Scaggion et al., 2025a) and the compiled literature dataset is reported as supplementary material.

articles.title: The Ostrya virginiana (Mill.) K. Koch [Betulaceae] genome: a chromosome-level assembly for a foundational understory tree in eastern North America
articles.abstract: Ironwood ( Ostrya virginiana (Mill.) K. Koch) is an ecologically important tree species in temperate forests and holds significant horticultural and economic value. Despite its importance and the recent emergence of a threatening foliar rust disease, genomic resources for this species have been largely lacking. To address this gap, we present a high-quality, haplotype-phased, chromosome-level diploid genome assembly using a combination of PacBio HiFi long reads and Hi-C scaffolding. The finalized assembly successfully resolves into 8 pseudo-chromosomes per haplotype, with a total size of approximately 325 Mb each and an estimated heterozygosity rate of 1.15–1.18%. Genome annotation identified 45.71% and 45.57% repetitive content, along with 21,978 and 22,050 protein-coding genes in haplotype 1 and haplotype 2, respectively. Furthermore, BUSCO assessments indicated exceptional assembly quality, with approximately 99% completeness for the genome assemblies and 90% completeness for the predicted protein-coding gene sets. Functional characterization, assessed through homology-based assignments against the SwissProt, Pfam, and Gene Ontology (GO) databases, demonstrated that 92% of predicted proteins received at least one functional annotation. This robust reference genome provides a vital foundational resource for future research in forest ecology, phylogenomics, and host-pathogen interactions.

articles.title: The Dresden Dataset for 4D Reconstruction of Non-Rigid Abdominal Surgical Scenes
articles.abstract: Abstract The D4D Dataset provides paired endoscopic video and high-quality structured-light geometry for evaluating 3D reconstruction of deforming abdominal soft tissue in realistic surgical conditions. Data were acquired from six porcine cadavers using a da Vinci Xi stereo endoscope and a Zivid structured-light camera, registered via optical tracking and manually curated iterative alignment methods. Three session types (whole deformations, incremental deformations, and moved-camera sessions) probe algorithm robustness to non-rigid motion, deformation magnitude, and out-of-view updates. Each clip provides rectified stereo images, per-frame instrument masks, stereo depth, start/end structured-light point clouds, curated camera poses and camera intrinsics. In postprocessing, ICP and semi-automatic registration techniques are used to register data, and instrument masks are created. The dataset enables quantitative geometric evaluation in both visible and occluded regions, alongside photometric view-synthesis baselines. Comprising over 300,000 frames and 369 point clouds across 98 curated sessions, this resource can serve as a comprehensive benchmark for developing and evaluating non-rigid SLAM, 4D reconstruction, and depth estimation methods.

articles.title: Telomere-to-Telomere Genome Assembly and Graph-Based pan-genome Construction of Grifola frondosa (Maitake)
articles.abstract: Abstract Grifola frondosa , also known as the “Maitake,” is a large fungus with both edible and medicinal value. Through whole-genome sequencing, we newly assembled five high-quality genomes from 36.7 to 39.6 Mb in size, with the scaffold N50 lengths of 2.8–3.2 Mb, including one telomere-to-telomere assembly (HT01). Together with five publicly available genomes, we constructed the pan-genome of G. frondosa , which contains 17,874 protein-coding gene clusters. Among these, 47.41% were core, 5.9% soft-core, 27.92% dispensable, and 18.78% private gene clusters, respectively. Using the T2T genome as a reference, we identified 3,741 nonredundant structural variants (SVs) and constructed a reference-based graph-based pan-genome of 46.9 Mb and a reference-free graph-based pan-genome of 62.6 Mb, respectively. This comprehensive pan-genome resource will provide a useful resource for breeding and genomic studies of G. frondosa .

articles.title: AS-OCT dataset with anatomical structure segmentation and scleral spur localization in cataract and glaucoma
articles.abstract: Abstract Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography (AS-OCT) provides high-resolution, non-invasive visualization of the anterior eye and is widely used for clinical diagnosis and surgical planning. However, automated analysis of AS-OCT images remains limited by the lack of publicly available datasets with comprehensive anatomical annotations and disease labels. Here we present the AS-OCT Multi-Structure and Disease Classification Dataset (ASOCT-MSDC), a curated dataset designed for anatomical structure segmentation and disease classification. The dataset contains 1106 AS-OCT images from 1106 eyes of 627 individuals across four clinical categories: normal, glaucoma, cataract, and glaucoma-cataract comorbidity. Each image underwent stringent quality assessment, and three standardized image quality scores—eyelid obscuration, black-line anomaly, and central light artifact—are provided as metadata. Expert-validated annotations include segmentation masks for the anterior chamber, iris, lens, and nucleus, together with scleral spur localization points. By combining anatomical annotations, disease labels, and image quality metadata, ASOCT-MSDC supports research on anatomical segmentation, disease classification, and image quality assessment in anterior segment OCT images.

articles.title: A whole-genome resequencing dataset of Kecai yaks from China
articles.abstract: Endemic to the northeastern edge of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, the Kecai yak, a geographically distinct local yak population, serves as a useful resource for exploring the molecular mechanisms underlying high-altitude adaptation. In this study, we described a whole-genome resequencing dataset for Kecai yaks. Initially, 49 unrelated adult animals (25 males and 24 females) were sampled from Kecai Town, Xiahe County, Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Gansu, China, across elevations of 3200–3800 m. We generated roughly 3.09 TB of raw sequencing data, with an average sequencing depth of 20.11×. We mapped clean reads to the yak reference genome, yielding an average alignment rate of 99.09%. Strict variant filtering identified 23.41 million high-confidence single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). This genome-wide SNP dataset can support studies of the genetic origins and high-altitude adaptation of Kecai yaks and provide genomic evidence to aid the conservation and practical use of this local yak germplasm.

articles.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the mangrove-dwelling bivalve Enigmonia aenigmatica (Pectinoida: Anomiidae)
articles.abstract: Abstract Enigmonia aenigmatica is a unique mangrove-dwelling bivalve species with remarkable ecological and morphological adaptations, yet its genomic background has remained unexplored. In this study, we combined PacBio HiFi long reads, WGS short reads, Hi-C data, Oxford Nanopore long-read transcriptome sequencing, and Illumina short-read transcriptome sequencing to assemble and annotate a high-quality reference genome for E. aenigmatica . We obtained a chromosome-level genome assembly with a total genome size of 465.97 Mb, comprising 8 chromosomes. The assembly exhibits exceptional contiguity, with a scaffold N50 of 58.83 Mb. Comprehensive gene annotation identified 17,728 protein-coding genes. This chromosome-level genome of E. aenigmatica provides a valuable genomic resource for future studies on mangrove-associated bivalves, molluscan evolution, and ecological adaptation in intertidal environments.

articles.title: Chromosome-Level Genome Assembly of the Hybrid Grouper Epinephelus fuscoguttatus × Epinephelus lanceolatus
articles.abstract: We present a chromosome-level genome assembly for the hybrid grouper ( Epinephelus fuscoguttatus ♀ × Epinephelus lanceolatus ♂). PacBio HiFi sequencing generated 5,951,738 reads totaling 122.82 Gb, with a read N50 of 21.55 kb. The 1.12-Gb primary assembly comprised 89 contigs with a contig N50 of 45.74 Mb, of which 1.08 Gb was anchored to 24 chromosomes. Two phased companion assemblies, Haploid 1 and Haploid 2, each contained 24 chromosome-scale sequences and spanned 1.085 and 1.088 Gb, respectively. Because parental ancestry was not assigned, these labels do not indicate maternal or paternal origin. BUSCO analysis using the actinopterygii_odb10 dataset recovered 97.80% complete orthologs. Repetitive sequences accounted for 44.24% of the genome. We identified 28,310 protein-coding gene models with a combined gene span of 604.72 Mb. The corresponding all-isoform set contained 124,025 predicted protein sequences representing translated coding transcripts rather than additional gene loci. Functional annotation was conducted at the protein-sequence level, with 122,472, 80,031, 64,401, and 74,117 sequences annotated against NR, KOG, GO, and KEGG, respectively. The principal features of this resource are its chromosome-scale organization, high contiguity, high BUSCO completeness, and phased companion assemblies. Because no genome-wide comparison with parental species or other groupers was performed, these features should not be interpreted as hybrid-specific or evolutionarily distinctive. This assembly provides a reference for future ancestry-aware comparative genomics and molecular breeding in groupers.
articles.authors: Kianann Tan, Leong-Seng Lim, Julian Ransangan, Mohammad Tamrin Mohamad Lal, Annita Seok-Kian Yong, Uun Yanuhar, Kit Yue Kwan, Gang Wang, Fui Fui Ching, Xiaohui Cai

articles.title: Citizen science dataset of urban heat perception and environmental measurements in outdoor public spaces across climate-vulnerable neighborhoods in the Barcelona metropolitan area
articles.abstract: We present a dataset generated to investigate urban heat and thermal perception across five neighborhoods in the Barcelona metropolitan area. In collaboration with 14 non-academic partner organizations, we conducted a series of citizen science campaigns involving 439 residents as co-researchers engaged throughout all stages of the research process. Participants—residents of areas classified as highly or very highly climate-vulnerable—identified 210 public outdoor sites relevant to their daily lives. These locations were subsequently characterized using a range of spatial and environmental indicators pertinent to urban heat island effects, urban health, and climate resilience. Over the course of 48 thermal walks, participants carried portable, low-cost sensors that continuously recorded air temperature, relative humidity, and geolocation, resulting in 296 286 processed microclimatic data points. At pre-defined sites, individuals completed standardized surveys to report their Thermal Sensation Votes and Thermal Comfort Votes, yielding 5 169 self-reported entries. Sociodemographic data were also collected to further contextualize participants’ responses. The resulting dataset integrates objective environmental measurements with subjective perceptions of heat, enabling point-by-point analysis of thermal experience within the urban fabric. It offers a novel, multi-dimensional resource to support research on heat, thermal inequality, and the experiential dimensions of climate vulnerability, and is intended to inform evidence-based decision-making in urban planning, public health, and climate adaptation.

articles.title: The m6A epitranscriptomic landscape of Setaria viridis and the domesticated foxtail millet (S. italica)
articles.abstract: N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) is a pivotal epitranscriptomic modification that post-transcriptionally regulates RNA metabolism and contributes to plant growth and immune responses. However, the evolution and roles of m 6 A modifications in plant domestication remain largely unexplored. This study combined RNA-seq and MeRIP-seq data to compare m 6 A modifications profiles between foxtail millet ( Setaria italica , Yugu1) and its wild ancestor S. viridis (A10). Peak calling analysis identified 6,928 m 6 A peaks associated with 6,407 protein-coding genes in Yugu1 and 6,274 m 6 A peaks in 5,858 genes in A10, respectively. Comparative analysis revealed numerous differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially methylated peaks (DMPs), whose functions were elucidated by GO and KEGG enrichment analyses. Integration of DMPs paired with DEGs, we found 209 hyper-methylated peaks associated with upregulated transcription levels, and 90 hypo-methylated peaks associated with downregulated transcription levels. This dataset provides valuable resource for further investigating the roles of m 6 A modification in crop domestication.

articles.title: TCM4NSCLC: A real-world dataset and benchmark for Chinese-medicine reasoning on non-small-cell lung cancer
articles.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains one of the most burdensome malignancies worldwide. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) holds promise for stabilizing disease progression, alleviating symptoms, and improving quality of life. However, current evidence is predominantly derived from small-scale randomized controlled trials, which are inherently limited in capturing the complexity and longitudinal dynamics of pattern-based individualized care in real-world clinical settings. To address this gap, we present TCM4NSCLC—a standardized, computable, and shareable real-world dataset documenting TCM care for NSCLC. The dataset aggregates expert outpatient records from a senior TCM physician and comprises 3,790 structured cases with multiple visits. It encompasses demographic information, Western diagnoses and staging, pathology and laboratory tests, key imaging findings, clinical symptoms, tongue and pulse features, as well as original decoction prescriptions and Chinese Patent Medicines. We provide fine-grained annotations across ten named-entity categories, including diseases, drugs, investigations, tongue features, pulse signs, and symptoms. All data have undergone rigorous de-identification, denoising, deduplication, and quality control procedures. Multi-angle validation—including quality metrics, baseline modeling, and expert review—confirms the dataset’s internal consistency, usability, and clinical interpretability. TCM4NSCLC serves both as a digital repository of expert clinical knowledge and as a formalized knowledge representation that facilitates the integration of TCM into precision oncology. It supports (i) syndrome differentiation and prescription generation, (ii) real-world effectiveness assessment and subgroup discovery, and (iii) multimodal integrative decision-making and the development of intelligent clinical tools. The resource will be released with a unified schema, data dictionary, and usage guidelines to provide a reusable infrastructure for evidence-driven and intelligent TCM research in NSCLC.As a single-expert longitudinal corpus, TCM4NSCLC offers a uniquely coherent therapeutic philosophy and consistent clinical reasoning paradigm, providing a foundational resource for interpretable modeling while establishing a template for future multi-expert expansions.

articles.title: SPAMS10: an InSAR-derived soil motion parameter dataset to model relative peat surface elevation changes
articles.abstract: Peat subsidence poses a significant challenge to long-term land and environmental stability by increasing flood risk and producing greenhouse gas emissions. Field monitoring with extensometers reveals variability in relative surface elevation changes, which are then modeled using simple parameterization for the motion of soils (SPAMS). To extend the spatial scale of monitoring, Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) time series are used. InSAR-derived SPAMS parameters provide displacement models that can describe peat subsidence and dynamics with a set of parameters, namely four parameters for modeling and six variance-covariance terms for model uncertainties. We publish the SPAMS10 dataset, which refers to the descriptive displacement model SPAMS with ten parameters. The dataset also provides additional contextual information, such as soil code, at the parcel level, defined by the administrative boundary of an agricultural field. This dataset promotes data sharing among stakeholders, shifting products from InSAR-based relative elevation estimates to InSAR-derived displacement model parameters. These parameters enable the reconstruction of displacement models for peat subsidence analyses. The dataset is available through the 4TU.ResearchData repository: https://doi.org/10.4121/dfbe9109-d058-4a64-a5b4-1cc9d9a5f836 (Lumban-Gaol et al., 2025) and is distributed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license.

articles.title: Chinese Historical Epidemic Dataset
articles.abstract: Epidemics represent high-impact events within the spectrum of human catastrophes, and China preserves a rich record of such occurrences. However, standardized, spatially explicit datasets with long-term temporal coverage remain limited. This study presents Chinese Historical Epidemic Dataset (CHED), a spatiotemporal database of epidemic events in China from 1056 BCE to 1949 CE. Derived primarily from A Compendium of Chinese Epidemic Disaster Records over Three Millennia , the dataset contains 32,389 annually resolved records with county-level spatial granularity and six core variables: time, location, cause, effect, category, and response. This systematic design enables source traceability, multi-granular querying, and precise spatiotemporal localization. As one of the longest-term and most spatially detailed historical epidemic dataset for China available, CHED is designed to support research on the historical globalization of infectious diseases and the long-term evolution of environment–health interactions.

articles.title: A spatiotemporally harmonized dataset of utility-reported power outages and NWS VTEC weather warnings for the contiguous United States (2015–2024)
articles.abstract: Power grids across the United States are increasingly exposed to weather-related disruption, yet reproducible analyses are limited by differences in the spatial and temporal structure of outage and meteorological records. This Data Descriptor presents a harmonized, event-based archive linking county-level customer power-outage records from the U.S. Department of Energy EAGLE-I platform with National Weather Service watches, warnings and advisories encoded through the Valid Time Event Code system. The archive spans the contiguous United States from 2015 through 2024. The primary released file contains hourly indexed, positive processed outage observations that overlap at least one VTEC warning and include event identifiers, matched warning types, and source-record availability diagnostics. Companion files provide the consolidated warning archive, daily county-level EAGLE-I source-record availability and sensitivity summaries evaluating missing-record treatment, temporal aggregation, and recovery persistence. Technical validation quantifies the consequences of preprocessing assumptions and documents spatial, temporal and warning-matching consistency. The dataset supports reproducible analysis of spatiotemporal co-occurrence between reported power disruptions and operational weather warnings while explicitly retaining limitations associated with the underlying outage record.

articles.title: The ParlLawSpeech Parliamentary Text Data Collection > 3 Million Parliamentary Bills, Laws, and Speeches from 8 Legislatures
articles.abstract: Abstract Parliamentary texts are central sources for studying democratic representation, policy-making, and institutional decision-making, and they also constitute a highly valuable domain for natural language processing research. Despite their importance, access to comprehensive, clean, and machine-readable parliamentary corpora remains limited. This paper introduces the ParlLawSpeech (PLS) collection, a large-scale, curated corpus comprising more than three million documents from eight European parliaments, each covering over two decades. PLS extends existing parliamentary text resources in two key ways. First, it integrates full texts and metadata not only for parliamentary speeches but also for legislative bills and finally adopted laws. Second, it provides systematic data linkage across these document types, enabling researchers to trace the full parliamentary decision-making process from draft legislation through debate to adoption. Covering seven national parliaments and the European Parliament, PLS offers a uniquely rich resource for political science and advanced NLP research.

articles.title: A Synchronous EEG-fNIRS Motor Execution and Imagery Dataset
articles.abstract: In the field of motor imagery brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCI), researchers have developed multimodal BCI systems that leverage the complementary spatiotemporal characteristics of electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). This integration has been shown to substantially improve the accuracy and robustness of decoding movement intentions. However, publicly available synchronous EEG-fNIRS datasets for motor imagery tasks remain scarce. Such scarcity severely constrains the development of multimodal fusion algorithms. To address this gap, we introduce and openly release the Synchronous EEG-fNIRS Motor Execution and Imagery Dataset (SEFMEID), a concurrent hybrid EEG-fNIRS motor imagery dataset collected from 50 healthy participants. The dataset includes resting baseline, left-right hand motor execution (ME), and left-right hand motor imagery (MI) conditions, with each subject performing 25 trials for the right task and 25 trials for the left task. We also provide single-modality and multimodal classification results, as well as neurovascular coupling analyses, to validate the usability and quality of the dataset. In the deep learning results, the multimodal fusion algorithm achieves an improvement of approximately 10% over the best-performing unimodal approach. The public release of SEFMEID aims to serve as a valuable resource for advancing multimodal MI-BCI algorithms, investigating neurovascular coupling mechanisms underlying motor imagery, and accelerating clinical translation in neurological rehabilitation.
