articles.title: Mapping EU biological medicines’ regulatory guidance through contributors and documents (1990/2026)
articles.abstract: Abstract European Union Legislation in the sector of biological medicines is complemented by a substantial volume of guidance documents which are essential for strategic choices regarding biologicals development from lab to patients, especially authorisation processes as regards to quality, safety, and efficacy aspects. This corpus of guidance documents has historically been underutilised for research. Hence, the I-BioLex project has focused on both documents and actors, in a genealogical perspective. The two datasets presented in this paper gather all guidance documents relevant to this field, with comprehensive metadata, as well as a list of all contributors to public consultations conducted during the process of adoption or revision of these guidance documents in the field of biologicals at the EU level from 1990 to 2026. It constitutes an original foray into interdisciplinary research at the crossroads of social sciences (law, sociology,…) and biomedical sciences (medicine, pharmacy,…) in order to better understand how guidance documents are shaped and who is influencing them, in the field of biologicals.

articles.title: A High-Resolution UAV Color and CHM Dataset for Bamboo Forest Segmentation and Mapping
articles.abstract: Accurate mapping of bamboo forests is essential for effective management, sustainable utilization, and enabling reproducible research in forest remote sensing and ecological monitoring. To support this, we present a high-resolution unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) dataset for bamboo mapping in unmanaged forest environments. The dataset consists of co-registered RGB orthomosaics and a canopy height model (CHM) derived from UAV LiDAR point cloud data, providing centimeter-level spatial resolution. A total of 76 images were manually annotated to support supervised learning tasks. To facilitate reuse, we also provide baseline methods for training bamboo segmentation models using either a single data source or fused multimodal data. The dataset offers a reliable and scalable resource for forest science and remote sensing communities, particularly for developing and benchmarking methods for bamboo detection, multimodal data fusion, and UAV-based forest mapping in structurally complex, unmanaged landscapes.

articles.title: SARD: A Large-Scale Synthetic Arabic OCR Dataset for Book-Style Text Recognition
articles.abstract: Arabic Optical Character Recognition (OCR) plays a critical role in converting extensive Arabic print media into digital formats. The development of modern OCR models, particularly advanced vision-language models, is hindered by the lack of large, diverse, and well-structured datasets that accurately replicate real-world book layouts. Most existing Arabic OCR datasets focus on isolated words or lines and are limited in scale, typographic diversity, or structural complexity representative of books. To address this limitation, this paper introduces SARD (Large-Scale Synthetic Arabic OCR Dataset). SARD is a synthetically generated dataset specifically designed to simulate book-style documents, comprising 2,621,075 document images and 794.6 million words rendered in six fonts: Sakkal Majalla, Arial, Calibri, Scheherazade New, Amiri, and Traditional Arabic. Unlike datasets derived from scanned documents, SARD is free from real-world noise and distortions, providing a clean and controlled environment for model training. Its synthetic nature enables exceptional scalability and precise control over layout and content variation. This study describes the dataset’s composition, generation process, and technical validation, and presents benchmark results for several traditional and deep-learning OCR models to highlight the challenges and opportunities associated with the dataset. SARD serves as a valuable resource for developing and evaluating robust OCR and vision-language models that can process diverse Arabic book-style texts.

articles.title: A Dataset of Temporally Consistent Instance Annotations for 4D Plant Phenotyping
articles.abstract: Abstract Spatio-temporal 4D plant phenotyping requires high-quality datasets with precise and temporally consistent annotations. However, such datasets are currently limited due to the substantial effort required for data acquisition and manual annotation. To address this limitation, we present Sugar4D, a publicly available 4D plant phenotyping dataset of sugar beet acquired using a terrestrial LiDAR scanner. The dataset comprises 768 point clouds from 48 individual plants representing twelve genotypes, recorded semiweekly across 16 consecutive time points during the growing season. All point clouds are provided with temporally consistent, pointwise instance annotations at the organ level, enabling the tracking of individual leaves over time. Sugar4D includes 6778 annotated leaves corresponding to 675 unique leaf instances. In addition to the annotated point cloud data, we provide 58 plant- and five leaf-related morphological parameters for each plant and leaf at each time point, validated using a 3D-printed plant reference model and invasive manual reference measurements. Sugar4D supports the development and evaluation of methods for plant instance segmentation, temporal registration, organ tracking, and spatio-temporal morphological analysis.

articles.title: Refined annotations of intrahepatic portal and hepatic veins from thin-slice CT images
articles.abstract: Accurate segmentation of intrahepatic vessels in contrast-enhanced CT is limited by spatial resolution, variable contrast timing, and the complexity of peripheral vascular anatomy. Public datasets such as the Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task 08 include annotations of hepatic structures but provide incomplete delineation of small-caliber portal and hepatic veins. This work describes HVA-CT (Hepatic Venous Annotations CT), a dataset derived from the contrast-enhanced thin-slice CT volumes of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task 08, in which intrahepatic venous structures were re-annotated with more complete anatomical delineation. The dataset comprises refined three-dimensional segmentations of portal and hepatic venous systems generated through a structured workflow combining baseline model outputs, AI-assisted vessel branch identification, and expert review. For each case, updated venous segmentation masks, liver segmentations, and a standardized tool for intrahepatic vessel extraction are provided. The dataset is intended to support the development and evaluation of automated methods for hepatic vessel segmentation and analysis.

articles.title: UCOD: A Near-Field Benthic Organism Dataset for Underwater Visual Camouflage and Multi-Task Analysis
articles.abstract: Abstract Accurate near-field underwater visual perception plays a crucial role in marine ecological monitoring and benthic resource exploration. However, the superimposition of the biomimetic characteristics of benthic organisms and the optical degradation caused by the water medium frequently induces significant underwater visual camouflage phenomena. This causes the target foreground and the background to become highly fused in terms of color, texture, and structure, thereby severely limiting the performance of underwater vision algorithms in core tasks such as object detection, image segmentation, and 3D reconstruction. Existing public datasets predominantly focus on salient targets in clear water or under simple backgrounds, lacking comprehensive multi-task benchmarks explicitly tailored for visual camouflage scenarios. To address this gap, we constructed an Underwater Camouflaged Object Dataset (UCOD) for near-field benthic organisms, designed for multi-task analysis to jointly support image enhancement, object detection, pixel-level segmentation, and 3D scene reconstruction. The dataset comprises 7,000 high-resolution RGB images, including 3,500 images with detection annotations, 3,500 images with segmentation masks, and 16 reconstruction sequence folders for 3D reconstruction. It covers six categories of benthic organisms exhibiting typical camouflage characteristics: scallops, fish, conches, abalones, starfish, and sea cucumbers. During data acquisition, calibrated underwater imaging equipment was employed, and the kinematic parameters of the acquisition platform were controlled to improve the stability and spatial consistency of the collected data. The dataset provides useful training data and an evaluation basis for underwater multi-task perception research under visual camouflage conditions, while offering complementary data support for studies on underwater optical sensing and intelligent exploration.

articles.title: A U.S. inventor–patent linkage dataset for National Inventors Hall of Fame inductees
articles.abstract: Elite inventors are important subjects for studying technological change, inventor careers, and innovation networks. However, honorary institutions usually list only representative inventions or seed patents, and general-purpose patent databases do not directly provide audited inventor-level portfolios for externally defined recognition-based inventor groups. Here, we present a U.S. inventor–patent linkage dataset for inductees of the National Inventors Hall of Fame (NIHF). Starting from official NIHF records and U.S. induction-related seed patents, we construct an NIHF–PatentsView public baseline and combine it with broad retrieval of U.S. patent candidates from InCoPat, record-level evidence variables, PatentSBERTa-based semantic clustering, and manual adjudication. The final curated release contains 28,330 inventor–patent links representing 27,155 unique U.S. patent identifiers and covers 638 NIHF inductees. Compared with a public baseline based only on NIHF seed patents and PatentsView inventor identifiers, the dataset retains most baseline links while substantially expanding inventor and patent coverage. The dataset supports studies of NIHF inventors’ U.S. patent portfolios, patenting careers, technology trajectories, collaboration networks, and innovation activities, and can be linked to external patent metadata through standardized patent identifiers.

articles.title: Grid2Text Dataset Aligning Meteorological Grid Data with Expert Reasoning Chains
articles.abstract: Abstract Accurate meteorological forecasting is fundamental to public safety and economic stability, but it heavily relies on numerical weather prediction (NWP) models, whose complex outputs are often inaccessible to non-experts. Although large language models (LLMs) show potential in translating structured data into natural language to automate forecast reporting, progress has been constrained by a critical scarcity of datasets that bridge the modality gap and capture the implicit reasoning of human experts. To address this, we present Grid2Text , a rigorously developed dataset aligning ERA5 meteorological grid features with expert-verified textual forecasts, encompassing explicit reasoning chains for temperature trends, wind vector transitions, humidity ranges, and precipitation types. Furthermore, we establish validation benchmarks derived from a human-in-the-loop workflow to ensure the physical consistency and logical accuracy of the data. We anticipate that this open-access dataset will catalyze the development of interpretable LLM approaches for weather forecast discussions, ultimately advancing the field of scientific text generation.

articles.title: A spatially and temporally aligned contrast-non-contrast cardiac CT dataset of pigs
articles.abstract: Abstract Traditionally, cardiac CT imaging relies on the use of contrast agents. However, in some cases such agents cannot be used, and there is a need to develop novel AI-based algorithms to accurately segment cardiac structures from CT images, recorded without the use of contrast agents. To address this challenging problem, we have collected a spatially and temporally aligned cardiac CT dataset of pigs with and without the use of contrast fluid. This dataset consists of 10 different pigs, CT-scanned multiple times between 15 and 130 kg to cover a wide set of body weights. A subset of the dataset is manually labelled, to enable development of supervised learning-based segmentation techniques.

articles.title: A Comprehensive Multimodal Gait Dataset for Lower-Limb Wearable Robotics in Indoor and Outdoor Environments
articles.abstract: Abstract Daily walking locomotion exhibits variability, asymmetry and ground constraints. Recording and analyzing real-world locomotion data is essential for expanding the application scenarios of wearable robots such as exoskeletons and prostheses. However, most existing gait datasets are collected with specialized equipment under predefined laboratory conditions, lacking visual information from natural walking environments and annotations for transitional states across different surfaces. To address this problem, we collected walking data from 17 healthy participants across diverse indoor and outdoor environments, including kinematic data from seven inertial measurement units (IMUs), foot pressure data from force sensing resistors (FSRs) with 96 points, and visual data from three front-facing cameras with 1280 × 720 resolution. All modalities are time-synchronized, with 448 clips and 243607 data frames in total. Full annotations are provided, covering 16 classes of lower-limb locomotion states (8 steady states, 8 transitional states), bilateral gait phases and bilateral coordinates of the center of pressure (COP). This dataset can be utilized for exploring the applications of machine learning in locomotion state recognition and intelligent control of lower-limb wearable robotics.

articles.title: A Semantically Annotated Ex Vivo Orthopedic Hyperspectral Imaging Dataset for Surgical Tissue Segmentation
articles.abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is an emerging medical imaging modality that provides dense spatial and spectral information for tissue characterization. Despite its growing interest in surgical research, the lack of publicly available, semantically annotated hyperspectral datasets has limited the development and validation of data-driven methods for surgical tissue segmentation. Here, we present HIST-Seg, a semantically annotated hyperspectral imaging dataset designed for surgical tissue segmentation in an orthopedic context. The dataset comprises 220 hyperspectral acquisitions obtained from ten ex vivo bovine specimens using a snapshot hyperspectral camera system. Each datacube has a spatial resolution of 608 × 968 pixels and covers the visible and near-infrared spectral range from 402 to 998 nm. Pixel-level annotations are provided for five orthopedic-relevant tissue classes (bone, cartilage, ligament, fat, and flesh), as well as for surgical instruments and operative-field background. A comprehensive technical validation, including spectral consistency analyses and baseline segmentation experiments, confirms the reliability of the hyperspectral data and annotations. HIST-Seg provides a high-quality reference dataset for the development and benchmarking of machine-learning methods for surgical tissue segmentation. In addition, the dataset may serve as an independent resource for the external evaluation of models developed on other hyperspectral datasets. The source code is publicly available on GitHub.

articles.title: A pediatric ultra-widefield fundus image dataset for artery-vein segmentation
articles.abstract: Retinal artery-vein segmentation has emerged as an important task in medical image analysis, given the close associations between retinal vascular parameters and a wide range of systemic biomarkers and health outcomes. Although several public datasets have been established, important gaps remain due to the lack of pediatric data and the scarcity of ultra-widefield (UWF) fundus imaging, a novel modality capable of capturing richer features across a broader field of view. In this study, we present a Pediatric Ultra-Widefield Fundus image dataset for Artery-Vein segmentation (PUWF-AV), comprising 60 UWF fundus images annotated for artery-vein segmentation by professional ophthalmologists. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first UWF fundus image dataset for artery-vein segmentation in a pediatric population. Technical validation demonstrates the reliability of the dataset, highlighting its potential to advance the development of artery-vein segmentation methods for UWF fundus images in children.

articles.title: Long-term high-frequency hydro-salinity dataset across an intermittent Mediterranean river-estuary continuum
articles.abstract: Abstract Estuaries, acting as interfaces between the land and the sea, provide vital ecosystem services, considered as biodiversity hotspots. Within a Mediterranean climate, they undergo strong hydroclimatic variability, receiving variable riverine inputs from no freshwater to flash floods and being intermittently connected to the sea. We present a ready-to-use dataset, including quality-controlled surface and groundwater measurements along the Fiume Santu, a small Mediterranean temporarily closed estuary. Salinity, temperature and water level were measured hourly for three to seven years, from 2014 to 2022, using multi-parameter probes. Multi-annual recordings highlight the intermittency of connection between aquatic compartments and the buffering role of the estuary, recording recurrent extreme events such as floods, estuarine mouth closures or hypersalinity. The long-term high-frequency hydrological recording of the associated surface and groundwater measurements of a temporarily closed estuary, being scarce, offers a new medium for a broad panel of scientists and environmental managers to expand and further develop in terms of environmental conditions considered in coastal and estuarine studies.

articles.title: A Labelled Dataset of Healthy and Diseased Maize from Tanzania
articles.abstract: Abstract Early detection of crop diseases is essential for improving maize productivity and strengthening food security, particularly in regions where agriculture is the main source of livelihood. This paper presents a labelled image dataset of healthy and diseased maize leaves collected in Tanzania to support the development of machine learning models for crop disease diagnosis. The dataset includes data on: healthy leaves, and diseased leaves of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN) and Maize Streak Virus (MSV) which are among the most significant threats to maize production in the country. All images are annotated to support tasks such as image classification, object detection and image segmentation. The dataset comprises a total of 243,539 labelled images covering multi-season, making it one of the largest publicly available maize image datasets from Tanzania. It serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners advancing artificial intelligence applications in agriculture.

articles.title: Mass balance of the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets from the 1970s to 2023
articles.abstract: Abstract The Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets are major drivers of global mean sea level rise and are predicted to continue to do so in the future. However, they also represent the largest source of uncertainty in projections of future sea level rise making robust estimates of observed ice sheet mass changes critical. Here, we compare and combine 42 independent estimates of ice sheet mass balance derived from satellite observations of temporal changes in ice sheet flow, volume, and gravitational attraction to determine the ice sheet mass balance from 1972 (Greenland) and 1979 (Antarctica) until 2023. We then use regional climate models to partition the total mass balance into contributions associated with surface mass balance and ice dynamical imbalance. The ice sheets lost 11,309 ± 565 billion tonnes of ice between 1979 and 2023, with glacier dynamical imbalance driving 84% of the ice loss and surface mass balance the remainder. This dataset can be used to track the contribution of the ice sheets to sea level rise and constrain projections of future sea level rise.

articles.title: High-resolution European soil property maps based on LUCAS and AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings
articles.abstract: Abstract High-resolution soil property maps have a wide range of applications, e.g. policymaking and precision agriculture. Previously published maps covering the EU-27 plus the UK range in resolution from 250 to 30 metres depending on the soil property. In this work, we produced 10 m resolution maps for soil texture (clay, silt, sand), coarse fragments, pH and bulk density. They are the products of a machine-learning workflow trained on LUCAS soil datasets and using AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings as predictors. We performed hyperparameter tuning and training on Random Forests (RF) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). The best-performing models were ANN, with R 2 values ranging from 0.21 for coarse to 0.69 for pH. The best-performing ANN hyperparameters for each soil property were used to produce soil property maps over Europe as well as uncertainty estimate maps obtained from Monte Carlo dropout. The generated maps aim to close the resolution gap for the EU-27 + UK and provide a promising baseline for precision agriculture, soil health assessment at field scale and spatial planning.

articles.title: A national fish pond dataset for Nigeria generated using automated detection and segmentation
articles.abstract: Fish and other aquatic foods are a vital source of nutrients and livelihoods around the world, and with the stagnation of capture fisheries, countries have increasingly turned to aquaculture. While the geographic expansion of aquaculture is evident from national statistics, much less is known about subnational patterns of growth. Notably, the spatial extent of smallholder aquaculture ponds is poorly understood, limiting our ability to ask basic questions about local risks and benefits stemming from aquaculture investments. To begin to address this, we develop a national dataset of open-air fish pond boundaries for Nigeria using an open-source automated segmentation pipeline to systematically delineate individual fish ponds. As Africa’s most populous nation and third-largest fish producer, Nigeria plays a crucial role in regional food security. With its diversity of geographies and fish production systems, Nigeria offers the ideal case for developing automated approaches to fine-scale fish pond mapping. First, we use georeferenced point labels of fish pond locations to manually delineate fish pond boundaries and create a labeled dataset (N = 14,021). Combining these labels with high-resolution satellite imagery, we then train a national segmentation model and perform predictions across the entire country (precision: 86.3%; recall: 87.9%). We then train a post-processing random forest classifier to distinguish fish ponds from false positives (overall F1: 96.9%, with a per-state F1 mean of 63.5 ± 36.8%). Applying this approach, we identify a total of 246,786 fish ponds throughout Nigeria. Our scalable approach offers a flexible means for fine-scale tracking of smallholder aquaculture patterns, potentially applicable across other smallholder-dominated geographies. Such data are central for food system monitoring and informing interventions to bolster smallholder productivity and market access.

articles.title: A Cantonese speech corpus with picture-based and topic-based discourse tasks across the adult lifespan
articles.abstract: This report introduces CanSpeak , a multi-task, multi-age speech corpus centered on Cantonese, with supplementary Mandarin samples from multilingual speakers. The corpus includes standardized topic-based and picture-based discourse tasks completed by younger and older adults, enabling analyses of speech production and discourse across the lifespan. CanSpeak provides orthographic transcriptions, fine-grained native-speaker annotations of disfluencies and errors, time-aligned annotations, and a range of discourse-level measures indexing fluency, lexical diversity, syntactic complexity, and speech organization. Participant demographic information and cognitive assessment scores are provided, including global cognitive status, processing speed, working memory, and depression scales. Annotation reliability was supported through intra-coder reliability assessment. The dataset was further validated by examining cross-age sensitivity in discourse measures, and cognitive–linguistic associations via relationships between speech features and global cognitive status as measured by the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). By combining cross-generational coverage, task diversity, fine-grained annotation, and cognitive profiling, CanSpeak constitutes a valuable research resource for psycholinguistics, neurolinguistics, aging research, and natural language processing, with particular significance for the study of Cantonese speech production and discourse.

articles.title: Long-read metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets from marine plankton
articles.abstract: Short-read sequencing (SRS) technologies, when applied to the study of environmental communities, present significant limitations that long-read sequencing (LRS) technologies are increasingly overcoming. However, the application of LRS for the integrated study of eukaryotic metagenome and metatranscriptome remains underexplored. Here, we present long-read metagenomic and metatranscriptomic sequencing datasets from four marine plankton samples collected during the Tara Pacific expedition. The metatranscriptome was characterized using high-depth poly(A)-selected cDNA-based Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) PromethION sequencing, and the metagenome using PacBio Revio (HiFi) sequencing. These long-read datasets represent among the first publicly available resources to combine accurate metagenomic datasets with deeply sequenced metatranscriptomes from marine eukaryotic plankton, providing a valuable resource to study their transcript diversity and functional gene expression.

articles.title: The Corpus of English–Tagalog Code-switching: an integrative corpus of linguistic contact effects
articles.abstract: Abstract The Corpus of English–Tagalog Code-switching (CEnTaCS) is a new corpus designed to document naturalistic English–Tagalog bilingual speech. Locally referred to as Taglish, it is a widely-used yet understudied contact variety in the Philippines. Recorded in 2025 in Metro Manila, the corpus comprises three interrelated datasets: individual story retelling recordings, cognitive control data based on the Arrow Flanker task, and sociolinguistic questionnaire data. CEnTaCS offers fine-grained data on code-switching across clausal, lexical, and morphemic levels, with particular attention to intra-word code-switching, a salient but still insufficiently documented feature of Taglish. Beyond code-switching, the corpus captures a broad range of language contact phenomena, including borrowing, calquing, convergence, and interference. By making these data systematically available, the corpus supports an integrated account of mixed-language practices that brings together structural, cognitive, and sociolinguistic perspectives. CEnTaCS thus enables researchers to investigate how contact-induced structures are constrained linguistically, how they relate to bilingual processing, and how they index social meaning and identity in a community where bilingualism is deeply embedded in everyday life.

articles.title: Daily intercity human mobility estimates across Chinese cities from 2020 to 2025
articles.abstract: Intercity human mobility data are essential for regional resource management, ecological footprint assessment, and public-health research. However, existing datasets are often constrained by a trade-off between public accessibility and fine spatiotemporal resolution. To address this gap, we developed the Multi-scale Anchor-Calibrated Mobility (MAC-Mobility) framework, which integrates relative mobility indicators with official national aggregate mobility statistics published by the Ministry of Transport of China (MoT) to estimate daily intercity mobility networks. Through multiscale calibration, benchmarking, and model selection, MAC-Mobility combines 110 directly observed daily national totals, nine monthly aggregate constraints, and spatial allocation constraints derived from the Baidu Migration Index (BMI). The resulting dataset, Daily Intercity Mobility Networks for Chinese Prefecture-Level Cities (DIMNet-CPC), provides directed daily intercity mobility networks with estimated trip volumes from 2020 to 2025, covering 366 administrative units in China. The CatBoost model selected by MAC-Mobility achieved a weighted absolute percentage error (WAPE) of 4.74% and an R 2 of 0.899 in held-out validation at the national aggregate scale. Independent validation of the resulting dataset at the provincial aggregate, prefectural aggregate, and origin–destination (OD) pair scales yielded WAPEs of 14.37%, 25.45%, and 26.52%, respectively, with R 2 values exceeding 0.8 at all three scales. This open-access resource fills an important gap in intercity mobility data and provides an empirical foundation for multidisciplinary research on urban-system resilience, carbon dynamics, public health, and socio-ecological sustainability.

articles.title: Global Warming and Frequency Amplification of Extreme Sea Levels
articles.abstract: Abstract Extreme sea level (ESL), a major driver of coastal flooding, is widely used as a benchmark for coastal engineering design, coastal zone management, and risk assessment. With global warming, ESL events are projected to become more frequent and intense along most of the world’s coastline. Previous work has estimated the minimum global warming level (GWL) and timing at which the present-day 100-year ESL becomes an annual event along the global ice-free coastline. Comparable information for other return periods—such as 10-, 20-, 50-, 100-, and 200-year events—relevant to broader applications remains unavailable. Here, we present global datasets describing the minimum GWL and timing at which multiple present-day ESL return levels transition to annual occurrence. The datasets are derived using a multimethod framework, combining multiple global datasets of present-day ESL and projections of relative sea level change, while accounting for uncertainties. The resulting datasets provide a consistent global reference for assessing how the frequency of ESLs changes across return periods and GWLs, supporting applications in large-scale coastal impact assessment, planning, and risk analysis.

articles.title: A gridded standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index dataset for China spanning the past millennium
articles.abstract: Abstract The lack of reliable, spatiotemporally-completed and millennium-long drought dataset for China has limited a full-field and accurate understanding of drought variability over the past millennium. Here, we present a millennium-long gridded dataset of summer (June-August) Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) for China at 1.875° spatial resolution and annual temporal resolution. This dataset was generated using the paleoclimate data assimilation (PDA) approach by assimilating an expanded proxy network comprising 186 tree rings, 69 historical documents, three stalagmites and two ice cores from China and adjacent regions - addressing the limitations of previous gridded drought reconstructions that lacked proxies in eastern China and had sparsely-distributed proxies in northwestern China. Validation indicated that this dataset exhibits substantially-improved reliability compared to model-only calculations and previous PDA-based reconstruction. As a significantly-improved, millennium-long gridded SPEI dataset for China, this product provides essential support for elucidating the spatiotemporal evolution of drought variability over the past millennium, contextualizing current droughts within that period and evaluating climate model performance in simulating long-term drought events.

articles.title: Fused Geospatial Dataset Linking Climate Hazards and Road Infrastructure for Victoria, Australia
articles.abstract: Abstract This Data Descriptor presents a fused geospatial dataset linking road infrastructure attributes with climate hazard indices for Victoria, Australia. The dataset integrates publicly available road network records from DataVic (traffic volume, pavement condition, and road configuration) with gridded climate hazard indices obtained from the Australian Climate Service (ACS) Hazard Insights Explorer. These hazard indices are derived from dynamically downscaled Climate Modelling Intercomparison Project 6 (CMIP6) projections processed by the Bureau of Meteorology Atmospheric Regional Projections for Australia (BARPA) and CSIRO Cubic Conformal Atmospheric Model (CCAM) regional climate models and provided for multiple global warming levels. All input datasets were harmonised to a common spatial reference and schema to support reproducible climate risk and infrastructure resilience analyses. Quality control procedures included schema validation, topological checks, and sample-based verification. The dataset is openly published on Zenodo under a CC-BY 4.0 licence, with accompanying metadata and reproducible processing scripts to facilitate transparent reuse.

articles.title: A Dataset for Visual Detection of Litchi Fruit Borer Infestation and Anthracnose
articles.abstract: The litchi industry has long been severely plagued by the litchi fruit borer ( Conopomorpha sinensis ) and litchi anthracnose ( Colletotrichum gloeosporioides ). Despite the rapid development of deep learning in agricultural monitoring, there is currently no public dataset that supports the simultaneous detection of these two stresses, let alone a systematic simulation of variable lighting conditions in real postharvest environments. To address this issue, we constructed LitchiPestDisease—the first multi-illumination image dataset dedicated to the detection of litchi fruit borer infestation and litchi anthracnose. This dataset contains images collected from the core production areas in Maoming, Guangdong, China, during 2024 and 2025. To support the simulation of realistic grading scenarios, the dataset includes the original images and three systematically enhanced illumination variants (front lighting, back lighting, and side lighting) generated following the protocol described in this paper. All these images are provided in the public repository. The pest subset includes 3,061 original images, all annotated with bounding boxes for borer damage holes. The disease subset consists of 3,644 original images, a portion of which are additionally annotated with polygon instance segmentation, where each lesion is labeled by its severity (mild, moderate, severe). The corresponding enhanced images under three lighting conditions are fully provided in the public repository. Benchmark experiments based on YOLOv12n validated the effectiveness of the dataset: severe anthracnose detection reached near-perfect mAP50 levels, while pest detection achieved an mAP50 of 0.6539 under mixed lighting conditions. Comparative analyses across different lighting conditions and disease severity levels revealed the robustness and limitations of the model (e.g., the recall rate for mild disease under side lighting dropped to 0.878). Furthermore, benchmark experiments on instance segmentation revealed the performance variation of segmentation models under different lighting conditions, jointly providing a multi-task evaluation benchmark for algorithm optimization. LitchiPestDisease provides an important benchmark resource for the intelligent detection of fruit quality in real-world scenarios.

articles.title: Harmonised climate and Aedes albopictus arboviral vector mosquito surveillance datasets for the European continent
articles.abstract: Abstract We present two harmonised datasets linking Aedes albopictus mosquito surveillance observations with standardised climate variables, designed to support benchmarking and reproducible modelling of mosquito distribution and abundance across Europe. The first dataset pairs polygon-level presence/absence records from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) with ERA5-Land and CORDEX climate grids, yielding 157,918 and 79,398 spatially explicit grid points respectively, of which 34,482 and 20,832 carry confirmed presence labels. The second dataset combines 15,374 trap-level observations from 1,648 trap locations across western and southern Europe (AIMSurv v2.3) with ERA5-Land daily and monthly climate variables aligned to sampling periods. Both datasets are generated through transparent, documented preprocessing pipelines with explicit quality-control criteria, relying exclusively on open data sources. Rather than introducing new primary surveillance observations, this secondary data resource provides a reproducible transformation of public surveillance and climate sources into common, analysis-ready benchmark datasets. Together, they provide a consistent foundation for methodological benchmarking and reuse across ecological and epidemiological applications. Both datasets are publicly available via the JRC Data Catalogue.

articles.title: A Cyber-Attack Detection Dataset for Distribution Systems Generated from a Scaled Cyber-Physical Testbed
articles.abstract: Modern power distribution systems, characterized by deep integration with communication networks, are increasingly susceptible to cyber threats. A critical challenge for attack detection research lies in the scarcity of authentic datasets derived from physical hardware testbeds. To address this critical need, an open dataset, termed CPDS-AD, is established for cyber-attack detection in cyber-physical distribution systems. This dataset is generated utilizing a developed laboratory-level scaled testbed, which emulates the steady-state operating and cyber-measurement processes of a 13-node three-phase unbalanced medium-voltage-type radial distribution feeder and a three-layer cyber architecture. It captures both normal-operation data and data recorded under various realistic cyber-attacks, including multiple types of false data injection and denial-of-service attacks. Raw communication messages are meticulously recorded and processed into synchronized, time-aligned measurement data. The quality and effectiveness of the dataset for developing data-driven attack detection methods are demonstrated through technical validation, employing dimensionality reduction and unsupervised machine learning models.

articles.title: Single-cell transcriptomes of mouse prostate cancer models and human blood after irreversible electroporation
articles.abstract: Irreversible electroporation (IRE) is a focal ablation approach for localized prostate cancer. We generated a data resource comprising single-cell RNA-sequencing profiles from subcutaneous and orthotopic RM-1 mouse tumors collected 7 days after IRE or sham intervention and paired peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) samples from five patients collected before and 7 days after IRE. All three components were prepared from whole-cell suspensions. This Data Descriptor documents cohort design, sample processing, sequencing, computational quality control, integration diagnostics and cell-annotation evidence for 20 sequencing libraries (six subcutaneous tumors, four orthotopic tumors and ten PBMC samples). Per-sample quality-control summaries, software and parameter records, sample composition tables and canonical-marker panels support independent assessment and reuse of the datasets.

articles.title: Full-ocean-depth EM124 mapping of the Challenger Deep by R/V Hakuho-maru and depth-estimate sensitivity tests
articles.abstract: Abstract The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is the deepest known point on Earth, yet recent depth estimates still differ by several meters because of environmental and instrumental uncertainties. Here we present a new full-ocean-depth multibeam bathymetric dataset collected with a Kongsberg EM124 echosounder aboard R/V Hakuho-maru during the KH-23-9 cruise in 2023. The survey comprises east–west and north–south lines acquired at vessel speeds of 4–15 kt. Five seawater sound velocity models were constructed from contemporaneous XCTD data, historical full-depth CTD data, and a recent full-depth reference profile to test the sensitivity of depth estimates. After ping-by-ping editing and gridding, the preferred KH23XCTD+KH92CTD solution resolves three basins deeper than 10,900 m, with maximum depths of 10,926, 10,912, and 10,927 m in the western, central, and eastern basins, respectively. Alternative sound velocity models yield maximum depths from 10,914 to 10,932 m, illustrating the meter- to >10-m-scale sensitivity of full-ocean-depth multibeam estimates to the applied sound velocity structure. Cleaned point soundings, gridded bathymetric surfaces for each sound velocity model, and the gridding script are provided. The dataset enables assessment of how sound velocity structure, survey speed, and beam-footprint geometry influence depth estimates in full-ocean-depth multibeam mapping, and provides a new reference for cross-comparison of Challenger Deep bathymetry.

articles.title: GloSVeT: a global 0.05° monthly mean surface soil and vegetation component temperature dataset (2003–2023)
articles.abstract: Current satellite-derived land surface temperature (LST) products represent a mixed radiative signal that integrates soil and vegetation contributions, obscuring the physical mechanisms controlling surface energy partitioning and ecosystem functioning. To overcome this limitation, this study developed the Global Soil and Vegetation Temperature dataset (GloSVeT), the first global product that simultaneously provides surface soil and vegetation component temperatures at 0.05° spatial resolution for the period 2003–2023. GloSVeT was generated using the multisource data fusion-based global surface soil and vegetation temperature retrieval (FuSVeT) method, which integrates multi-temporal MODIS observations with ERA5-Land reanalysis to improve spatial completeness, retrieval accuracy, and computational efficiency. Its performance was extensively assessed through a comprehensive evaluation framework combining internal closure check, flux-tower validation at 72 representative sites, triple collocation (TC) analysis, and physical consistency assessments. Results show that GloSVeT largely preserves the original MODIS mixed-pixel LST constraint, and achieves reliable accuracy with coefficients of determination mostly at or above 0.9 and root mean square errors generally around 2 K for both components. TC analysis further demonstrates globally consistent performance, with advantages in humid tropics and transitional ecosystems compared with reanalysis products. In addition, soil temperature anomalies are predominantly negatively correlated with soil moisture whereas vegetation temperature aligns with solar-induced fluorescence along a clear gradient from energy-limited to water-limited biomes, indicating the physical consistency of GloSVeT. Over pixels where soil and vegetation temperatures are simultaneously available, both components exhibit evident warming trends during 2003–2023, with rates of 0.44 ± 0.04 K per decade for soil temperature and 0.39 ± 0.04 K per decade for vegetation temperature. In summary, GloSVeT provides a physically consistent, observation-driven depiction of surface thermal dynamics, offering new opportunities for quantifying land–atmosphere energy exchange, monitoring ecosystem hydrothermal responses, and improving the representation of land surface processes in Earth system models. GloSVeT is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.11888/RemoteSen.tpdc.303317 (Liu and Li, 2026a) and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22724289 (Liu and Li, 2026b).

articles.title:
Signal-domain guided deep learning for gap-filling of XCO and XCH
                    <sub>4</sub>
                    : a masked spatio-temporal fusion of TROPOMI and GEOS-Chem (2019–2023)
articles.abstract: Long-term, high-resolution monitoring of carbon monoxide (CO) and methane (CH 4 ) is essential for understanding their spatiotemporal variability and supporting climate mitigation strategies. However, satellite observations from instruments such as the TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) are often spatially and temporally incomplete, while existing fusion methods still struggle to achieve both high accuracy and spatiotemporal continuity. Here, we propose a signal-domain fusion approach that combines three-dimensional discrete cosine transform (3D DCT) and singular value decomposition (SVD) to integrate TROPOMI retrievals with GEOS-Chem simulations. A lightweight residual U-Net is further employed to refine the initial reconstruction by learning residual fields from GEOS-Chem simulations and DCT/SVD reconstruction outputs, guided by a masked loss. The method generates global 0.25° and China-specific 0.05° daily gap-free XCO and XCH 4 datasets from 2019 to 2023. In the time-series comparison analysis at representative sites, the fused datasets generally follow the temporal variations observed by the Total Carbon Column Observing Network (TCCON) and TROPOMI. Missing-rate-threshold experiments further show that the fused products perform comparably to original TROPOMI retrievals under low and moderate missing-rate conditions and show improved performance under sparse TROPOMI coverage (MR >0.5), with R 2 values of 0.91 for XCO and 0.83 for XCH 4 , along with reduced biases and standard deviations. The fused datasets also capture regional XCO increases in parts of North America, decreases over eastern China, and widespread XCH 4 growth, wildfire-related enhancements in Chongqing in 2022, and short-term variations over rice-growing regions. These results indicate that the proposed framework can reconstruct missing satellite observations with improved continuity and provide useful fused datasets for studying regional variability, event-related enhancements, and atmospheric composition changes. The generated datasets are publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22010891 (An et al., 2026).
articles.authors: Chengkun An, Yuan Tian, Zhiwei Li, Qiaoyu Jiang, Peize Lin, Bowen Chang, Jingkai Xue, Youwen Sun

articles.interpretationCn: 该研究面向一氧化碳（CO）和甲烷（CH4）的长期高分辨率监测，针对TROPOMI卫星反演在时空上不完整的问题，提出信号域融合方法：结合三维离散余弦变换（3D DCT）与奇异值分解（SVD），将TROPOMI反演与GEOS-Chem模拟相融合，并用轻量残差U-Net在掩膜损失引导下学习残差场以精化初始重建。方法生成2019至2023年全球0.25°和中国区域0.05°的每日无空缺XCO与XCH4数据集。在代表性站点的时间序列对比中，融合数据总体跟随TCCON和TROPOMI观测的时间变化；缺失率阈值实验显示，在低和中缺失率条件下融合产品与原始TROPOMI反演表现相当，在稀疏覆盖（MR>0.5）下表现更优，XCO的R2为0.91、XCH4为0.83，偏差和标准差降低。融合数据还捕捉到北美部分区域XCO上升、中国东部下降、XCH4广泛增长、2022年重庆野火相关增强以及水稻种植区短期变化。生成的数据集公开可用。

articles.title: A global gridded dataset of significant wave height via fusion of multi-mission altimetry and numerical hindcast
articles.abstract: Satellite altimeters provide long-term, high-accuracy observations of significant wave height (SWH) over the global ocean. However, their sparse spatial and temporal sampling introduces undersampling errors in wave climate analyses. Direct gridding of multi-mission altimeter data through spatiotemporal interpolation still results in low-accuracy global SWH fields due to this limitation. To overcome this challenge, we use SWH outputs from a WAVEWATCH III hindcast as a background field and apply an offline fusion with along-track, jointly calibrated altimeter observations from the Climate Change Initiative Sea State dataset. As a retrospective reconstruction, the offline fusion allows observations acquired both before and after a target time to contribute to the estimate, with their influence explicitly constrained by temporal separation. Validation against buoy measurements and withheld satellite data demonstrates that the fused gridded product achieves high accuracy. To address different application needs, we provide two versions of the fused dataset: (1) a “two-sat” version that incorporates data from only two satellites at any given time, designed for wave climate studies. This configuration is designed to reduce sampling-related temporal inhomogeneity by maintaining a relatively stable number of observations and broadly consistent orbital sampling characteristics throughout the record. (2) A “multi-sat” version that integrates data from as many altimeter missions as possible, intended to support applications such as the training of artificial intelligence-based wave models, where higher spatial and temporal accuracy is prioritized. The dataset is freely available at https://doi.org/10.57760/sciencedb.29314 (Su and Jiang, 2025).

articles.title: A Reference Dataset of 66 High-Quality Plastid Genomes across Three Algal Phyla
articles.abstract: Algae represent a diverse group of photosynthetic organisms, and their plastid genomes provide valuable molecular resources for investigating plastid evolution, photosynthetic adaptation, and phylogenetic relationships. However, algal plastomes exhibit remarkable evolutionary diversity, with substantial variation in genome structure and organization across different lineages. Currently, high-quality algal plastid genomes and a standardized and reliable workflow for generating high-quality algal plastid genomes is still lacking. To address these challenges, we successfully assembled 66 high-quality, complete algal plastid genomes, including 7 green, 19 brown, and 40 red algal genomes. During this process, we developed and established a standardized workflow for plastid genome assembly and quality assessment. Notably, these newly assembled genomes enrich existing NCBI resources by contributing 29 species, 13 genera, four families, and one order for the first time, offering both expanded taxonomic coverage and a standardized foundation for subsequent comparative and evolutionary analyses.

articles.title: A high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly of a swimming sea cucumber Hansenothuria sp. from a deep seamount in the Western Pacific Ocean
articles.abstract: Sea cucumbers are an important echinoderm lineage for studying the evolution trajectory and environmental adaptability. However, the limited availability of high-quality chromosomes for sea cucumbers from deep sea ecosystems has hindered a thorough understanding of mechanisms underlying their adaptive evolution. In this study, we reported the first chromosome-level genome assembly in the order Persiculida, Hansenothuria sp. M1226 from a deep seamount in the Western Pacific Ocean, which was sequenced on the PacBio Sequel II platform using the CLR (continuous long reads) mode. The Hansenothuria sp. M1226 genome assembly has a total length of 3.52 Gb with a scaffold N50 length of 133.1 Mb, encompassing 23 chromosomes, highlighting high genome continuity. Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs (BUSCO) assessment yielded a completeness estimate of 85.0% for the genome assembly and 90.6% for its gene set. We predicted a total of 32,054 protein-coding genes (PCGs), with 27,273 functionally annotated. The availability of this high-quality chromosome-level genome of Hansenothuria sp. M1226 contributes to our understanding of the origin and evolution of sea cucumbers.

articles.title: A database of second-order rate constants for reactions of eight environmentally relevant oxidants with pollutants
articles.abstract: Second-order reaction rate constants are critical for quantifying oxidants’ reactivity and modeling contaminant transformation. However, such data are widely scattered across the published literature and public databases, and their reuse is severely limited by inconsistent chemical identifiers, non-uniform metadata, and heterogeneous reporting formats. Here, we constructed a curated database of second-order reaction rate constants for reactions between pollutants and eight environmentally relevant oxidant/radical including hydroxyl radical ( • OH), sulfate radical (SO 4 •− ), carbonate radical (CO 3 •− ), chlorine radical (Cl • ), dichlorine radical (Cl 2 •− ), ozone (O 3 ), hypochlorous acid/hypochlorite (HOCl/OCl − ), and singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ), containing 11,579 individual records. The dataset was systematically compiled from peer-reviewed publications, experimental kinetic studies, and public repositories including the NIST database. Chemical identifiers were standardized to CAS Registry Numbers and SMILES strings, metadata were unified across entries, and duplicate or inconsistent records were resolved using a rigorous multi-step quality control process. The final dataset is deposited in Figshare as machine-readable CSV files for direct download and reuse. This integrated resource will advance research in oxidation kinetics, comparative reactivity analysis, and data-driven applications in environmental chemistry and water treatment.

articles.title: A Global Dataset of Surface NO2 Estimation Based on Machine Learning Using Process-based Information
articles.abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a key air pollutant associated with numerous adverse human and environmental health outcomes, yet globally consistent, fine-resolution long-term surface NO 2 datasets remain scarce due to the shortcomings of available data sources and the complex relationships between emissions and surface NO 2 concentrations. Here, we improve estimates of global monthly surface NO 2 concentrations at fine spatial resolution (0.01° × 0.01°) over 2005–2023 by developing, optimizing, and applying a highly efficient gradient boosting decision tree (LightGBM) framework underpinned with multi-source datasets, including geophysical process-based a priori information that leverages simulations with the GEOS-Chem chemical transport model, road‐network metrics, land‐cover features, and other relevant environmental predictors over 2005–2023. Evaluated against 9,913 ground monitors across 66 countries, the machine learning model achieves significant agreement for the benchmark year 2023 with 10-fold spatial cross-validation for monthly surface NO 2 estimates ( \({R}^{2}\) = 0.82, RMSE = 2.34 ppb, slope = 0.97), and similar long-term performance over 2005–2023 ( \({R}^{2}\) = 0.76, RMSE = 3.42 ppb, slope = 0.97). We apply Buffered Leave Isolated Sites and Clusters Out (BLISCO) spatial cross-validation to rigorously account for spatial autocorrelation, finding that traditional spatial cross-validation overestimates performance over unmonitored areas and that process-based physical and chemical information from chemical transport model (GEOS-Chem) simulations significantly improves R 2 by 20% globally. Global per-pixel uncertainty quantification indicates that this dataset provides NO 2 estimates with median relative uncertainty of 35% and absolute uncertainty of 1.81 ppb. This 19-year fine-resolution global NO 2 dataset with a consistent methodology, process-based information, rigorous validation and uncertainty quantification offers a valuable resource for quantifying the magnitude, spatial patterns, long-term trends and impacts of global NO 2 exposure.

articles.title: A single-cell RNA sequencing dataset of kidney and peripheral blood mononuclear cells from Dahl salt-sensitive rats under high and low salt diets
articles.abstract: Hypertension is a major global health burden, with high dietary sodium intake being a key environmental risk factor. The Dahl salt-sensitive (SS) rat is a well-established model for studying salt-sensitive hypertension and renal damage. To facilitate research into the cellular mechanisms of salt-sensitivity, we generated a single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset from the kidney and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of Dahl SS rats. Male rats were fed either a high-salt (4% NaCl) or low-salt (0.4% NaCl) diet for three weeks. We profiled high-quality cells from kidney tissue and from PBMCs. This dataset captures the cellular diversity of these tissues, including immune, epithelial, and endothelial cell populations, under different dietary conditions. This resource provides a foundation for investigating how high sodium intake influences cellular composition, gene expression, and cell-cell communication at single-cell resolution. As the Dahl SS rat remains one of the most widely used models for hypertension research, this dataset offers a valuable reference for exploring cell-type-specific responses to salt and generating hypotheses for future mechanistic studies.

articles.title: A Large-Scale Standardized Pediatric Normal Electrocardiogram Dataset
articles.abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) is a widely used non-invasive method for diagnosing cardiovascular diseases. ECG signal characteristics vary markedly across age groups, with pediatric recordings differing substantially from those of adults. Establishing a reliable baseline for defining a “normal” pediatric ECG across developmental stages is essential prior to designing algorithms for abnormality detection. Existing ECG databases are predominantly composed of adult data and lack comprehensive age stratification, while a few pediatric ECG databases are only from hospitalized children, resulting in a scarcity of large-scale, publicly available pediatric datasets that accurately reflect typical cardiac physiology of children. To address this gap, we present a large-scale, standardized pediatric normal ECG dataset comprising recordings from children aged 0-6 years. The dataset was compiled from a larger collection acquired at the Children’s Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, between 2019 and 2023. It includes 58,672 standardized 12-lead ECG recordings, each 10 seconds in duration and sampled at 500 Hz, all annotated as “NORM” by experienced pediatric cardiologists. This resource aimed to serve as a high-quality reference baseline for pediatric ECG research and algorithm development.

articles.title: A daily 0.025° gridded column-averaged carbon dioxide dataset for terrestrial Europe from 2019 to 2023
articles.abstract: High-resolution, continuous monitoring of atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) is essential for assessing regional carbon dynamics and tracking the effectiveness of climate mitigation policies such as the European Green Deal. Here, we present a daily, 0.025° × 0.025° column-averaged dry-air CO 2 mole fraction (XCO 2 ) dataset covering terrestrial Europe (12°W–40°E, 34°N–72°N) from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023. The dataset is generated using a categorical boosting model that integrates Orbiting Carbon Observatory satellite retrievals, CarbonTracker 2025, and meteorological, land surface, and anthropogenic emission data. Independent validation against six European Total Carbon Column Observing Network stations yields a coefficient of determination of 0.95 and a root-mean-square error of 1.06 ppm. Comparison with the independent Greenhouse Gases Observing Satellite product shows accuracy comparable to mainstream products, with high-XCO 2 regions more clearly resolved. Feature-attribution diagnostics indicate that the learned relationships align with known atmospheric processes. This dataset is designed to advance regional carbon monitoring in Europe and support the evaluation of climate policies like the European Green Deal.

articles.title: A global, historical, harmonized land-use dataset spanning 1900 to 2023 at 0.05° resolution reconstructed based on remote sensing and statistical data
articles.abstract: Understanding long-term land-use and land-cover dynamics is fundamental for quantifying human impacts on Earth system and supporting global carbon-cycle and climate assessments. However, existing global land-use and land-cover datasets rarely reconcile high spatial resolution with long-term temporal coverage, limiting their applicability for century-scale Earth system analyses. To address this problem, we developed a top-down land-use reconstruction framework integrating fine-resolution remote-sensing land-cover information with Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) cropland and grazing-land statistics to produce a global, historical, harmonized land-use dataset for 0.05° resolution (approximately 5.6 km at the equator) (called HLUH-5km), a dataset providing spatially explicit fractions of six major land-use types for the period 1900–2023. HLUH-5km was assessed through a multi-level validation framework. It shows strong agreement with FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment (FRA) national forest area statistics, which were collected separately from the FAO Statistical Database (FAOSTAT) cropland and grazing-land data used as allocation inputs at the national level (slope = 1.01, R 2 = 0.96), indicating that the reconstructed forest trajectories are consistent with reported national forest inventories. The dataset also captures within-country spatial variability consistent with reported subnational land-use records across multiple regions. Grid-level comparison with satellite-derived land-cover products and regional historical reconstructions further demonstrate improved spatial consistency relative to existing global historical reconstructions. HLUH-5km provides a coherent basis for land-use analysis, terrestrial carbon accounting, and Earth system modeling.

articles.title: A Legacy Snow Load Dataset: Long-Term Measurements of Roof and Ground Snow Loads in Norway
articles.abstract: Long-term empirical datasets are fundamental to the development, calibration, and verification of structural design models, yet the sustained efforts required to establish such datasets are often under-recognised. This Data Descriptor presents a curated and digitised dataset of roof and ground snow-load measurements collected by Professor Halvor Høibø (1924–2013) in Norway between 1966 and 1986. The dataset comprises full-scale measurements on agricultural buildings with gable roofs, including windward and leeward roof snow loads, ground snow loads, snow densities, roof geometry, exposure descriptors, and temporal information. These measurements have played a central role in the development of structural snow-load models and have informed international design standards, including ISO 4355 and EN 1991-1-3, as well as related North American standardisation work. The dataset has now been standardised, quality-controlled, and extended with geolocation and harmonised metadata, enabling integration with modern climate reanalysis products and facilitating climate-sensitive snow-load research. The dataset is provided in an open, reusable format to support reproducibility, comparative studies, and future assessments of non-stationarity in snow loads under a changing climate.

articles.title: Reporting and hosting a dataset of high-impedance faults in medium-voltage covered conductors
articles.abstract: Abstract This work presents a multimodal dataset characterizing high-impedance faults (HIF) in medium-voltage covered conductors under controlled single-phase, phase-to-ground contact conditions. Insulation reduces wildfire risks but restricts fault currents below conventional detection thresholds. This restriction delays the onset of the fault signature. The dataset documents the temporal evolution of these events by integrating high-resolution electrical waveforms sampled at 20 kS/s with power-quality metrics from an IEC 61000-4-30 Class A analyzer. Complementary modalities include radiometric thermography and visual video with embedded audio for selected cases. The experimental design covers 22 groups and 142 segments, spanning conductor tip geometry, air gaps, surface materials, and moisture actions. Instrumentation uses independent acquisition platforms to minimize electromagnetic interference. Technical validation confirms a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 5:1 at nominal voltage and metrological consistency between platforms. This repository provides a structured framework for validating physical models and developing detection algorithms addressing incipient dielectric failure in overhead distribution networks.

articles.title: GermND-3M: A multi-crop multi-variety multi-modal dataset for germplasm variety-quality-viability nondestructive detection
articles.abstract: Rapidly nondestructive assessment of germplasm variety, quality, and viability (VQV) is required to ensure genetic integrity and support the secure conservation and utilization of crop germplasm. However, large-scale, standardized, and openly available scientific datasets encompassing multiple crops, varieties, and modalities are still lacking in the field of intelligent nondestructive VQV detection of germplasm resources. We constructed GermND-3M, a multi-crop, multi-variety, and multi-modal dataset for germplasm VQV nondestructive detection. The dataset comprises 3,214 varieties from four major crops, including 1,000 rice varieties, 595 wheat varieties, 1,000 maize varieties, and 619 soybean varieties. Each variety comprised 100 seeds. The dataset integrates hyperspectral imaging, volatile-gas sensing, and grain phenotypic imaging data from seeds, together with corresponding variety, quality, and viability labels. Standardized acquisition and processing protocols were applied to ensure data comparability. Dataset usability was evaluated using classical machine-learning and deep-learning models. GermND-3M provides a standardized resource for the development and benchmarking of nondestructive germplasm assessment methods and supports data-driven germplasm conservation and crop breeding.

articles.title: Dataset for Glycemic Control Analysis in Type 1 Diabetes under Multiple Daily Injection Treatment in Free-living Conditions
articles.abstract: Open-source datasets of glucose monitoring play a critical role in facilitating research in diabetes management and treatment, while allowing the development of Artificial Intelligence models for blood glucose forecasting. While many efforts are spent on patients with Type 1 Diabetes with Continuous Glucose Monitoring, many patients are still relying on Multiple Daily Injection treatment due to lower cost and easier accessibility. Due to individual differences in living styles and physiological responses to various insulin treatments, more structured datasets with detailed behavioral and physiological factors in real-life living conditions are expected. Contributing to the research on Type 1 Diabetes, this study introduces the OU-DATASET, a longitudinal, multimodal resource for analyzing glycemic control within multiple daily injection treatment. The dataset includes glucose level monitoring, insulin injection, activity tracker data (heart rate, steps) records, and self-reported lifestyle events (meals, exercise, stress) collected from 22 participants on multiple daily injection therapy over an 8-week period. This descriptor details the data collection protocol, data architecture, and accessibility of the dataset. The OU-DATASET supports further development of data-driven algorithms and models for the treatment management of Type 1 diabetes.

articles.title: Steady-State Visual-Evoked EEG Dataset for Visual Function Assessment via Biomarker Extraction
articles.abstract: Amblyopia and intermittent exotropia (IXT) are prevalent pediatric visual impairments characterized by deficits in cortical visual processing. Understanding the underlying neurophysiological mechanisms and tracking neural recovery requires high–quality, objective data, yet open–access EEG datasets specifically designed for these pediatric populations—particularly those with a longitudinal dimension—remain scarce. Here, we present the steady–state visual–evoked EEG (S2VEEG) dataset, a 64–channel electroencephalography (EEG) dataset collected from pediatric participants, including amblyopia, IXT, and healthy controls. The S2VEEG dataset uses a multimodal experimental paradigm comprising resting–state recordings, transient Visual Evoked Potentials (VEP), and Steady–State Visual Evoked Potentials (SSVEP). The dataset employs a longitudinal design, capturing neural activity both at baseline and following therapeutic interventions (perceptual learning for amblyopia and strabismus surgery for IXT). For technical validation, differential entropy (DE) and small–worldness properties are extracted as features and analyzed using Support Vector Machine (SVM), Residual Graph Convolutional Broad Network (RGCB), and Emotion Transformer (EmT) classifiers. The classification performance suggests that the recorded EEG signals contain discriminative electrophysiological information across visual function states, thereby supporting the usability of the S2VEEG dataset as candidate discriminative measures for methodological development and exploratory analyses. These results are intended as a technical validation of data quality and feature separability, while this resource provides a valuable platform for future studies investigating brain–eye interactions, treatment–induced neuroplasticity, and the development of objective biomarkers for monitoring visual function recovery.

articles.title: Aerodynamic Data for Validation: The CHN-T1 Large Aircraft Standard Model Dataset
articles.abstract: Abstract With the increasing demand for high-fidelity aerodynamic validation benchmarks for advanced civil aircraft design, this paper presents an open-access, high-Reynolds-number transonic wind tunnel dataset for the CHN-T1 standard large aircraft model, generated from systematic tests conducted in the European Transonic Wind Tunnel (ETW). Tests were performed on the full CHN-T1 configuration with horizontal and vertical tailplanes, under two boundary layer transition settings: fixed artificial transition and free natural transition. The test envelope covers a Mach number range of 0.20–0.90, Reynolds numbers from 3.6 × 10 6 to 37.8 × 10 6 , achieved via pressurization combined with cryogenic cooling down to 115 K and ambient 300 K conditions, with a total of 33 valid aerodynamic polars acquired. The comprehensive dataset includes corrected aerodynamic coefficients, freestream flow conditions and model attitude data. It addresses the scarcity of high-Reynolds-number data and the common lack of lateral-directional and full-configuration measurements in existing public benchmarks. This dataset provides a reliable benchmark for CFD solver validation, wind tunnel flow quality assessment, and the development of data-driven aerodynamic model, supporting the advancement of modern civil aircraft design.

articles.title: OceanTACO: a multi-sensor global ocean sea surface state dataset
articles.abstract: We present OceanTACO, a harmonised global collection of sea surface state datasets designed to support reproducible Earth system research. The collection integrates satellite altimetry, sea surface temperature, salinity, surface winds, reanalysis fields, and Argo in situ observations within a unified cloud-optimised specification based on Transparent Access to Cloud-optimised datasets (TACO). It includes Level-3 observations, Level-4 gap-filled products, and reanalysis outputs while preserving native spatial and temporal resolution. The core dataset spans 29 March 2023 to 1 August 2025, covering the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission, with an extended record from 1 January 2015 until 29 March 2023 for non-SWOT sources. Datasets are harmonised through standardised metadata, spatial referencing, and temporal indexing, enabling consistent spatiotemporal queries across sensors and processing levels. The contribution is not a new regridding or compression method, but a sample-invariant, provenance-preserving organisation that allows the same data-access routines to be applied across regions, sensors, and studies. This supports Earth system analysis workflows such as validation against in situ observations, comparisons between observation and mapped products, observation system experiments, and multivariate sensor analyses. Example applications demonstrate cross-product collocation with Argo, analysis of sea surface height variability during extreme events, and relationships between surface variables relevant for data-driven reconstruction. OceanTACO improves accessibility to coordinated multi-source analyses while preserving data provenance and native observation characteristics, and can be extended with new missions without restructuring the dataset. The core and extended dataset are available at https://doi.org/10.57967/hf/8171 (Lehmann and Aybar, 2026a) and https://doi.org/10.57967/hf/8172 (Lehmann and Aybar, 2026b) respectively.

articles.title: FAO estimates of net forest emissions and removals, 1990–2025
articles.abstract: FAO officially collects, analyzes and disseminates forest data by country via the Forest Resources Assessment (FRA) program since the late 1950s. Since 2015, FAO uses a subset of the FRA data, namely forest area and carbon stocks, to compute and disseminate in FAOSTAT net forest emissions/removals estimates, as part of its efforts to assess emissions from agrifood systems. This paper presents the most recent update of the FAO net emission/removal estimates, based on estimates of carbon stock change from all pools, i.e., above- and below-ground living biomass, litter, dead wood and soils, covering over 200 countries and territories for the period 1990–2025. Results show that forests acted globally as net carbon sinks since the 2000s, on average ranging from −1.0 to -2.3GtCO2yr-1 over the most recent decade 2015–2025. This net flux was a result of substantial carbon removals on forest land over the same period, ranging from −3.8 to -6.1GtCO2yr-1, only partially counterbalanced by emissions from net forest loss of 2.8–3.8 Gt CO 2 yr −1 – used herein as a proxy of deforestation. Annex I (AI) and non-Annex I (NAI) countries contributed equally to the estimated forest removals, whereas 90 % of emissions from net forest loss were generated in NAI countries. Comparisons of the FAO estimates with data submitted independently by countries to the United Nations Framework Convention (UNFCCC), as well as with output from the Global Carbon Budget, showed good agreement at global, AI and NAI levels, including for major forest countries. At the same time, important discrepancies between FAO, UNFCCC and global carbon model data were identified in about a dozen countries. Improved convergence of evidence is achievable through dedicated statistical development programs in specific countries, to support international implementation and monitoring of effective climate mitigation actions. The FAO estimates and country data collected from UNFCCC were disseminated in FAOSTAT for 194 countries and 42 territories, with regional and global aggregates, in annual time-series covering the period 1990–2025. They were made available as open access at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20085666 (Tubiello and Obli-Laryea, 2026).

articles.title: A Global Database of Soil Methane Uptake (SMUD)
articles.abstract: Soil methane uptake (SMU), an important biological sink for atmospheric methane (CH 4 ) in terrestrial ecosystems, represents an important component of the global CH 4 budget. Although field SMU observations have been conducted since the 1980s, they have not yet been systematically compiled into a unified and openly available database. Here, we present the global Soil Methane Uptake Database (SMUD), which includes 2427 site-level records from 920 peer-reviewed publications spanning 1986 to 2025. SMUD contains SMU measurements at multiple temporal scales, including daily ( n =1425), monthly ( n =2001), seasonal ( n =1720), and annual ( n =1098), together with associated soil moisture and soil temperature data at daily and monthly scales where available. The collected datasets cover all major climatic zones and ecosystem types and reveal pronounced spatial and temporal variability in SMU. Our analyses show that seasonal- and biome-specific patterns are important for understanding intra-annual variability in SMU. In particular, quantitative classification showed that the relationships of SMU with soil temperature and moisture differed among biomes, resulting in four response types: temperature-dominated, moisture-dominated, jointly regulated by temperature and moisture, and no clear dominant control. Overall, SMUD provides a comprehensive basis for characterizing global SMU patterns, investigating underlying mechanisms, and improving estimates of the global SMU budget. The database, associated data, and code for reproducing the results are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20735332 (Jiang et al., 2026). We aim to maintain SMUD as a collaborative, community-supported, and regularly updated resource for the research community.

articles.title: LLM Board Game Tournaments: A Dataset of Moves, Validity, and Reasoning
articles.abstract: Abstract We present A Dataset of LLM Strategic Play , comprising 9,572 tournament records from a controlled eight-round Swiss-system tournament involving 20 LLMs across four board games: Tic-Tac-Toe, Connect Four, and their goal-inverted variants, Suicide and Not Connect Four. Move records include the model identity, board state, legal moves, observed latency, and textual justification. Moves are validated with a GDL-based arbiter and a rectification protocol that allows up to 10 retries. Overall, 25.2% of LLM-generated moves are invalid, approximately 50% in Suicide; in total, 106 game sequences ended in automatic forfeit, represented by terminal records in the dataset. Even the best-performing model records an invalid-move rate of 10.7%, showing that rule-following errors remain present under these evaluation conditions. These observations illustrate the use of simple board games as controlled domains for evaluating LLM behavior, where strategic decision-making can be examined together with compliance with formal constraints. The proposed pipeline–GDL-based validation, Swiss tournament design, and rectification protocol–is domain-agnostic and can be extended to other GGP settings, supporting scalable evaluation of LLM decision-making under formal rules.
