articles.title: A Proteomic Resource of Human iPSC-derived Neurons Exposed to Neurotropic Viruses
articles.abstract: Abstract Viral infections are common across the human lifespan, yet their molecular effects on human neurons remain poorly characterized. We present a mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomic dataset profiling human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived neurons following exposure to five neurotropic viruses: Herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1), Human coronavirus 229E (HCoV-229E), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), Varicella-Zoster virus (VZV), and Influenza A virus (H1N1). Neurons differentiated from the KOLF2.1 J iPSC line were infected at multiple viral doses and sampled at three post-infection time points. Protein abundance was quantified using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry and a customized human-viral proteome library, enabling simultaneous detection of host and viral proteins. The dataset includes approximately 7,500 human proteins and virus-specific peptides, providing a systematically controlled resource to compare virus- and time-dependent proteomic responses. All raw MS files and processed data are publicly deposited in the PRIDE repository, and an interactive web application supports data exploration and reuse. This dataset is designed to support cross-virus comparisons, hypothesis generation, and integration with transcriptomics and population-scale datasets.

articles.title: A 12-Year Orthopedic Discharge Dataset from a County-Level Hospital in Jiangsu Province, China (2014–2025)
articles.abstract: Abstract This Data Descriptor presents 55,791 orthopedic inpatient discharge records from a county-level hospital in Jiangsu Province, China, collected between January 2014 and December 2025. Each record holds patient demographics, place of residence, up to five discharge diagnoses, up to three surgical procedures with their dates, length of stay, and total hospitalization cost. Because the source records were kept in Chinese, every categorical and clinical field (residence, department, sex, diagnoses, and procedures) was translated into standardized English terminology aligned with international classifications, so that the data can be read and reused without knowledge of Chinese. Care was delivered across five orthopedic units: three general orthopedic departments, a hand and foot surgery department, and a rehabilitation department. We checked every record for temporal consistency, for completeness of the core fields, and for agreement between surgical procedures and their recorded dates. County-level hospitals treat much of China’s rural population but remain under-represented in openly available clinical data: to our knowledge, no comparable long-term, patient-level orthopedic discharge dataset from a Chinese county-level hospital is currently accessible to researchers. The purpose of this work is therefore to make these otherwise unavailable records openly usable by the international research community, with the full translation of all clinical content into English as a central part of that contribution. The dataset is intended to support research on orthopedic epidemiology, healthcare utilization and cost, clinical pathways, and regional health-policy evaluation in that setting.

articles.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the Poitevin stickleback (Pungitius vulgaris)
articles.abstract: The Poitevin stickleback ( Pungitius vulgaris ) is a Near Threatened freshwater fish endemic to France. Using PacBio HiFi long reads and Hi-C scaffolding, we generated the first chromosome-level reference genome for this species. The assembly spans 489.65 Mb across 21 chromosomes, with a scaffold N50 of 21.77 Mb and 99.5% BUSCO completeness. A total of 21,656 protein-coding genes were predicted, and approximately 25.65% of the genome was identified as repetitive sequences. Based on the enrichment of male-specific k-mers on chromosome 12 (chr12), we identified this chromosome as the putative sex chromosome, is consistent with an XY sex-determination system. A short male-specific region (~4 kb; chr12: 24,419,000-24,423,000 bp) was identified that is located in a highly repetitive region and contains one protein-coding gene ( gata1a -like). Although the exact boundary of the sex-determining region (SDR) can not be determined, this short male-specific region embedded in highly repetitive elements suggests a sex-determining architecture distinct from that reported in other sticklebacks. This reference genome provides a foundational resource for population genomics and for studies of sex chromosome evolution in the Poitevin stickleback.

articles.title: Near telomere-to-telomere gap-free genome assembly of the Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar)
articles.abstract: Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ) is a major aquaculture species and an important model for studying salmonid evolution. However, the highly repetitive genome and extensive duplicated regions retained from the salmonid-specific fourth whole-genome duplication (Ss4R) have impeded complete genome assembly, leaving unresolved gaps and structurally ambiguous regions in previous references. Here, we present a gap-free genome assembly of salmon generated using PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore (ONT) ultra-long reads, and Hi-C data. The 2.81 Gb assembly is anchored to 29 chromosomes with contig N50 of 110.45 Mb. Notably, 8 chromosomes are resolved to a complete T2T level. Quality assessments confirm the high accuracy of the assembly, yielding a quality value of 51.06 and the genome BUSCO completeness of 99.67%. Gene annotation identified 45,163 protein-coding genes with BUSCO completeness of 98.80%. By improving continuity and completeness in repetitive and duplicated regions, this resource provides an enhanced reference for structural variant discovery, comparative genomics, and breeding applications in Atlantic salmon.
articles.authors: Chunlong Miao, Shuo Li, Shuhong Jiang, Duan Liao, Shenglei Han, Caichao Dong, Yanan Li, Kaiqiang Liu, Xuwen Cao, Yuyan Liu, Qian Wang, Hong-Yan Wang, Changwei Shao

articles.interpretationCn: 该数据集为大西洋鲑（Salmo salar）的基因组组装，采用PacBio HiFi、Oxford Nanopore超长读长和Hi-C数据构建。组装大小为2.81 Gb，锚定到29条染色体，contig N50为110.45 Mb，其中8条染色体达到完整的端粒到端粒（T2T）水平。质量评估显示组装质量值51.06，基因组BUSCO完整度99.67%；基因注释鉴定出45,163个蛋白编码基因，BUSCO完整度98.80%。该资源提升了重复和重复区域连续性与完整性，可用于结构变异发现、比较基因组学和育种应用。

articles.title: A haplotype-resolved chromosome-level genome for the staghorn sumac Rhus typhina (Anacardiaceae)
articles.abstract: The staghorn sumac Rhus typhina is native to North America but has been introduced into China, where it has become widely established owing to its high adaptability and ecological and economic importance. In this study, a chromosome-level and haplotype-resolved genome of R. typhina was generated using PacBio HiFi, Illumina, and Hi-C sequencing technologies. The two haplotypes, Hap1 and Hap2, were assembled to sizes of 333.98 Mb (scaffold N50 = 21.27 Mb) and 332.18 Mb (scaffold N50 = 21.23 Mb), respectively. A total of 27,336 protein-coding genes (26,489 functionally annotated, BUSCO completeness = 96.09%) and 27,397 protein-coding genes (26,601 functionally annotated, BUSCO completeness = 96.09%) were identified in Hap1 and Hap2, respectively. The phylogenetic analysis and time estimation indicated that R. typhina clustered with the Pistacia species within the Anacardiaceae, diverging from them approximately 31.68 million years ago. This study presents the first high-quality haplotype-resolved genome of R. typhina , providing a valuable resource for its functional and evolutionary studies and insights into its coevolution with Melaphis insects.

articles.title: High-quality annotated histopathological skin melanoma subtype slides for AI model development and validation
articles.abstract: Abstract Cutaneous melanoma (CM) is a highly aggressive form of skin cancer requiring accurate subtype classification for effective prognosis and treatment. To address the scarcity of high-quality datasets, we curated 82 Hematoxylin & Eosin (H&E)-stained whole slide images (WSIs) from 32 patients in the Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC)-CM collection. A senior dermatopathologist oversaw a rigorous multi-stage annotation process, involving a medical trainee and a board-certified pathologist, aligning with the 2022 World Health Organization (WHO) classification. The curation process resulted in a robust dataset comprising 196 tissue sections annotated with histopathologic biomarkers and prognostic metadata, such as ulceration status and tumor cell proportion (TCP). Furthermore, statistical validation using Chi-squared and Fisher’s exact tests confirmed that our final selection represents the original cohort without demographic or histological sampling bias, evidenced by a p-value greater than 0.05. Comprising 196 tissue sections in high-resolution SVS format, this expert-annotated dataset serves as a foundation for developing deep learning AI models to enhance dermatopathology and personalized patient care.

articles.title: A large-scale dataset of sub-institution name disambiguation and hierarchical structures from OpenAlex
articles.abstract: Accurate attribution of scholarly work to specific sub-institutional units, such as schools or departments of a university, is crucial for granular research assessment and policymaking. While robust identifiers exist for top-level institutions, standardized data for sub-level units remains scarce due to the linguistic and structural variability of affiliation strings. In this study, we introduce OpenSubAffil, a large-scale dataset mapping raw affiliation strings from OpenAlex to disambiguated sub-institutional entities and their hierarchical structures. We developed a pipeline integrating named entity recognition (NER) with embedding-based clustering. Furthermore, we proposed a multi-signal scoring function that synthesizes lexical and co-occurrence evidence to reconstruct the sub-institutional hierarchy. OpenSubAffil comprises mappings for 40 million affiliation strings to 638,843 disambiguated sub-units across 18,635 top-level institutions, together with their hierarchical relationships. Validation against Wikidata benchmarks and manual investigation show that our method achieves promising performance. Overall, this dataset bridges the granularity gap between individual researchers and top-level institutions, enabling high-resolution analyses of scholarly output and communication at the sub-institutional level.

articles.title: The Tangrams Codeswitching Corpus
articles.abstract: Abstract Most research in the language sciences has centered on monolingual data, limiting the relevance of its insights for multilingual populations. The Tangrams Codeswitching Corpus , a Spanish-English dataset containing 30,858 words from 45 dyadic repeated reference games, bridges this gap by offering a richly annotated dataset on bilingual communication and codeswitching. In addition to the corpus, the dataset includes detailed metadata on language experience and proficiency of 90 habitual codeswitchers, enabling studies of individual differences in social coordination and switching behavior. This publicly available resource is valuable for exploring bilinguals’ language choices and the interactional dynamics through which they communicate, collaborate, and coordinate with one another. By providing a transdisciplinary perspective on codeswitching, this dataset offers a unique opportunity to explore how bilinguals adapt their language choices and communicative behavior in everyday interaction.

articles.title: Post-retrofit building performance dataset: Energy, IEQ, HVAC operation, and occupant behavior in university apartment buildings
articles.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive monitored dataset from single-family attached residences that underwent deep energy retrofits, complementing a previously published pre-retrofit dataset from the same buildings. The dataset is distinct by its multi-domain scope and temporal resolution, simultaneously capturing whole-building and end-use energy consumption, indoor environmental quality, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system operation (including thermostat setpoints and supply air temperature), window and door operation, building envelope performance, and outdoor environmental parameters at sub-hourly intervals. Data were collected from sixteen occupied apartments across two residential buildings over a continuous twelve-month period, enabling detailed analysis of performance across all seasonal conditions. This high-resolution, multi-faceted dataset uniquely documents the coupled dynamics between building envelope functions, HVAC systems operation, occupant interactions, and weather conditions in the post-retrofit state. A semantic metadata model of building systems and sensors was developed using a JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schema. Standardized cleaning and pre-processing steps were applied to produce a research-grade dataset. Post-retrofit results reveal improved thermal stability, enhanced ventilation effectiveness with reduced CO 2 concentration, and measurable energy performance improvements compared to pre-retrofit conditions. This openly available dataset provides researchers and practitioners with a unique opportunity to evaluate retrofit impacts through granular time-series analysis, study occupant-building-weather dynamics, perform comparative pre/post retrofit analysis, and develop predictive models for human-centered, energy efficient building transitions.

articles.title: Multi-decadal high-resolution historical simulations with the ECMWF global atmosphere model
articles.abstract: Abstract This paper describes an ensemble of global atmosphere reference simulations covering the period 1980 to 2023 produced with the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) Integrated Forecasting System (IFS). The resulting dataset consists of 6-hourly three-dimensional global outputs from higher- and lower-resolution configurations of the IFS, which have average horizontal grid spacings of ~9 km (one ensemble member) and ~28 km (ten ensemble members), respectively. The atmosphere is constrained by high-resolution satellite-based estimates of daily mean sea surface temperature and sea ice concentration and time-evolving external climate forcings, including observed greenhouse gas and estimated aerosol concentrations. These data were produced as part of the European Eddy-Rich Earth System Models (EERIE) project and will serve as a reference for corresponding ocean-atmosphere coupled simulations and idealised sensitivity experiments. We have made this dataset publicly available and expect it to be a valuable resource for scientific research and other applications that extend beyond the lifetime of the EERIE project.

articles.title: Two years of in situ measurements of biophysical variables of mountain meadows in northeastern Italy
articles.abstract: This dataset contains vegetation biophysical variables of eight meadows in the Provinces of Bolzano and Trento, in the Italian Eastern Alps, monitored approximately every two weeks during the growing seasons of 2023 and 2024. The primary objective of the field campaigns was to generate a reference dataset for the calibration and validation of Sentinel-2-derived biophysical products, particularly leaf area index (LAI), for mountain grasslands. Unlike conventional grassland monitoring programmes, the sampling strategy was specifically designed to ensure spatial representativeness at the Sentinel-2 pixel scale while minimising sampling-induced disturbance due to frequent measurements. Complementary variables were also collected, including fresh and dry aboveground biomass yield, photosynthetically active radiation, soil moisture, chlorophyll content, and sward height. The measurement protocol includes reporting of mowing events, weather conditions, yield proportions of functional groups, top cover, and lodging. Signs of recent manure application were also recorded when visible during field surveys. Regular measurements were conducted at multiple geographical locations, each corresponding to a single satellite pixel for the Copernicus Sentinel-2 mission. These measurements were taken biweekly at different pixels within the test sites to monitor and quantify the evolving leaf area and productivity of the meadows, providing detailed ground-based insights into vegetation dynamics. The complete data set is part of the Grassland Research and Innovation Lab of the Horizon Europe project ScaleAgData.
articles.authors: Mariapina Castelli, Abraham Mejia-Aguilar, Caroline Göhner, Laura Stendardi, Giovanni Peratoner

articles.title: A multi-task full-body motion capture and ground reaction force dataset of children and adolescents
articles.abstract: Open reusable biomechanical datasets from generally healthy children and adolescents remain limited, particularly for studies requiring full-body three-dimensional motion capture with synchronized ground reaction force data. Here we describe a laboratory dataset from 43 participants aged 13–18 years, containing more than 4,600 C3D motion-capture records and corresponding force-platform files across locomotor, obstacle-crossing, jumping, functional-screening, sit-to-stand, active range-of-motion, and simulated abnormal-gait tasks. The simulated abnormal-gait trials comprise genu-varum and stroke-like compensation conditions performed by healthy participants, rather than recordings of patients with gait pathology. These simulations have not been clinically validated and should not be used for pathological normative modeling or as diagnostic reference data; instead, they are intended as controlled movement-variation conditions for methodological development and benchmarking. Trial-level metadata, task-standardization tables, marker-label documentation, quality-control reports, manuscript tables, and reproducibility scripts accompany the dataset. The release is intended to support pediatric and adolescent movement research, sports biomechanics, clinical screening method development, musculoskeletal modeling, ground reaction force estimation, and machine-learning benchmarks, with key limitations for reuse documented in the Technical Validation and Usage Notes sections.

articles.title: RobustPDx: A Structured Web-Based Parkinson’s Assessment Dataset and Benchmark for AI Robustness to Device Type and Handedness
articles.abstract: Abstract Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder associated with motor symptoms and cognitive changes. Its increasing global disease burden highlights the need for scalable approaches to support remote assessment and digital biomarker discovery. Digital health platforms offer scalable opportunities to assess motor and cognitive performance metrics relevant to PD diagnosis remotely, minimizing logistical and geographic barriers. We introduce RobustPDx, a dataset comprising structured motor and cognitive tasks performed remotely via an accessible web-based assessment completed by 261 participants, including 73 individuals with self-reported PD, 33 individuals reporting suspected PD, and 155 non-PD controls, each completing standardized tasks remotely using their own computer. The dataset includes raw task-level interaction data and a feature-engineered analytic dataset containing 79 derived features spanning five task categories related to fine motor control and working memory. Each record in the resulting dataset is paired with demographic data, device type, and handedness annotations. Notably, including device type and handedness metadata enables analyses along traditionally underexplored but important axes of variation in remote consumer digital health. Together, these data support the development and benchmarking of AI-driven models for remote PD detection and robust digital biomarker discovery.

articles.title: The Global Volcanic Radiative Power (VRP) Dataset: Twenty-Five Years of Middle InfraRed Satellite Observations (2000–2025)
articles.abstract: We present a global dataset of Volcanic Radiative Power (VRP) derived from Mid-InfraRed (MIR) satellite observations at 170 active volcanoes worldwide between 2000 and 2025. The dataset includes VRP measurements derived from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) and the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS), processed using the Middle InfraRed Observation of Volcanic Activity (MIROVA) system. Data from different sensors have been harmonized to ensure temporal continuity and cross-sensor comparability of VRP measurements providing consistent long-term coverage of volcanic thermal activity over the 25-year-long period. Sensor-specific thresholds and an unsupervised density-based clustering algorithm were applied to classify volcanic sources and reduce false alerts while preserving thermal detection capabilities spanning six orders of magnitude (from 10⁴ to 10¹⁰ W). The dataset is intended for reuse in studies of volcanic activity, hazard assessment, long-term trend analysis, and satellite-based volcano monitoring, supporting analyses at multiple spatial scales – from individual volcano characterization to multi-volcano comparisons, regional assessments, and global surveys of volcanic thermal activity.
articles.authors: D. Coppola, M. Laiolo, S. Aveni, A. Campus, F. Massimetti
articles.titleCn: 全球火山辐射功率（VRP）数据集：二十五年中红外卫星观测（2000–2025）

articles.title: Dataset of 201 healthy elbow CT scans with humeroulnar segmentation, 3D models, and anatomical features
articles.abstract: Accurate 3D representations of elbow joint anatomy derived from CT imaging are essential for total elbow arthroplasty (TEA) planning, biomechanical modelling, and patient-specific implant design. However, publicly available datasets that support such applications remain scarce. Here we present the first open, large-scale dataset that pairs raw elbow joint CT scans and segmented humeroulnar joint masks with expert-validated 3D bone models and quantitative morphometric measurements. The dataset includes de-identified CT scans from 201 individuals aged 16-86 years with no elbow pathology. Orthopaedic surgeons manually segmented the distal humerus and proximal ulna to generate STL-format 3D surface meshes. Ten clinically relevant anatomical parameters related to TEA were measured using standardized protocols. The dataset is expected to accelerate development of automated segmentation algorithms, validate finite element models, and support population-matched implant design. All data are publicly available under a CC BY 4.0 license via the Zenodo platform.

articles.title: Infrared Spectra Database of Microplastics from the Arctic Marine Environment
articles.abstract: The first spectral database of Arctic microplastics, MICROSCAN (MICROplastics Spectroscopy data for Contamination ANnalysis), is presented. It comprises 2010 FTIR spectra and is freely available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15277130 . The database contains spectra of microplastic particles (0.5–5 mm) collected in the Eastern Arctic Seas in 2020–2021, representing polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, and mixed PE/PP polyolefin spectra. For analysis, multiple annotation approaches were employed, including spectral matching, expert validation, and a convolutional neural network (CNN1D) from the mPSAT package ( Environ. Sci. Technol . 2023, 57, 6656). Using these methods, we thoroughly verified the MICROSCAN database, establishing it as a valuable resource for training and validating advanced classification models of environmental microplastic.

articles.title: A Digital Holography-Based Dataset of Red Blood Cells for Machine and Deep Learning Analysis of Hereditary Anemias
articles.abstract: Abstract Hereditary Anemias (HA) are genetic blood disorders affecting a large number of subjects and can cause important clinical complications. Correct, rapid and automatic identification of each type of anemia is pivotal for proper treatment and patient management. Digital holographic microscopy provides label-free quantitative phase measurements of red blood cells (RBCs) morphology. However, standardized and reproducible computational workflows for feature extraction and RBCs classification are still scarce. Here we present a collection of roughly 4600 holographic phase-contrast maps (PCMs) representing RBCs from healthy controls and patients affected by five different HA subtypes. Furthermore, a complete and openly available set of MATLAB scripts is released to implement an analysis workflow, taking PCMs as input. The workflow includes handcrafted feature extraction, as well as different conventional machine and deep learning models. Notably, deep learning architectures are trained directly on PCMs. By releasing the full pipeline, from raw phase maps to trained models, this work delivers an open and extensible framework that facilitates method comparison, ensures reproducibility, and supports the development of new approaches.

articles.title: A chromosome-level genome of Eutrema heterophyllum, an edible and medicinal plant of Brassicaceae
articles.abstract: Eutrema heterophyllum is a perennial alpine species mainly distributed on the eastern Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau and represents a valuable resource for studies of high-altitude adaptation and germplasm utilization. However, genomic research on this species has been constrained by the absence of a chromosome-level high-quality reference genome. Here, we performed chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of E. heterophyllum , the final genome size was 348.43 Mb with a scaffold N50 of 48.54 Mb, and the anchoring rate reached 99.81%. Quality evaluation of the genome assembly yielded a BUSCO gene completeness of 99.01%, a CEGMA completeness of 96.77%, an LAI score of 20.52, and a short-read alignment rate of 98.84% that covered 97.44% of the genomic regions. Subsequently, the repetitive content was estimated to be 57.08%, and a total of 33,498 protein-coding genes were annotated with 97.63% complete BUSCO genes. Then, a total of 32,930 genes (98.30%) were successfully functionally annotated. This genomic resource will facilitate comparative genomics, studies of high-altitude adaptation, germplasm conservation, and investigation of glucosinolate metabolism and isothiocyanate formation in Eutrema .

articles.title: Telomere to telomere genome assembly of a wild soybean Glycine soja accession HAAS216
articles.abstract: Abstract Wild soybean ( Glycine soja ), the progenitor of cultivated soybean ( Glycine max ), represents an important reservoir of genetic diversity crucial for soybean improvement. However, the limited availability of high-quality reference genomes for wild soybean has constrained its comprehensive genomic characterization. Here, we present a telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly of a wild soybean ( G. soja ) accession HAAS216 with a size of 1,018.17 Mb, generated using PacBio HiFi, ultra-long Oxford Nanopore sequencing, and Hi-C data. The assembly spans all 20 chromosomes and captures 20 centromeric and 40 telomeric regions, forming a gap-free T2T genome assembly. This assembly exhibits superior quality regarding completeness (BUSCO: 99.6%), contiguity (contig N50: 51 Mb), and base-level accuracy (QV: 55.53). Repetitive sequences make up 55.84% (568.57 Mb) of the genome, and 48,390 protein-coding genes were predicted, of which 47,567 (98.30%) were functionally annotated. This genome assembly provides a genomic resource for comparative genomics and facilitates genetic research and crop improvement in soybean.

articles.title: A global dataset of the landward extent of Earth’s Coastal Critical Zone
articles.abstract: The Earth’s Coastal Critical Zone (ECCZ) acts as a vital nexus for land–sea material and energy exchange. However, in the Anthropocene, conventional fixed-distance buffering (e.g., 100 km from the coast) does not adequately represent its complex physical processes and ecological boundaries. Here, we provide a vector dataset of the global landward extent of the ECCZ for 2022, derived from a 30 m resolution delineation dataset. The dataset was generated using 18 features representing physical geography, ecosystem processes, and human activity within a block-adaptive support vector machine (SVM) framework. The global ECCZ covers approximately 1.45 × 10 7 km² (9.7% of the global land area), with the largest extents in Asia (4.79 million km², 33.1%) and North America (3.42 million km², 23.6%), followed by Europe (14.1%), South America (11.6%), Africa (9.6%), and Oceania (8.0%). The mean block-level overall accuracy was 91.24% (±1.98%). The dataset shows broad inland extents in low-lying deltaic settings, narrow coastal strips in steep tectonically active margins, and encompasses major coastal urban agglomerations including the Tokyo Metropolitan Area, the New York Metropolitan Area, and the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area. This dataset provides a spatial baseline for studies of land–sea interactions, coastal environmental change, and related Earth system applications.

articles.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the parasitoid wasp Eretmocerus corni (Hymenoptera: Aphelinidae) for functional genomics and biological control research
articles.abstract: Eretmocerus corni (Hymenoptera: Aphelinidae) is an economically and ecologically important parasitoid wasp widely used as a biological control agent against whitefly pests, including the greenhouse whitefly ( Trialeurodes vaporariorum ) and the sweetpotato whitefly ( Bemisia tabaci ). To enable research on its evolutionary biology, host-parasitoid interactions, and applied pest management, we present a high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly of E. corni . The assembly was generated using an integrated sequencing strategy combining Illumina short reads, PacBio continuous long reads (CLR), Oxford Nanopore long reads, and Hi-C chromatin interaction data. The final genome spans 778 Mb, with a scaffold N50 of 217.5 Mb and a BUSCO completeness of 94%. Repetitive sequences constitute 59.24% of the genome, and 22,725 protein-coding genes were annotated using a combination of de novo prediction, homology-based inference, and transcriptome data. The present comprehensive genomic resource provides a foundation for studying the genetic basis of parasitism, host specificity, and adaptive traits in parasitoid wasps. This dataset also supports functional genomics, evolutionary research, and the development of improved biological control strategies.

articles.title: Dataset of lipidome and transcriptome of Gentiana crassicaulis seeds during artificial aging
articles.abstract: Abstract Gentiana crassicaulis is a significant traditional medicinal plant in China. Currently, seed reproduction is the predominant method for large-scale seedling cultivation. However, the seeds of Gentiana are typically susceptible to aging and deterioration, which severely impacts seedling production and germplasm preservation. Research on the seed aging process of G. crassicaulis is still relatively limited, particularly in terms of systematic multi-omics data support. In this study, transcriptomic and lipidomic analyses were conducted on G. crassicaulis seeds artificially aged for 0, 5, 10, and 25 days. A total of 119.21 Gb of high-quality transcriptome sequencing data were generated, and 611 lipid molecular species across five major classes and 28 subclasses were comprehensively identified. This dataset provides a comprehensive multi-omics resource for investigating lipid metabolism and transcriptional regulation during seed aging in G. crassicaulis , which may facilitate future studies on germplasm conservation and seed quality improvement.

articles.title: Development of a monthly groundwater well observation dataset in India
articles.abstract: Accurate, reliable, and continuous groundwater level observations are essential for assessing sustainable water management in India. However, the absence of quality-controlled and high-frequency groundwater datasets has significantly hindered large-scale groundwater assessments. The existing groundwater levels data in India are available at a quarterly time scale (January, May, August, and November), but with substantial data gaps. Here, we developed a monthly groundwater level dataset for India, covering the period from 1996 to 2021, by combining quarterly observations from 4,514 wells. We first employed a combination of Quantile Regression Forests and K-means clustering to impute the missing quarterly groundwater levels using topographical, climatological, and hydrogeological variables. Subsequently, a Chow-Lin disaggregation method was employed to convert quarterly data into monthly data, ensuring temporal consistency with observed values. The developed monthly groundwater level data enable the analysis of groundwater storage changes, identification of potential recharge zones, water budget studies, groundwater-surface water interactions, and the calibration of hydrological models, thereby supporting sustainable groundwater management across India.

articles.title: Multi-Target Behavior Detection Dataset for Simmental Beef Cattle
articles.abstract: This paper presents an image dataset designed for multi-target behavior detection in Simmental beef cattle. The dataset aims to address the current lack of high-quality and diverse data in beef cattle behavior recognition research, thereby promoting the development of computer vision-based intelligent farming technologies. Collected from real farm environments, the dataset encompasses various seasons, lighting conditions, and indoor/outdoor scenes. It comprises 3,218 images annotated with 11,318 instances across ten behavior categories: lying, standing, walking, running, feeding, foraging, drinking, excreting, fighting, and mounting. To ensure both quality and efficiency in annotation, a semi-automatic pipeline combining “auto pre-labeling and manual verification” was employed. Annotation files are provided in both PASCAL VOC and YOLO formats. To validate the dataset’s utility, we trained and evaluated a behavior detection model using YOLOv8s. Experimental results show that the model achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) of 76.9% on the validation set, demonstrating high recognition accuracy for most behaviors, which confirms the dataset’s practicality and reliability. This dataset serves as a foundational resource for research related to cattle behavior recognition, health monitoring, and precision livestock farming management.

articles.title: A near telomere-to-telomere genome assembly of coltsfoot (Tussilago farfara)
articles.abstract: Abstract Tussilago farfara L., commonly known as coltsfoot, is a perennial medicinal member of the Asteraceae family. It has a long history of use in traditional medicine to relieve coughs and other upper respiratory ailments. We report a near telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome assembly for Tussilago farfara , constructed by integrating PacBio HiFi long reads, Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) ultra-long reads, MGI short reads, and high-throughput chromatin conformation capture (Hi-C) data. The resulting 1.60 Gb genome assembly with approximately 94.92% of the sequences anchored onto 30 pseudochromosomes. Notably, this assembly is exceptionally contiguous, featuring only two gaps and capturing 50 of the 60 telomeres. Its exceptional completeness and accuracy are further supported by a BUSCO score of 99.50% and a consensus Quality Value (QV) of 68.16. Genome annotation revealed 51,235 protein-coding genes, 98.67% of which were functionally annotated. This high-quality reference genome provides a robust genetic foundation for elucidating the biosynthetic pathways of key medicinal compounds and will profoundly advance future evolutionary and functional genomics studies of coltsfoot.

articles.title: A Multimodal Dataset for Large Language Model Applications in the Energy Domain
articles.abstract: This paper presents the mAIEnergy dataset, an open-access, multimodal corpus developed to support Large Language Model (LLM) applications in the energy sector. The dataset integrates approximately 50,000 textual documents, 20,000 images, 25 million numerical time series records, and 2 million geospatial and relational data entries. It includes policy and regulatory texts, scientific articles and news articles, satellite and contextual imagery, electricity system measurements, weather observations, statistical indicators, and geospatial representations of energy infrastructure and related entities. All data have been harmonized into structured, ready-to-use formats, accompanied by consistent metadata and reproducible data retrieval and preparation workflows. The dataset can serve as a foundational energy knowledge base, allowing energy stakeholders to integrate additional open-source or proprietary data. The mAIEnergy dataset adheres to Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) principles, enhancing its applicability for AI-driven energy research, modeling, and decision-making.

articles.title: A global dataset of forest disturbance regimes derived from satellite biomass observations
articles.abstract: Forests play a central role in the global carbon cycle by serving as critical carbon sinks for atmospheric CO 2 . Yet, the stability and continued capacity of these sinks are increasingly threatened by a growing number, size, and severity of disturbances. Accurately representing the stochastic nature of disturbance remains a major challenge and a key source of uncertainty in our understanding of carbon cycle dynamics. This study presents a novel framework for deriving disturbance regimes characterized by disturbance rate ( μ ), gap-size distribution ( α ), disturbance severity ( β ), as well as background mortality ( K b ) directly from landscape features of high-resolution satellite biomass data. These regimes reflect the characteristics of long-term disturbances at the landscape scale rather than the properties of any single event. Our analysis inverts the model framework developed by Wang et al. (2024), which used a machine learning model trained on a massive synthetic dataset of over 8 million forward model simulations to link known disturbance regimes to spatial biomass patterns. Instead of predicting patterns from regimes, we use observed satellite biomass patterns to infer the underlying disturbance regimes. To ensure robustness, we first identified the optimal spatial resolution for aggregating both simulation and satellite data, minimizing discrepancies in feature value ranges and reducing extrapolation risk. Using this framework, we produced the first globally continuous, observationally constrained dataset of forest disturbance regime parameters and their associated uncertainties, provided at both a 25×25 km tile level and as a gridded 0.25° global product. Additionally, we used a Dissimilarity Index (DIK) to quantify prediction uncertainty and identify potential extrapolation by measuring the divergence of observations from the training set. An empirical evaluation comparing paired forest landscapes with contrasting extremes in their predicted disturbance parameters support the methodology and assumptions used to build the dataset. The datasets are available at https://doi.org/10.17617/3.EF4QGR (Wang et al., 2026). Our global maps of disturbance regimes provide a novel, process-based tool for investigating the coupled dynamics of disturbance, vegetation, and the carbon cycle, with potential applications for improving the representation of stochastic disturbances in large-scale ecosystem models.

articles.title: Multimodal Benchmark for Safety Assessment in Industrial Inspection Scenarios
articles.abstract: With the rapid development of industrial intelligence and unmanned inspection, reliable perception and safety assessment for AI systems in complex and dynamic industrial sites has become a key bottleneck for deploying predictive maintenance and autonomous inspection. Most public datasets remain limited by simulated data sources, single-modality sensing, or the absence of fine-grained object-level annotations, which prevents robust scene understanding and multimodal safety reasoning for industrial foundation models. To address these limitations, InspecSafe-V1 is released as the first multimodal benchmark dataset for industrial inspection safety assessment that is collected from routine operations of real inspection robots in real-world environments. InspecSafe-V1 covers five representative industrial scenarios, including tunnels, power facilities, sintering equipment, oil and gas petrochemical plants, and coal conveyor trestles. The dataset is constructed from 41 wheeled and rail-mounted inspection robots operating at 2,239 valid inspection sites, yielding 5,013 inspection instances. For each instance, pixel-level segmentation annotations are provided for key objects in visible-spectrum images. In addition, a semantic scene description and a corresponding safety level label are provided according to practical inspection tasks. Seven synchronized sensing modalities are further included, including infrared video, audio, depth point clouds, radar point clouds, gas measurements, temperature, and humidity, to support multimodal anomaly recognition, cross-modal fusion, and comprehensive safety assessment in industrial environments.

articles.title: Whole-Genome Variants Resource of 144 Oryza rufipogon Accessions
articles.abstract: The global food security crisis highlights the urgent need to improve rice yield and quality. Oryza rufipogon , the wild progenitor of cultivated rice, offers valuable genetic diversity, yet its genome remains underexplored. We conducted whole-genome resequencing (WGS) of 144 O. rufipogon accessions from 13 countries, generating ~400 GB of data using the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform. After quality control, 97.58% of reads aligned to the reference genome, achieving 87.97% coverage with 12.47× average depth. We identified a total of 6,183,832 SNPs and 748,493 InDels across 12 chromosomes. Chromosome 1 exhibited the most variants (715,636 SNPs and 91,276 InDels), while chromosome 9 had the fewest (384,000 SNPs and 44,817 InDels). Mutation rates were 67 SNPs and 559 InDels per million base pairs. Notably, 40.75% of SNPs and 46.09% of InDels were found upstream of genes, with 19.13% and 22.26% located downstream, respectively. A transition-to-transversion ratio (Ti/Tv) of 2.72 confirmed the data’s reliability. Our findings offer a comprehensive genomic variation resource for O. rufipogon , supporting future genetic research and rice breeding efforts.

articles.title: Subnational disaggregation of SSP-coherent population projections for Europe
articles.abstract: Age- and sex-specific, subnational population projections are scarce despite their essential role, e.g., in planning the provision of health, education, or social services. This Data Descriptor presents a new, open dataset providing downscaled population information for 305 NUTS-2 regions across 34 European countries covering the 2020 to 2100 period in 5-yearly steps. It is consistent with the latest country projections under the SSPs and provides population information by sex and five-year age groups. The dataset results from (1) the application of a neural-network model architecture to project regional age structures, before (2) imposing an SSP-consistent sex split that propagates country-level scenario trends while preserving regional heterogeneity. The dataset is accompanied by the fully documented R code, ensuring transparency, reproducibility, as well as generalizability to other regions or possibly demographic dimensions. This new resource facilitates analyses of demographic heterogeneity across regions and over time, as well as integrated assessments of social policies, regional development, and climate-related risks under alternative socioeconomic futures.

articles.title: China rainfall erosivity (2015–2023): A new annual dataset inferred from national hourly meteorological station records
articles.abstract: Rainfall erosivity (R-factor) is a critical parameter for soil loss prediction and ecological risks assessment, yet its quantification is often limited by the coarse temporal resolution of available precipitation data. While high-frequency observations provide a more accurate characterization of rainfall kinetic energy, a national-scale assessment of the uncertainties induced by these varying data resolutions in China has been lacking. This study presents a new, high-precision annual rainfall erosivity dataset for China (2015–2023) derived from hourly precipitation records across 57,740 meteorological stations (at least 5 years). Using the hourly-derived erosivity (R hourly ) as the benchmark, we systematically evaluated the estimation biases of widely used daily and monthly empirical models. Results show that R hourly exhibits a decreasing gradient from southeastern to northwestern China, peaking at over 8,000 MJ mm ha −1 h −1 y −1 in the Southern Red Soil Hilly Region. Nationwide, daily-scale estimates show a mean absolute error of 20.7%, transitioning from systematic underestimation in the southeast to severe overestimation in the northwest. Monthly-scale estimations yield a higher mean absolute error of 25.8%, with intensified underestimation in southern regions and a reversal of error direction in the northwest. Across China, the interannual coefficient of variation averages 59.0%, with the highest variability (93.8%) observed in the Northern Wind-Sand Region. By providing station-based benchmark data and identifying spatial error patterns, this dataset offers a robust foundation for high-precision soil erosion mapping, regional conservation planning, and climate change impact assessments.

articles.title: A High-Quality Haplotype-Resolved Reference Genome for Drakensberger Cattle (Bos taurus indicus/taurus) Achieved Through Trio-Binned Long-Read Sequencing
articles.abstract: Drakensberger cattle is indigenous to South Africa and represent a unique genetic resource which is known for its quality beef production and adapted to the harsh climatic conditions. Despite its significance within the beef industry, no high-quality chromosomal level genome has been reported for this breed, limiting genomic selection and conservation efforts. Although there is a bovine genome reference, we need a breed specific reference to identify breed-unique alleles and structural variants that might not be explained by a distant reference. To address this, we generated a haplotype resolved assembly for Drakensberger cattle using a trio-binning where we employed PacBio HiFi reads for sire and dam, a combination of PacBio HiFi reads, Oxford Nanopore Technologies reads and Omni-C reads for the offspring. The assembled diploid genome size is 2.89 Gb with a scaffold N50 of 111 Mb and contig N50 of 61 Mb. The consensus accuracy was exceptionally high (QV = 70.23) and a genome completeness of 97.5%, as analysed by the Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs (BUSCO). The k-mer profiling suggested one of the strong haplotype separation for livestock with the paternity assembly containing 97.1% and maternity with 99.0%, combined diploid genome recovered 99.46% of all the statistically solid read k-mers. We identified 14 telomeric ends across 13 scaffolds. The final genome encompassed a total of 22,854 protein-coding genes. This is the first high-quality, haplotype resolved genome assembly of the Drakensberger breed. This assembly high accuracy, contiguity and completeness place the genome among the highest-quality cattle genomes produced to date. This genomic resource is essential in designing programs to studies for breed evolution, adaptation, genomic selection and for conservation of the South African indigenous resources.

articles.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of Hovenia acerba (Rhamnaceae)
articles.abstract: Hovenia acerba , commonly known as Guaizao or Wanshou fruit, is a plant of significant economic and medicinal value with dual use as both food and medicine. In this study, we generated a chromosome-level genome assembly of H. acerba by integrating PacBio HiFi long reads, Illumina short reads, and Hi-C chromatin interaction data. The final assembled genome is 342.88 Mb in length with a contig N50 of 25.60 Mb, and 98.62% of the sequences were anchored to 12 chromosomes. Although high-quality genomes have previously been reported for several Rhamnaceae species, including Ziziphus jujuba , genomic resources for Hovenia species have remained unavailable. This study presents the first chromosome-level genome assembly for H. acerba , thereby filling a genomic gap in medicinal and edible plants within the Rhamnaceae family. A total of 27,157 protein-coding genes were identified through comprehensive structural and functional annotation. Flavonoid biosynthesis genes showed conserved upstream pathways but variation in downstream genes ( F3 ′ H , F3 ′ 5 ′ H ) compared with Z. jujuba . This high-quality genome provides a key reference for functional gene discovery, elucidating the biosynthetic pathways of active ingredients, and comparative genomics research in medicinal and edible plant species.

articles.title: GaitIntent: A Kinematic Dataset Focusing on Steady-State to Transitional Locomotion for Lower-Limb Motion Rehabilitation
articles.abstract: Motion intent recognition (MIR), the real-time interpretation of user movement, is crucial for advanced motion rehabilitation. MIR enables responsive control of prostheses and exoskeletons, enhancing mobility for lower-limb impaired individuals. Most existing datasets prioritize steady-state locomotion, often overlooking complex transitional movements critical in daily activities, which limits anticipatory control development. We introduce GaitIntent, a novel kinematic dataset. Inspired by gait symmetry, it uses sound limb kinematics for predictive MIR for the affected side—an approach less comprehensively covered. We collected multi-node Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) data from the thigh, shank, and foot of 11 subjects’ sound limbs performing 13 daily activities, emphasizing eight distinct transitional movements. GaitIntent provides a valuable resource for developing low-latency, robust algorithms for wearable rehabilitation and human-centric control systems.

articles.title: EEG-based brain-computer interface (BCI) dataset for directional word recognition
articles.abstract: We present an EEG dataset recorded from 22 neurologically healthy volunteers (12 native Russian speakers and 10 native Spanish speakers) during overt and covert articulation of six spatial-direction words. Monopolar EEG signals were acquired from 38 electrodes positioned according to the international 10-10 system using a Neurovisor-BMM-52 (NVX) amplifier at 500 Hz. In a subset of participants, electromyography (EMG) was simultaneously recorded from the masseter muscle and laryngeal region to exploratorily characterize articulatory muscle activation. Exploratory spectral and coherence analyses, together with classification using standard machine learning methods (Random Forest, SVM, LDA), confirm the presence of condition-specific neural activity distinguishable by standard classifiers (best accuracy 78 ± 4%). The dataset is intended to support the development and benchmarking of algorithms for inner speech recognition in brain-computer interface applications.

articles.title: Corpus for orthographic and emotional factors in word and nonword recognition
articles.abstract: The present article describes a Spanish lexical decision dataset designed to support analyses of how orthographic letter-position coding relates to affective properties during visual word recognition. The dataset provides trial-level response times and accuracy for 406 five-letter words and three transposed-letter nonwords derived from each base word. It also includes lexical, orthographic, and affective measures, including word frequency, orthographic neighborhood, valence, arousal, and discrete emotion ratings. Data were collected online from 92 native Spanish speakers. We describe the materials, procedures, preprocessing steps, and quality checks, and provide technical validation based on well-documented word-frequency and orthographic-neighborhood effects. The repository includes raw data, processed data files, analysis code, and a complete variable dictionary, offering a reusable resource for research and modeling how letter-position coding and affective factors interact during visual word recognition.

articles.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of the Diptychus maculatus
articles.abstract: Diptychus maculatus is a state second-class protected fish species with significant ecological value, primarily distributed in Xinjiang, China. This study reports a high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly of D. maculatus , offering an essential resource for investigating its adaption to extreme environments. The assembly was achieved by integrating PacBio long-read sequencing, Hi-C chromatin interaction data, and transcriptomic evidence. The final genome assembled size was 1.805 Gb, with a contig N50 of 2.84 Mb and a scaffold N50 of 34.86 Mb. Based on Hi-C sequencing data, 94.4% of the assembled sequences were successfully anchored and oriented onto the 49 chromosomes. The genome contains 52.29% repetitive sequences. A total of 51,356 protein-coding genes were annotated, of which 99.37% received functional annotations. BUSCO assessment indicated a genome completeness of 98.08%. This high-quality reference genome provides a solid foundation for elucidating the genetic mechanisms underlying high-altitude adaptation in D. maculatus and will facilitate further studies in evolutionary genomics, conservation genetics, and aquaculture.

articles.title: Synthetic PET and CT Data using Generative Model in Projection Domain
articles.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has substantially increased the demand for large-scale datasets; however, available datasets remain insufficient for data-intensive tasks, particularly in nuclear medicine. While large-scale datasets exist for computed tomography (CT), few provide paired projection-domain and image-domain data across diverse lesion types. This issue is more pronounced for positron emission tomography (PET), where datasets are scarce, particularly for multiple tracers such as 18 F-DOPA, 18 F-FDG, and 68 Ga-PSMA, anatomical regions, and disease categories. This work presents SPC-Gen, a large-scale S ynthetic dataset for P ET and C T, Gen erated using a latent diffusion model. The dataset covers diverse disease types, lesion characteristics, tracers, anatomical regions, and modalities, while preserving the intrinsic correspondence between projection and image domains. SPC-Gen contains 50,104 released synthetic slice records, including PET projection-image records and CT image-domain records, forming a standardized large-scale dataset. Experimental results show that the generated samples closely align with real data distributions and can support improved performance on downstream tasks such as lesion segmentation. Compared with conventional VAE models and more recent GAN- and NCSN-based baselines, SPC-Gen achieved stable KID values around 0.021 across the single-modality evaluation and an FID of 40.960 for the PET Trunk image-domain setting, indicating improved global distributional alignment between synthetic and real data.

articles.title: An LLM-driven Chinese Corpus of Human Olfactory Descriptions and Entity Annotations
articles.abstract: Language plays a pivotal role in artificial olfactory perception, serving as a crucial bridge that translates chemical stimuli into human experience. The mapping from olfactory stimuli to linguistic descriptions constitutes the foundation for modeling artificial olfaction with human-like descriptive capabilities. However, this field is currently constrained by a lack of publicly available, culturally diverse olfactory corpora, with existing datasets predominantly reflecting Western odor profiles. To address this gap, we constructed a large-scale Chinese olfactory corpus by employing a dual-iterative strategy assisted by a large language model (LLM). Beginning with an initial set of standardized descriptors and a defined annotation template, our strategy iteratively alternated between lexicon expansion and corpus refinement throughout the process. The resulting large-scale corpus of domain-relevant sentences enables the training of computational language models. A downstream olfactory semantic clustering task was performed. The result demonstrates that language model fine-tuning on the proposed corpus improves embeddings for capturing Chinese olfactory experience. Consequently, our work provides an essential foundational resource for advancing culturally inclusive models of olfactory perception.

articles.title: Chromosome-level genome assemblies of the parental lines of GCH-7, a high-performing castor (Ricinus communis L.) hybrid
articles.abstract: Gujarat Castor Hybrid-7 (GCH-7) is a high-performing castor ( Ricinus communis L.) variety developed from the parental lines SKI-215 and SKP-84. This variety holds significant economic importance, as it is a high yielding hybrid variety and its seeds are widely used for castor oil production. In this study, we report the first high-quality genome assemblies of the parental lines of GCH-7, SKI-215 and SKP-84, generated using Oxford Nanopore sequencing and polished with Illumina data. The assembled genome sizes were 310.23 Mb and 325.63 Mb, with N50 values of 30.21 Mb and 32.12 Mb for SKI-215 and SKP-84, respectively. The assemblies exhibited high completeness (BUSCO: 98.6% and 98.8%) and base-level accuracy (Merqury QV: 42.87 and 46.50) for SKI-215 and SKP-84, respectively. Genome annotation identified 18,620 in SKI-215 and 18,598 in SKP-84. Repetitive sequences constituted 31.62% and 31.76% of the SKI-215 and SKP-84 genomes. In addition, complete chloroplast and mitochondrial genomes were assembled and anchored to the nuclear genomes. These high-quality parental genome assemblies provide a valuable resource for genetic studies, plant breeding and offer practical applications in genetic purity testing of GCH-7 seeds.

articles.title: A telomere-to-telomere gap-free genome assembly of Alpinia oxyphylla Miq.
articles.abstract: Alpinia oxyphylla is a medicinal plant of the Zingiberaceae family with established neuroprotective and gastrointestinal therapeutic effects. The absence of a complete genome has hindered the elucidation of its metabolic pathways and impeded genetic improvement. Here we present the first telomere-to-telomere (T2T), gap-free genome assembly of A. oxyphylla , together with comparative genomic analyses that explore its evolutionary history and biosynthetic capacity. The 2,045.52 Mb assembly spans 24 chromosomes with a contig N50 of 91.56 Mb and exhibits high quality: 97.5% BUSCO completeness, a base-level quality value (QV) of 69.69, and a long terminal repeat assembly index (LAI) of 22.59. We annotated 38,703 protein-coding genes, 98.21% of which were functionally assigned against multiple databases. Phylogenetic analysis clarified the species’ position within Zingiberaceae and revealed extensive chromosomal conservation. This T2T gap-free genome provides a foundational resource for investigating the genetic basis and evolutionary dynamics of A. oxyphylla , supporting germplasm conservation, phytogeographic studies, and functional genomics in this pharmacologically valuable species.

articles.title: Gap-free T2T genomic landscape of an XY male Larimichthys crocea
articles.abstract: Larimichthys crocea (the large yellow croaker) is one of the most economically significant marine fish in East Asia. While chromosome-scale genome assemblies for three female (XX) geographical populations (Mindong, South China Sea, and Daiqu) were available, the lack of a high-quality male (XY) reference genome has hindered the exploration of male-specific sequences and the molecular mechanisms underlying sex determination. Here, we present the male T2T reference genome for the Mindong population of L. crocea by integrating Oxford Nanopore ultra-long, PacBio HiFi, and Hi-C sequencing. The assembly totals 747.28 Mb with a contig N50 of 31.79 Mb. We further achieved telomere-to-telomere (T2T) assembly and haplotype partitioning of the X and Y sex chromosomes. Telomeric repeats (TTAGGG) were identified at both termini of all 23 autosomes and two sex chromosomes. Moreover, centromeric regions exhibited significant enrichment of six major transposable elements, including DNA MULE, LTR Gypsy, DNA CMC-EnSpm, RC Helitron, LTR ERV1, and DNA TcMar-Tc2, with 76.19–93.42% of their total copies localized to centromeres. Together with a 42 bp tandem repeat (Cen-42), these elements form the centromeric architecture characterized by higher-order repeats (HORs). The T2T genome assembly exhibits high technical quality, with a BUSCO completeness of 99.6% and a base accuracy (QV) exceeding 59.75. The genome annotation yielded 29,933 protein-coding genes, providing a comprehensive map of the male-specific regions. This gap-free male reference genome provides a definitive genetic resource for studying sex-biased traits, sex chromosome evolution, and precision molecular breeding in L. crocea .

articles.title: A Multi-view Dataset for Vietnamese Word-Level Sign Language Recognition
articles.abstract: Abstract This research introduces VSL400, a multi-view video dataset for isolated word-level recognition of Vietnamese Sign Language (VSL). The dataset contains 74,259 manually annotated video clips covering 400 glosses performed by 28 signers, including deaf student signers and additional trained VSL signers. Each signing instance was recorded simultaneously from three synchronized RGB camera views: front, left, and right. This design captures complementary visual perspectives of sign articulation and supports single-view, cross-view, and multi-view recognition studies. To facilitate reproducible research, we provide a preprocessing pipeline for temporal boundary detection, segmentation, and spatial normalization, together with structured metadata and reference code. Metadata, documentation, and processing code are available from Zenodo, while the de-identified human video files are shared through controlled access governed by a Data Usage Agreement. VSL400 addresses a major resource gap for Vietnamese Sign Language and provides a practical reference dataset for research on isolated sign recognition in a low-resource language setting.

articles.title: A Correlative Microscopy Dataset for Multimodal Data Fusion and Image Matching in Materials Science
articles.abstract: Abstract Gaining understanding of process-structure-property relationships in materials at a mechanistic level relies on correlative microscopy workflows. These workflows, in turn, fundamentally depend on image matching, i.e., a computer vision task with the objective of finding point correspondences in pairs of images. Matching models are difficult to evaluate quantitatively in the materials field due to a shortage of representative benchmark datasets. Nonetheless, prior research indicates that traditional rule-based image matching techniques such as the surface-invariant feature transform (SIFT) currently fall short on such matching tasks. We present a dataset for cross-modal image matching and data fusion in the materials microscopy domain, which we coin AmalgaMatch , to support model benchmarking and fine-tuning efforts. All images are micrographs captured using the most widely applied imaging techniques in materials science including light-optical, scanning electron, and transmission electron microscopy, as well as electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD). Therein, various detectors and imaging modes are employed to capture micrographs of diverse materials. While the majority of images are raw images, some underwent typical processing routes using digital image correlation or EBSD indexing. Common regions in image pairs are populated with hand-annotated keypoint correspondences. While mutual information is limited in cross-modal, multi-scale image pairs, we relied on characteristic defects such as dislocations, grain boundaries, triple junctions, inclusions, pores or topographic features for annotation. Furthermore, the dataset is divided into groups, defined by distinct registration use cases, and further into subsets, defined by the imaged material. The dataset covers many typical use cases for image matching in materials science, including slip partitioning, dislocation characterization, and surface fractography. In total, it comprises 6 groups and 19 subsets with 35 scenes and 187 annotated image pairs to support autonomous multimodal materials data fusion. For each image, we provide structured metadata to facilitate training of hybrid matching models which process textual alongside image-based inputs to improve the matching quality and robustness. A formal ontological model for correlative microscopy and image matching processes is proposed to express image contents, relationships, and transformations through knowledge graphs and to enable aligning with FAIR data principles.

articles.title: Non-stationary Multivariate Bias-corrected CMIP6 Climate Projections of Daily Precipitation and Temperature over India
articles.abstract: General circulation models (GCMs) exhibit systematic biases and coarse spatial resolution that limit their direct applicability for regional climate analyses, particularly under non-stationary climate conditions. While statistical BC methods are widely applied, most adjust each variable independently and therefore do not explicitly preserve cross-variable dependence structures required for physically consistent multivariate climate assessments. A non-stationary multivariate bias-corrected daily dataset of precipitation and maximum, minimum, and mean temperature for India at 0.25° spatial resolution is presented, derived from 13 CMIP6 GCMs using the Rank Resampling for Distributions and Dependences (R 2 D 2 ) framework. The approach accounts for evolving distributional characteristics under changing climate conditions while preserving inter-variable dependence. The dataset spans the historical period (1951–2014) and future projections (2015–2100) under four SSP scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5). Performance is evaluated against observations using multivariate statistical properties that capture dependence structures, including Pearson correlation, Kendall correlation, and Clausius–Clapeyron scaling between precipitation and temperature. The resulting dataset provides a physically coherent resource for regional climate impact assessments, compound event analysis, hydrological modelling, and drought studies under non-stationary climate conditions.

articles.title: A database of extrachromosomal circular DNAs (eccDNAs) profiles across primary intracranial tumors
articles.abstract: Extrachromosomal circular DNAs (eccDNAs) have recently emerged as critical drivers of tumor evolution, functionally and physically distinct from linear chromosomal DNA. The presence of eccDNA often correlates with poor patient outcomes and rapid cancer progression, suggesting a potential role as a biomarker for early detection. Here, we present a comprehensive dataset of eccDNA landscapes generated via extrachromosomal circular DNA sequencing (Circle-Seq) across four types of primary intracranial tumors: glioblastoma, meningioma, pituitary adenoma, and vestibular schwannoma. We provide detailed functional annotations of the derived eccDNA profiles, characterizing their genomic distribution and potential oncogenic content. This study characterizes the eccDNA population within these distinct brain tumour subtypes, offering a reliable resource for future biomarker identification and tumour-specific mechanistic investigations.

articles.title: Classification of trees in New York City at the genus level from PlanetScope satellite imagery and airborne lidar
articles.abstract: Urban tree maps are used by urban tree professionals, researchers, and the general public. However, urban tree inventories are often limited to publicly managed trees along streets and occasionally in parklands, leaving trees on private lands and in natural areas largely unmapped. This restricts understanding of citywide urban forest composition and its ecological and societal functions. Here, we present a genus-level classification of urban trees in New York City, USA, derived using high resolution remote sensing. This spatial dataset classifies 1.8 million tree crown polygons into 18 common genera with an overall accuracy of 82.0% (kappa = 0.794). For example, Platanus has producer’s (omission) and user’s (commission) accuracies of 95% and 93%, and Quercus has accuracies of 88% and 80%, respectively. The classification extrapolates labels from an existing urban forest inventory to tree-level crown objects citywide using an XGBoost classifier, trained on time series of 3 m PlanetScope satellite imagery and structural metrics derived from airborne lidar. This classification methodology is applicable to other temperate cities with extensive deciduous canopies.

articles.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the dung beetle Synapsis davidis (Coleoptera: Scarabaeidae)
articles.abstract: Abstract Dung beetles of the subfamily Scarabaeinae are important contributors to terrestrial ecosystem processes, playing key roles in dung decomposition, soil bioturbation, and nutrient cycling. Among these, large-bodied species are often considered functionally important due to their strong dung-processing capacity. One such example is Synapsis davidis , a large-bodied dung beetle endemic to China. This species exhibits dual dung-processing strategies—both tunneling directly beneath dung pats and rolling dung balls for burial—and is found in forest, grassland, and ecotonal habitats. These ecological traints suggest that S. davidis may help remove dung and the maintain essential processes, making it a promising target for studies on grassland conservation and ecological restoration. However, genomic resources for this species remain unavailable. To address this gap, we generated a chromosome-level genome assembly for S. davidis using PacBio HiFi, Illumina, and Hi-C sequencing data. The final assembly spans 1.10 Gb and comprises 10 assembled chromosomes, with a scaffold N50 of 107.51 Mb and a BUSCO completeness of 99.40% based on the endopterygota_odb10 database. We predicted 10,955 protein-coding genes, of which 99.11% were functionally annotated. Altogether, this resource provides a foundation for future ecological, evolutionary, and comparative genomic studies of dung beetles.

articles.title: A century-scale dataset of hydropower stations in mainland China (1909–2025)
articles.abstract: Under the background of carbon emission reduction and energy transition, hydropower plays a key role in global clean energy systems and sustainable development. Here we present a century-scale dataset of hydropower station records in mainland China (1909–2025), compiled through multi-source integration and standardized processing. The dataset contains 2,918 georeferenced hydropower station records with attributes including station identity, spatial information (e.g., name, administrative units, coordinates, river basin), commissioning year, operational status, and installed capacity, together with additional dam and reservoir and performance attributes where available. Data curation involved schema harmonization, unit conversion to MW, duplicate reconciliation, and archival supplementation for early and small-scale stations. Data quality was evaluated through cross-source consistency checks, benchmarking against national statistics, and coordinate verification using high-resolution imagery for records with uncertain locations. Core attributes (station identity, spatial attributes, and capacity attributes) show high completeness (>80%), while infrastructure attributes are less complete due to historical data limitations. Beyond providing a standardized hydropower inventory, the dataset supports analyses of long-term spatial–temporal evolution, basin-scale energy–water interactions, and comparative assessments of hydropower infrastructure development. The dataset is publicly available via Mendeley Data and is intended to support broad reuse in hydropower-related research.

articles.title: A Comprehensive Dataset for Job Allocation in Internet of Things Networks
articles.abstract: This paper presents the Network and Application Dataset for Internet of Things (NAD-IoT [1]), a dataset built to support research on job allocation in large-scale IoT networks. The dataset provides instances from 10 (10 1 ) up to 1,000,000,000 (10 9 ) network nodes, each associated with multiple jobs that represent application demands. Nodes and jobs of the dataset have essential attributes such as processing capacity, bandwidth, and latency, allowing researchers to explore performance under a wide range of operating conditions. NAD-IoT is organized into scenarios defined by the ratio between jobs and nodes: Lightweight scenarios, where jobs represent up to 20% of the nodes, and Heavyweight scenarios, where jobs correspond to 70% of the nodes. It enables systematic assessments of heuristics, metaheuristics, and optimization strategies, supporting analyses of scalability, efficiency, and runtime. It provides a reliable foundation for benchmarking algorithmic behavior, examining job-distribution patterns, and evaluating resource-management techniques. Beyond optimization studies, NAD-IoT can be used for experiments, simulation design, model training, and validation in investigations involving large-scale, heterogeneous, and resource-constrained IoT environments.

articles.title: A global high-resolution dataset of snowmelt runoff onset timing from Sentinel-1 SAR, 2015–2024
articles.abstract: Snowmelt runoff onset timing represents a critical hydrological parameter, particularly in mountainous regions where seasonal snow serves as a natural reservoir for downstream water resources. Despite this importance, high-resolution observations of snowmelt runoff onset across complex terrain are limited, due to challenges from sparse in situ monitoring networks, intermittent optical remote sensing data, and coarse passive microwave remote sensing data. To address this gap, we prepared a global snowmelt runoff onset timing dataset (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16953614, Gagliano et al., 2026) for the 10-year period spanning 2015–2024, with 80 m spatial resolution and 9.5 d average temporal resolution. We created this dataset by identifying backscatter minima empirically associated with runoff onset in a time series of Sentinel-1 C-band SAR images, with detection constrained by a custom MODIS-derived snow phenology dataset. We evaluated our dataset using in situ snow pillow estimates of runoff onset from 1116 automated weather stations across the Western United States, British Columbia, Norway, and Nepal, finding a median timing difference of −2.0 d and a median absolute deviation of 10.0 d. The local agreement between our runoff onset estimates and snow pillow runoff onset estimates varies with site-specific variables like forest cover fraction, SWE, and dataset temporal resolution. We characterized these dependencies to provide empirically-derived thresholds for quality filtering as well as guidance for interpretation and use of our products. The dataset includes global annual runoff onset products for each water year, annual local temporal resolution products for each water year, and 10-year composites of median runoff onset, median absolute deviation, and local temporal resolution. This unique combination of high spatial resolution, global coverage, and decade-long temporal coverage provides unprecedented detail for the study of snowmelt runoff onset across snow-covered regions. Our snowmelt runoff onset dataset enables an improved understanding of mountain hydrological processes and informs water resource management in snow-dominated watersheds.

articles.title: ROP-VL: An Open Dataset Integrating Fundus Photograph and Clinical Knowledge for Retinopathy of Prematurity
articles.abstract: The development of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) for Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP) is hindered by a scarcity of public datasets that integrate color fundus photographs with the expert clinical knowledge required for building robust vision-language models. We present ROP-VL, an open-access dataset designed to bridge this critical gap. It contains 2,020 color fundus photographs from 1,116 infants, encompassing eight diagnostic categories including Normal, A-ROP, Laser-treated ROP, and ROP Stages 1-5. ROP-VL explicitly pairs these images with patient biological metadata and structured textual descriptions, providing the necessary components for multimodal learning. We perform a technical validation by training four image-only models and a vision-language model on ROP occurrence and severity classification tasks. The results demonstrate that the vision-language model, leveraging the integrated structured clinical data, consistently achieves superior performance. ROP-VL provides a purpose-built resource to facilitate the development of more robust, knowledge-aware AI, aiming to advance automated ROP diagnosis.

articles.title: An integrated single-cell transcriptomic and microbiome dataset of orbital adipose tissue in thyroid eye disease
articles.abstract: Abstract Thyroid eye disease (TED), also historically referred to as thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy (TAO) or Graves’ orbitopathy (GO), is an autoimmune ophthalmopathy characterized by inflammation and adipogenesis within orbital adipose (OA) tissue. While the contribution of immune cell infiltration and fibroblast activation is recognized, the cellular heterogeneity and the potential role of local microbial dysbiosis in the orbital microenvironment remain poorly defined. Here, we present a multi-omics dataset derived from OA of patients with TED and healthy controls collected at Beijing Tongren Hospital. The dataset comprises single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data generated from human orbital adipose tissue and subcutaneous fat. Following quality control filtering and doublet removal, a total of 61,302 high-quality singlet cells were retained for downstream analyses, capturing the transcriptomic landscape of orbital fibroblasts, immune subsets, and vascular cells. In parallel, 16S rRNA gene sequencing was performed on orbital adipose tissue samples collected from the integrated study cohort, alongside environmental samples for contamination assessment, to characterize the low-biomass orbital microbiome DNA signatures. Raw sequencing reads, quality-controlled gene-expression matrices, and contamination-corrected microbial feature tables are provided. Our dataset provides an opportunity to investigate the crosstalk between host cellular immunity and potential local microbiome signatures, facilitating hypothesis generation regarding host-microbiome crosstalk and the exploration of novel therapeutic targets for TED.
